# Section 2. *Mosaical Philosophy.*

Just as the Second and the Third proceed from them both, so the aevial <note>Spiritual beings existing in "aevum," the state between time and eternity.</note> or Empyreal Angels pour down the influences of life into the Olympian or heavenly ones; and the Olympian or starry spirits send them down to the Elementary ones. In the same manner, the Empyreal Spirits are the soul or life to the Starry or Ethereal heaven, which animates the Elementary heaven by its influences, and the earth is animated by them all.

Thus, therefore, we see that God operates through his divine organs in various ways, "all in all." When this is well understood in the first place, we may boldly conclude that all the individual angelic lights also proceed from one and the same universal <note>original: "catholick"</note> emanation. Consequently, we find that the diversity and opposition of their natures proceed from the multiplicity of properties within that general emanation, which comes from the throne of God—the Unity—before all beginnings. This is the reason that this eternal creating Spirit of wisdom is termed by <term>Solomon</term>, *One and manifold* <note>original: "Unicus & multiplex"</note>; One (I say) in regard to his essence (Wisdom 7), and manifold in regard to the multiplicity of its properties, by which it works variously and sometimes through opposition in the world. All of this is excellently expressed by the learned Cabalistic Rabbis in their description of the *Numerical or Sephirothic Tree.*

You must therefore understand that just as the mystical <margin>+</margin> theologians observed only ten special names or attributes which were ascribed to God in the Hebrew Bible, <gloss>according to his property <note>original: "a proprietate"</note></gloss>, they also perceived that each of these implied a different operation to be performed. Thus, the Hebrews called upon this or that Name of God mentioned in the holy text according to the nature of the specific need they had for God’s assistance. They gathered from the word of God that the Divinity or Godhead is but one internal, immutable essence, and therefore has only one truly essential title to be expressed: namely, the *Tetragrammaton* or <term>Jehovah</term>. This is his inseparable name because it is appropriated to him alone; for as <term>Rabbi Moses the Egyptian</term> <note>Moses Maimonides (1138–1204), the influential Jewish philosopher.</note> says, it includes and proves by pure signification the substance of the Creator, without any respect or participation with the creature. Yet, they nevertheless found that the other names ascribed to him in Scripture denote or signify God as he participates with his creatures, or as he relates to things that are created, and consequently are known by the effects of his works.

Regarding his essential name, it was held in such high esteem and reverence among the Hebrews or Jews that it was never uttered except in the Sanctuary, and then only by such priests as were consecrated and made holy to the Lord alone; it was then pronounced in 그 Benediction which the High Priest uttered on the day of fasting. For this reason, that name was held in such honorable regard that it was never rashly spoken or uttered, because (as the said Rabbi Moses says) it denotes *that God is and was above all essence, forasmuch as he existed before any thing was existent in the world* <note>original: "Deum esse & fuisse super omnem essentiam quatenus, antequam ulla res esset, existeret"</note>. This was that precious Name of God which <term>Moses</term> was so desirous to hear and know from him, when he received this answer: יהוה <note>The Tetragrammaton, YHWH.</note>, *This is my name forever* <note>original: "Hoc est nomen meum in æternum"</note>, *JEHOVAH is my everlasting name.* This name is so pure and simple that it cannot be articulated, compounded, or truly expressed by a human voice. As for the other names assigned to God, they do not express him according to his Essence, but only in respect of his works (as was said)—namely, as he appears as "all in all" and exists in all things.

We must understand, therefore, for our better instruction, that since the Divine Nature is and operates in all created things as well as outside them (for he is the center of all his creatures, whose circumference is not to be found), in this regard his essential name *Tetragrammaton* is the common agent in every bough or branch of the Sephirothic or Cabalistic Tree. It has dominion or preeminence over the entire trunk or body of that Tree. Consequently, all the other ten names <margin>+</margin> are assigned to it as having relation to the properties or the effects of his multiplicity of virtues or actions within one individual essence. Therefore, all the rest are subject to it and are wholly comprehended within it. All these opposite effects are testified by Scripture <margin>Wisdom 16:13.</margin> to spring from one essential fountain, forasmuch as it comprehends the power of life and death, and leads to the brink of the grave, and reduces or brings back again—

Sect. 2. Mosaical Philosophy.

The reason why the Divinity created or sent forth one specific radiation <note>original: "eradiation"</note> so contrary to another was for both the preservation and destruction of creatures. Just as the final effect of each of these contrary emanations of radiant flows <note>original: "radious effluences"</note> is the creation, or generation and preservation, of creatures of their own nature and condition, so also are they to be applied either for the preservation or restoration of decaying creatures. For example, we apply any poisonous simple—whether animal, vegetable, or mineral—to expel a dangerous disease or to poison a healthy nature. In the animal kingdom, this includes the venomous viper, scorpion, toad, spider, or blistering Spanish flies <note>original: "Cantharides"</note>. In the vegetable kingdom, there is the sleep-inducing and numbing poppy or opium; the searching and inflaming or burning spearwort <note>original: "Flammula"</note> and spurge <note>original: "Euphorbiun"</note>; the corrosive scammony; the vomit-inducing groundsel, daffodil, asarabacca <note>wild ginger</note>, bear's-foot, tithymal <note>spurge</note>, and the poisonous aconite <note>wolfsbane</note>. In the mineral rank, there is corrosive arsenic; the quick, piercing, and infecting quicksilver and corrosive sublimate; the destroying realgar <note>arsenic sulfide</note>; the vomit-inducing antimony, and such like. All of these have the property to take away dangerous diseases as well as to bring them. In some cases, they take away painful maladies, and in others, they bring them quickly and hasten the destruction of the creature. 

Thus, in some cases, all things both wound and destroy, and in others, they heal and cure. Yet to Him who sent them—the beams and radiations of their form coming from some of His particular properties—they all appeared good, since they were ordained not only to heal in His kindness <note>original: "benignity"</note> but also to destroy in His severity. To conclude, they effect His will one way or another, according to the pleasure of Him who alone works essentially in all things. Therefore Solomon <margin>Wisdom of Solomon 11:25</margin> says: *Could anything exist which you would not have to be?* So everything is good to God, although to wicked men who suffer from them, they may appear bad. *All the works of the Lord are very good* <note>original: "Opera Domini universa, bona valde"</note> (says the Wise Man) <margin>Ecclesiasticus 29:21</margin>. *Good things were created for the good from the beginning; so for the wicked, both good and evil things were created* <note>original: "Bona bonis creata sunt ab initio, sic nequissimis bona & mala"</note> <margin>Ecclesiasticus 39:30</margin>. There are spirits created for vengeance, and in their fury, they execute their torments; in the time appointed, they pour out their power <note>original: "virtue"</note> and carry out the fury of Him that made them—namely water, hail, the teeth of beasts, the scorpion, the serpent, and so on. All these rejoice to execute His commandments upon the Earth. 

For this very cause, therefore—namely the secret opposition of natures in the world, originally proceeding from the streams of those variable properties that radically spring from that one incomprehensible Fountain—Love and Hatred, and consequently <term>Sympathy and Antipathy</term>, were created to jostle and, as it were, shoulder one another in this world. This occurs generally under the titles of Light and Dark, and particularly in that friendship and hatred observed and testified in the Scriptures to exist first between the very angels themselves; then among the stars, which receive these opposite natures from the angels; thirdly, among the winds and elements, which derive their spirit of contention from the stars; and lastly, among those compound creatures which are composed of those elements by the active spirits of the winds. But because among all other opposite qualities in the world, this sympathy and antipathy are most <term>occult</term> <note>hidden or non-obvious</note> and hidden—for while we can explain the reason for the contrariety of elements from their obvious qualities, namely cold, heat, moisture, or drought, we find no such elementary ground for this hidden opposition—we will dive as far into the bowels of this mystery as our limited <note>original: "steril"</note> capacity will allow.

The will of God <note>original: "volunty"</note> is the highest perfection of things; necessity follows this will, and the result accompanies the necessity. So, whatever God wills must be perfect, and consequently, the effect must follow by necessity. Therefore, he concludes that God accomplishes both His will and its effect in an instant of time. But what He does not want cannot be; therefore, whatever exists in the *nature of things* <note>original: "rerum natura"</note>, whatever property it may have, it is brought about according to the will of one of these Divine Attributes.

<margin>Asclepius, chapter 4.</margin>
"Neither is it credible," he says, "that anything should displease God which once pleased Him, since He knew long before both the thing that was to come and that it would be pleasant to Him" <note>original: "Neque credibile est, Deo displiciturum esse quod placuit, cum & futurum id & placuturum multo ante sciverit"</note>.

<margin>Wisdom 11.</margin>
And therefore Solomon asks: *Could anything exist which you would not have to be?* Thirdly, we must understand that according to the variety of His divine will, things were created so that some spiritually sympathize in affection with one another, while others "antipathize" <note>feel a natural or spiritual repulsion</note> among themselves. This happens because of "beams" of a contrary disposition, depending on whether the angelic irradiation—the shining out of the beams from one spiritual creature to another—is concordant or opposite. This contrariety of conditions proceeded from the various properties found in the will of one and the same root and eternal Essence. In this way, all creatures in the world, both spiritual and physical, were composed; and thus were they given life and animated by beams that were either contrary to each other or, because of their harmony and likeness of nature, rejoiced greatly when they met together through the radiation of a single influence. 

We must also understand that although each creature received its fundamental information from these emanations, they may vary from the condition of their parents during generation and multiplication. This is because two different radiations may unite at the hour of their birth. Thus, it happens that a man may be unlike his parents in both shape and temperament; a horse may be more fierce or sluggish than its sire; a plant or fruit may be more limp, watery, or unwholesome than the stock from which the seed or sap came. Consequently, by the application of angelic beams of an opposite nature at a man's birth, it may happen that the radiation of a particular plant, flower, or beast will forever "antipathize" with that man, even though it might perfectly agree and "sympathize" with someone else. 

The opposition between contrary elements is obvious and manifest—namely, the fight or discord between clashing qualities or natures, such as cold and heat, or moisture and dryness <note>original: "drouth"</note>. In this case, the sympathy and antipathy of elements is well known to everyone: for example, the conflict between water and fire, or between earth and air. However, we must recognize that there is an even more hidden and internal cause of sympathy and antipathy in things. While some ascribe this to the "occult" <note>hidden or secret</note> natures of the stars, in truth it proceeds from those angelic influences. These influences stream out of creatures born under a discordant emanation in an invisible and most hidden manner, which Reuchlin <note>Johannes Reuchlin (1455–1522), a German humanist and scholar of Greek and Hebrew</note> describes exceedingly well in these words:

<margin>Reuchlin, *On the Art of the Kabbalah*, book 3.</margin>
"It is accepted by the Peripatetic <note>Aristotelian</note> philosophers that every spherical heaven, besides its own essential form, has an 'assistant intelligence' that moves its orb. By this angel, operations are effected in things which their own nature either would not do at all, or would not do in that specific way; others say these effects proceed from an 'occult property' or something similar" <note>original: "Philosophis Peripateticis id probatur, quod cælum quodlibet Sphæricum præter formam suam essentialem, habet assistentem intelligentiam orbis sui motricem, quæ vocatur Angelus, eò quod ad hoc officium missa, intelligens & volens complet jussa Creatoris, tanquam inter Deum & Naturam, virtus media; à qua fiunt operationes in rebus, quas natura earum vel non faceret, vel non sic faceret, quas alii provenire dicunt à proprietate occultâ, & aliquid tale"</note>.

### Mosaicall Philosophy: Book 2

We ought also to know in a similar way that the **Sign** which has the most **dignity** <note>In astrology, "dignity" refers to the strength or influence of a planet based on its position in the zodiac.</note> for a **Planet**—such as its **House**, **Triplicity**, **Face**, **Exaltation**, **Term**, or similar placements—best sympathizes with the **Geniture** <note>The astrological chart or conditions at the moment of birth or creation.</note> of that **Planet**. Conversely, the **Signs** or fixed impressions of the firmament which are opposite in nature or full of misfortunes (such as a planet's **fall** or **detriment**, etc.) cause a secret hatred and repulsion through their beams when things belonging to one another secretly influence each other through their aspects. 

Also, the manner in which they cast out their beams creates a wondrous alteration in the two subjects; for as the beams of the stars were toward one another at the birth of an animal or the sprouting of a plant, so shall their true character remain and be expressed in the thing born or produced. I will, therefore, describe the nature of these beams, or secret radiations, which accompany the influence of the stars in a more thorough manner, because the secret astrological mystery of the **Sympathy** or **Antipathy** that happens between things here below consists within them.

<margin>Al-Kindi, *On the Rays* <note>original: *Alkindus de Radiis*; Abu Yusuf al-Kindi (c. 801–873 AD) was an Arab philosopher whose work on the "radiation" of all things influenced Western occultism.</note></margin>

First, I must have you know that the most insightful and profound astronomers are of the opinion that every star in heaven has a nature or condition assigned to itself, which dictates how the projection of its beams with others is contained. Just as every star has a unique nature not found in any other (in which the emission of beams is included), these beams are observed to be of a different condition, just as the stars themselves are different in nature; for every star has its position in the heavens entirely distinct and different from every other. 

Therefore, it necessarily follows that each of them has a different relationship to one another and to all other things or places contained in this world. Now, it is certain that the variety of the **aspect** <note>The angular relationship between celestial bodies.</note> varies the effect of the beams, just as various other properties of the stars do the same. Because of this, it happens that each star operates differently and produces a different effect in various places and subjects, no matter how small the difference may be, since the entire operation of the stars proceeds from the beams, which vary in every different aspect. 

For the beams that issue from the center of the star to the center of the earth are found—and by experience are proven—to be the strongest in their kind of operation. But the beam that is emitted obliquely is weakened and diminished in its effect according to the angle of its slanted motion, unless it is strengthened and supported by the concurring beams of other stars in the same place or point; for each particular star casts its beams to every place. 

Therefore, when the diversity of beams is collected or gathered together, it alters the character of each place or subject, as there is a different combination of beams in every different place and thing, which is derived from the general or total **harmony of the stars**. Because of this, it happens that in every place and at every time, a diversity of individual creatures are produced in this world. The **celestial harmony** is said to effect all of these by the projection of beams into this lower elemental region, which continually vary and diversify themselves. 

By this, therefore, it is evident that the radiations of all the stars have different operations in the things of this world according to the different properties of those things; for every thing rises, springs, and exists by these emanations, or the streaming forth of beams. Moreover, we ought to note that the condition of the heavenly harmony is such that, since all the stars are of different natures and all their beams have different effects in the elemental world, it happens that these beamy operations are assisted or aided in the same matter or subject, while in another matter, they are hindered by one another. 

Furthermore, we must observe that over everything in this world, there is ordained a **predominant star**. And again, there is some celestial **Sign** that, in the work and government of that same thing, bears rule above all others. From this interaction of the starry beams between themselves, there arises such a great difference and diversity in the things of this world that two or more things can hardly be found which are alike in all respects, even if human senses are not always sufficient to perceive the difference.

To conclude, the celestial harmony works so differently in various places and times that it sometimes generates or produces "like from like," and at other times it brings forth things that are unlike. Also, it produces similar things at one time by a similar motion, and at another time, unlike things by a different motion—sometimes by a slow motion, and then by a swift motion. Thus, we see that by innumerable other ways, the things of this world and their motions are observed to vary according to places and times.

# Section 2. Mosaical Philosophy.

When every wise person well ponders this, it becomes evident that the elementary world is made after the example of the heavenly world. Therefore, everything contained within it carries its image. We should not hesitate to affirm that all things in this world—whether they are physical substances or essential properties <note>original: "essentiall accidents"; in philosophy, an "accident" is a property that does not change the essence of a thing, such as color or temperature.</note>—emit beams toward one another in their own way, imitating the stars from which they originate. Otherwise, it would be impossible for them to fully contain the form of the starry world.

This is clearly and sensibly confirmed by certain examples: fire sends out heat to its neighboring parts, and conversely, the earth expires or brings forth the beams of its coldness. Also, medicines taken internally or applied externally send the beams of their power into the body. We also observe that the collision or clashing together of two hard bodies produces a sound or noise, which spreads out or disperses itself through beams in its own fashion. Again, all colored things send out beams by which they are seen. Since this is the case, we may boldly state that everything that actually exists in this elementary world sends out beams in every direction, filling the entire surrounding space in its own way. Therefore, Al-Kindi <note>Abu Yusuf al-Kindi (c. 801–873 AD) was an Arab philosopher whose work on the "radiation" of all things influenced Western occultism.</note> asserts that every place in this world

Through this, it is made clear to us that every creature in the elementary world is not only shaped by these celestial beams poured out upon them, but is also preserved by the constant flow of their beamy influence. As for example, the attribute **ELOHIM** <note>A Hebrew name for God associated with justice and severity in Kabbalistic tradition.</note> sends down into the star or planet of <term>Saturn</term> the fruits of his chill and frozen effects, by which the spirits of that sphere are strengthened. *This name or attribute EL, which is translated as "God," fosters or nourishes all things and assists every creature by his piety and clemency, which is appropriate to him; therefore, grace is attributed to him. By this, therefore, we may discern how the spirits—who are the dispensers of both healthy and malevolent or destructive influences—are present in the mass of the lower elementary waters. By these, man and the other creatures of God may be either preserved or destroyed. 

To conclude, that middle spirit in the world called the "Firmament" divides the two extremely different waters from one another. It is that intermediate spirit of the world which equally participates in and observes each extreme. It is the central mansion of that eternal Spirit which emits his beams from his starry solar or sunny palace, even to the center of darkness, and extends his emanation even to the seat of Light, which is his root. For his brightness is emitted from the attribute **ELOAH** through the beautiful or glorious gate <term>TIPHERETH</term> <note>The sixth Sephirah in the Kabbalistic Tree of Life, representing beauty, balance, and the sun.</note>—which signifies grace, beauty, and loveliness—by the angelic order of the Virtues into that purified palace of the Sun. 

So, by his emanating presence, he penetrates everywhere and fills all things. He grants life to all things by his virtue and is the Father of life, growth, multiplication, and preservation. He has made his seat in the center of the heavens so that, by one most perfect harmony—namely a spiritual <term>Diapason</term> <note>In music, an octave; here used to mean a perfect interval or total encompassing of harmony.</note>—he might illuminate the angels above and the stars around him. Furthermore, by a more material <term>Diapason</term>, he might penetrate into the center of the elementary world to communicate his perfection to every creature. Thus, they might be beautified by his bright presence and given life by the penetrating beams of his essence. 

Consequently, the offshoots or spirits of darkness may be weakened by the appearance of his glory. It is as if one chord were stretched between the Fountain of Light and the abyss of darkness; if struck, it makes a unison. But if it is pressed down and divided directly in the middle, each part will, when struck, produce a double "diapason" (octave) relative to that unison. This signifies a double perfection proceeding from the bright, universal emanation: one side concerns the adorning of the lower waters with life and virtue, and the other creates a bond of friendship among the higher regions. 

Now, as the body of the Sun and the substance of the <term>Æther</term> <note>The "fifth element" or the subtle material that fills the space of the universe above the terrestrial sphere.</note> is made of a middle or moderate spiritual matter (or consistency of the waters), it is evident that it is also subject to being altered by "passion" (external influence), whether antipathetical or symphonical. If it were not, it would not be the immediate receiver of those opposite and contrary emanations that descend from the differing attributes of God. 

But in practice, we find the contrary to be true: for some stars are friends and sympathize in nature with certain creatures below, while others hate one another deadly. Consequently, they send down into this lower world contrary influences which move contrary passions or impressions in the vital spirits or souls of certain elementary creatures. Again, we find that the life of any animal consists of opposite actions—namely, <term>Systole</term> (contraction) and <term>Diastole</term> (expansion).

Therefore, so that no continuous, unnatural disturbance would follow—which might deprive this great formal craftsman <note>The "formal workman" refers to the divine creative principle or the Word of God.</note> of his expectation, which was to put concord and peace in the machine [the universe] he had ordered and framed—he divided each region in this lower world. He did this so that a neutral <note>original: "indifferent"</note> friend might be placed between two extreme enemies. This was achieved by weight, number, and measure. 

So, to the heaviest portion of the lower waters, he gave the smallest proportion of form, so that by its thickness and weight it might fall to the center and remain fixed there; this was called **earth**. Then, to another portion, he bestowed a double measure of light to make it reside in a higher region. Because of this, the matter next to the earth became thinner, lighter, and more movable. This increase of light melted the frozen waters slightly and made them fluid and transparent. Because its matter is continuous with that of the earth, and because of its cold nature, it is a temperate friend to the earth and takes its place next to it. Thus, it is not as cold as the earth, nor as moist as the air. 

The matter is not fully refined <note>original: "subtiliated"</note> until the bright Agent of the world bestows three portions of his light upon the dark, watery abyss above the water. This converted part of the thick lower waters into a thinner and lighter shape than the watery element. This was the **air**, which—because of the triple proportion of formal light—was hotter and more expanded <note>original: "dilated"</note> than the water. Therefore, just as the water was cold (but not as cold as the earth) and moist (but not as moist as the air), so the air is hot (but not as hot as the fire) and moister than the water. Because of its moisture, this portion of the universal <note>original: "catholick"</note> element is friendly to the water on one side, and to the fire on the other because of its heat. 

Lastly, that uncreated Spirit of life multiplied a part of those waters by an even higher degree of refinement and purity. It became the most subtle and highest portion of the general elements, and is consequently hot and dry. Because of its dryness, it agrees on one side with the earth (which follows it in the cycle of circulation), and on the other side with the air in respect to its heat. However, it is hotter than the air and not as dry as the earth.

## Section 2. Mosaical Philosophy.

"The occult properties in things, which are not produced by an earthly <note>original: "Elementary"</note> nature but descend from heaven, are hidden from our senses and barely known to our reason. For they are derived from the life and spirit of the world through the beams of the stars, which we cannot investigate or discover in any other way than through experience and conjecture. You must therefore know that every thing moves toward its like and, with all its power, leans toward its own kind." <note>original Latin: *vita spirituque mundi, per ipsos stellarum radios proficiscuntur, quæ à nobis non aliter quam experientia, & conjecturis indagari possunt. Scire ergo debes quod unaquæque res movet ad suum simile & inclinat ad seipsum secundum totum posse suum:*</note>

By this, the author argues that the universal <note>original: "catholick"</note> angelic spirit—which gives life to the world—is the main actor. In its more divine part, it contains the Sephirotic <note>The Sephirot are the ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself.</note> power or virtue of all the Divine Attributes. As *Ezekiel* testifies, this spirit also contains the virtues of the four winds. It operates through its "starry organs" (the planets and stars) by sending out various beams to produce all these occult and hidden effects below. These effects are beyond the understanding of an ordinary person, even though we can see that they happen through their results. 

There is not a single beam sent out from this spirit that does not have a secret, purposeful act. These beams differ from one another just as we find their effects to differ through our physical experience. Whatever was originally decreed in the secret counsel of the Archetype <note>The original model or blueprint in the mind of God.</note> is carried out from a general plan into many specialties, and from each specialty into an infinite number of individual particulars. 

Thus, the eternal <note>original: "æviall"</note> or angelic effect is the image of the eternal *Idea*, and the temporal world is the likeness of the eternal realm. Furthermore, in this temporal or symbolic world, every stellar shape is the pattern of the angelic *Idea*; and again, earthly <note>original: "Elementary"</note> things are the shadows of the spiritual shapes or images in heaven. 

Wherefore, just as God sends out His emanation (which is His Image) into the angelic world in many different ways and forms, the angelic spirits send their various different lights to each other—every rank to the one below it, and every upper sphere to the spheres below them. From the stars, which also share their lights with one another through different angles <note>original: "aspects"</note>, these influences are infused into earthly creatures by degrees downward, even to the very center of the earth. 

These creatures, following the manner of their heavenly pattern, also shine forth toward one another with beams that are either sympathetic and harmonious or antipathetic and discordant. We should not doubt that such agreeing and disagreeing beams exist here below, seeing that in the fountain of Unity from which all things flow (God), we observe an opposition of properties: namely, a negative "No-Will" <note>original: "privative Nolunty"</note> and a positive "Will" <note>original: "positive Volunty"</note>.

Nor should we think otherwise than that the passive spiritual matter of the world’s soul is the subject through which the Divine Virtue works. Within this matter, it stirs up loving and positive (or good and sympathetic) passions by pouring out life-giving beams of life. This adds delight and joy, satisfying the "appetite" of the created spiritual matter. Consequently, the matter forgets the rooted nature that its dark parents (the Mother *Chaos*) and the Divine Power bestowed upon it at its birth, and it is converted by adoption into a "child of Light." 

Therefore, in this case, it sympathizes with those golden showers of charitable and life-giving light sent down from the kind attributes of God. It begins to hate, dread, and loathe or avoid all the negative <note>original: "privative"</note> influences poured down from the severe, unhealthy, and destructive attributes. Just as light flies from darkness, this spirit—being delighted by the presence of more light and life—avoids and hates the presence of its contrary: namely, death and evil. 

From this it follows that the "children of Light"—who are grafted into this universal illuminated spirit—flee from the "children of darkness" and their works as if from a plague. The reason is that this moist, created spirit, now finding the pleasure, will, and happiness of its illuminated state, is afraid that the negative beams of darkness (the dismal emanations of God’s wrath) might dim its light and obscure the brightness of life. That is to say, it fears they might turn its sympathetic passions of joy and gladness into antipathetic storms of sadness and mourning by sucking the beautiful emanations of joy and love back from the edges of the spirit into its center. This would deprive it of that healthy and spirited radiance of love and life by hiding God’s face, which He had shone from the center out to the edges of the creature.

This was therefore a privative passion in the heart of the great world, or as one might say, a fainting fit <note>original: "Syncope"</note> of the world, when God <note>original Hebrew: "ELOAH"</note> refrained for that season from pouring forth his influence of beauty through the gate of Beauty <note>original Hebrew: "TIPHERETH"—one of the ten Sephirot or divine attributes in Kabbalah, often associated with the Sun and the heart</note>. For if the world was made by the sending forth of God’s bright emanation (for by the Spirit of the Lord the heavens were adorned, as *Job* tells us), it follows that by taking it away, all will return again to darkness and plain nothingness or deformity, even as it was before. 

But this production of good and sympathetic passions, by emitting light from the center to the circumference; and again, the effects of antipathetic passions, which oppose the concord and sympathy of life, is excellently described and illustrated by the careful examination of the vital action in man. 

For as there are noted to be, in general, two distinct active virtues in man's spirit: the first is voluntary, which is the prince over the other, and commands and moves the inferior actions. This is much like how the Divine Angel *Metatron* <note>In mystical tradition, Metatron is the highest of angels, often serving as the celestial "First Mover"</note> acts in the "First Mover" <note>original Latin: "Primum mobile"—the outermost sphere of the heavens in ancient astronomy</note> of the great world, which is referred to the Will <note>original: "Volunty"</note> and moves by it the celestial orbs and the world of the elements. So, in the human framework <note>original: "Microcosmicall Fabrick"</note>, the "first mover" is that divine mental beam which is the head of man's soul. 

The other kind of virtue is involuntary, because it is commanded by and rules according to the will of the intellectual or rational beam—no differently than all the lower celestial spheres are forced to move according to the will of the mover in the "First Mover." Thus, the vital action in man is one of those branches that is involuntary, and is no more subject to the will of the mental beam than the starry heaven is. (The starry heaven is the seat of life, because the Sun, which is the heart of the world, has his residence there, and is commanded by the Heavenly <note>original: "Empyreall"</note> Spirit.)

Now, we find that according to the will of the Divine essence poured out into the heavens, and consequently here below, both joyful and compassionate effects spring from the positive and expanding property of Unity, to recreate and stir up pleasure <note>original: "volupty"</note> in the creature. We also find sad and sorrowful <note>original: "trist"</note> outflows proceeding from the contracting virtue, by which God hides the face of his kindness from the creatures. Because of this, both desiring <note>original: "concupiscible"</note> as well as hateful <note>original: "odible"</note> or angry passions are caused in the world.

This opens the cabinet of the heart to produce in the vital spirit those good passions which sympathize with life and light: namely gladness, hope, confidence, love, mercy <note>original: "miserecord"</note>, and friendliness. 

Or, it is contracted, which gathers the spirits together in the heart. This engenders in the vital spirit those bad, privative passions that are in antipathy with the good ones that rejoice and comfort life. These passions are termed "antipathetic" because they are wholly contrary to the nature of those which are good. This number, proceeding from the heart's contraction, includes sadness, care, despair, fear, hatred, anger, fury, bashfulness, and so forth. 

So, by the former (expansion), the spirit looked up toward the Fountain of Light and rejoiced to see the pleasures thereof. By the latter (contraction), the spirit was forced to be deprived of the vision of light, and to look downward into the abyss of darkness, and so participate in the dark passions found there. As we observe the "little world" (the microcosm, or man), we may easily understand the logic and behavior of the "great world" (the macrocosm, or universe), since the principle of the part and the whole is the same <note>original Latin: "ea eadem sit ratio partis & totius"</note>. Likewise, the passions of the great world may be easily understood by observing those of the little world.

For example, the loadstone <term>loadstone: a naturally magnetized piece of the mineral magnetite</term> is to its mother earth as man is to the whole world. For this reason, man is called the "Son of the World" by Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure associated with hermetic philosophy</note>, just as Cardanus, Giambattista della Porta, Dr. William Gilbert, and others have identified the loadstone as the child or son of the earth. We find, I say, in the loadstone all the passions—both sympathetic and antipathetic—which affect its mother earth. It shares its poles with the earth; it shuns all things that are out of conformity with the earth; and it flees from whatever is contrary to its nature. 

Furthermore, it sympathizes with that which is like itself. It possesses its own equinoctials, colures <term>colures: two great circles on the celestial sphere that intersect at the poles</term>, meridians, and tropics, just as the earth has. In conclusion, its behavior suggests not only a sense of motion, but a kind of reason in its actions—namely, its refusal of what is contrary to it and its embracing and desiring of what agrees and conforms to its harmony. This shall be explained more extensively in the second part of this book, as well as in the magnetic experiments set down in the third and final book of this treatise.

To conclude, how this "mental beam" receives the commands or influences <note>original: "influxions"</note> of kindness or severity from above is explained in my previous discourse: specifically, by the permitting of bad spirits of darkness to reign and hold dominion, or by helping good spirits to execute their offices of joy and delight. 

Behold, here is the sum of all mystical and hidden sympathy or antipathy in the world. Because of the depth and difficulty of investigating this, some authors justly attribute it to the secret act and operation of an angelic power, which acts as a middle virtue between God and the creature. For this reason (as said before), an angel is defined as:

> As it were a middle power between God and Nature, from which operations are performed in things that their own nature <gloss>that is, their elementary form</gloss> would not produce—or at least would not produce in that way. Some say these operations come from a hidden property <note>original: "occult property"</note>, and others say "Because it is so" <note>original Latin: "Tanquam inter Deum & Naturam virtus media, à qua fiunt operationes in rebus quas vel natura eorum non faceret, non vel sic faceret; quas alii provenire dicunt à proprietate occulta, & alii quia tale"</note>.

### How this is demonstrated by Harmony, and what Sympathy and Antipathy are.

Sympathy and antipathy consist of a differing proportion or disproportion of matter (or world-spirit), guided by one and the same eternal soul. "Come, spirit, from the four winds" <note>original Latin: "Veni spiritus à quatuor ventis," a reference to Ezekiel 37:9</note>. This is demonstrated by a pipe, whose notes vary according to the proportion of spirit or air moved by one and the same breath. When these proportions meet disproportionately, they jar (discord); but when they meet proportionately, they accord and agree (concord). 

All spirits in creatures are proportioned by having more or less air, all within the spirit of life, moving and acting. According to these proportions in concord or discord, they agree or disagree, much like the weights of Pythagoras's hammers <note>Pythagoras supposedly discovered the ratios of musical intervals by listening to the different sounds made by blacksmiths' hammers of different weights</note> in proportionate or disproportionate bodies. Similarly, two strings stretched to the same tension give concording or discording sounds according to their length or thickness. We see this in the case of air in a pipe:

The creature's own quality performs good or evil, not the devil himself; rather, the devil acts through that quality. **Therefore, it is diabolical and to be abhorred.**

# The Second Part of this Second Book.

## In which the Magnetic Nature is truly dissected, and the reasons for Sympathetic and Antipathetic actions are revealed.

### CHAPTER 1.

#### The Author makes an introduction in this Chapter to his Magnetic Discourse, and then proceeds to the Chaos of opinions regarding the origin and attractive power of Magnetic Bodies.

I demonstrated to you in the previous section of this book the principles and origins of sympathy and antipathy. However, because it is not everyone's gift to soar so high at first as to be capable of a theory or meditation that penetrates into God’s storehouse or treasury—contained in the hidden depths <note>original: "abstruse bowells"</note> or center of His created nature—I will lower my focus a little for your better instruction and clearer information. I will clarify the hidden subject we have in hand by some common or visual demonstrations, which may guide and persuade people to believe that which might otherwise seem incredible.

In order to proceed more methodically, I will only lay down the chief foundation in this section, upon which I intend to build such experimental conclusions as shall direct those who disbelieve—even those who, through their ignorance, remain obstinate in their error (seeing that *Experience is the teacher even of fools* <note>original: "Experientia est etiam stultorum magistra"</note>)—into the more assured haven of faith and solid belief.

And because the effects of sympathy, and also those of antipathy in every thing, are brought about by a magnetic power—which is able both to repel by an angry or hateful expulsion, and to allure and draw toward itself by a desiring attraction (as shall be shown to you hereafter)—I think it most fit to search out diligently, and that with the eyes of Argus <note>In Greek mythology, Argus Panoptes was a hundred-eyed giant, representing all-seeing vigilance</note> (my brightest senses), or to penetrate deeply with the sharp sight of Lynceus <note>Lynceus was an Argonaut famed for his keen vision, able to see through trees and rocks</note> (my sharpest understanding), into the dark mystery of the loadstone’s or magnet's nature. This is so we may, with more assurance, enter into the practical demonstration of such a secret and hidden contemplation.

The secret operation of the weapon-salve <term>weapon-salve: a form of sympathetic medicine where an ointment was applied to the weapon that caused a wound rather than the wound itself</term> (so criticized by the ignorant) and the extraction of the "mummy" <term>mummy: in Paracelsian medicine, a spiritual essence or "vital balm" extracted from a living body or fresh corpse, not necessarily an Egyptian mummy</term> (both physical and spiritual, out of men or beasts) are termed "magnetic" because they imitate the active virtues of the magnet or loadstone. This also applies to the transplantation of an animal's vital, sickly, or healthy nature into any vegetable or animal; the secret of stealing the virtue and strength from one animal and infusing it into another; and the secret binding <note>original: "alligation"</note> of a plant's spirit with that of a man or any other animal (so that whatever happens to the one—such as moisture, dryness, cold, or heat—the other shall also experience).

Seeing, I say, that these operations are called magnetic, I will bend all my effort to create an open passage toward the dissection <note>original: "anatomising"</note> of all those mysteries by unpacking the spiritual bundle <note>original: "fardell"</note> of the loadstone. I will do this to peer into the fountain of its formal, interior, or central and essential actions, and to see the grounds of both its repelling and attracting passions. For if we are once able to find—by the subtlest gaze of our reason—its invisible passages and lurking places, and can then observe the specific root of their essences and discover the internal cause of each action, we shall easily conquer and surpass all the rest. This is because things that appear alike in external effect must necessarily prove to be of the same kind <note>original: "homogeniall"</note> and identical in their internal and hidden natures, as shall be proved more extensively to you. <insert>WW</insert>

But alas, why should I—being the least of the apostles <note>original: "minimus Apostolorum"</note>, the least of a thousand—presume to make so dangerous a voyage to that unknown island where this hidden magnetic nature dwells, among or in the middle of such dangerous and inaccessible rocks, when so many wise philosophers have failed and wandered...

# Sect. 2. Mosaicall Philosophy.
<sig>Dd</sig>

...on the variable and tempestuous seas of opinion, and have at last returned home only with the news of what others have reported about her being, her essence, and her active virtues. Do they know nothing of their own, except what they have attained by hearsay, or perceived by external operation? Good God! How many such "ships of fools" are there in this world? When they have traveled in their studies and learning for many years, sailing through the wide seas of vain and barely probable imaginings, they return home in their old age to the port of their infancy. Their wit or understanding is laden and burdened only with the poor fragments or merchandise of "He said it himself" <note>original: "*Ipse dixit*"; a phrase used to describe an assertion made but not proved.</note>, or other men's opinions, but they are able to say nothing fundamental based on their own knowledge.

So it is that we Christians, after we have traveled and made our life's journey <note>original: "peregrination"</note> and studies in the world, think it sufficient in the end to say: *Aristotle, Plato, Galen, Hippocrates*, and, in conclusion, "this man or that man said so"; therefore <note>original: "*Ergo*"</note>, it is so. This is despite the fact that the Scriptures teach us a truer Philosophy, which is entirely contrary to theirs. This kind of student is rightly pointed out by the Apostle, and numbered among those <margin>2 Timothy 3:6</margin> who are "always learning, but never arriving at the knowledge of the truth" <note>original: "*semper discentes, sed ad scientiam veritatis nunquam pervenientes*"</note>. For how is it possible for the blind to rightly lead or conduct the blind?

Others, having long steered the helm of their ship this way or that to find the hidden <note>original: "abstruse"</note> seat or home of the magnet's virtues, have barely dashed their vessel against her rocky island before returning with wondrous stories of what they have collected. In the end, their new imaginings have proved to be as superficial as the results of their search, and all have proved to be merely guesswork.

Others have been so far guided and directed in their search by the allure of the Pole Star that they have become stuck fast in the frozen seas and gone no further. But, when the ice thawed, they returned with imaginary wonders conceived of magnetic mountains and iron castles, even "eight degrees above the Moon"—that is, in the eighth sphere <note>In the traditional Ptolemaic model, the "eighth sphere" was the realm of the fixed stars, far beyond the planets and the Moon.</note>. Indeed, others soar even above that place as well.

By this we may understand how every man, according to his own fanciful chimeras, imagines a variety of "castles in the air"—and even above the stars—to be the home of the magnetic soul.

Some do not hesitate at all <note>original: "bogle not a jot"</note> to move away from the solid ground of the earth, but imagine the earth to be numbered among those stars which have the Sun for their fixed center, around which they move perpetually. Thus, they pretend the earth has the form of a star, which is very different from the <term>Peripatetic</term> <note>original: "Peripateticall"; referring to the traditional Aristotelian view of the universe.</note> form.

In conclusion, everyone has an opinion that differs somewhat from the next. So that you may know all this to be true, I will describe and recite some of their reports regarding this inquiry. These are the things they have recorded in their written monuments—as if in the chronicles or histories of their studious adventures or spiritual travels—after their long voyages in the muddy seas of their serious contemplations.

Among these, some soar upward and call the heavens as a witness to confirm their claims. Some sail to the far northern <note>original: "hyperboreall"</note> mountains, others to strange northern islands, to find the grounds of this miracle. Others send their spirits of inquiry down into the bowels of the earth and find it to be the universal starry form of the earth itself. Some claim the origin springs like atoms out of the stone and the object being attracted.

But among all these rational persons, I dare hardly rank one of another kind; for this man surely is to be numbered among those elders who have traveled in the "ship of fools." He, much like another Gryllus <note>original: "*Gryllus*"; a character from Plutarch who was transformed into a pig by Circe and preferred to remain an animal, symbolizing one who rejects human reason.</note> or a self-styled "eighth wise master" of Greece, insists that this power is <term>Cacomagical</term> <note>original: "Cacomagical"; meaning "bad" or demonic magic, from the Greek *kakos*.</note>, or the act of the devil.

Now, among those who have traveled in their spirits unto heaven to find out this mystery, one insists that the reason for the direction of the magnet <note>original: "*Load-stone*"</note> must be sought from the tail of the constellation of the Great Bear <note>original: "Bear-star"</note>. He affirms that the power of this starry Bear prevails over and has dominion over this stone, and is transferred from it into the iron; that man is Marsilio Ficino <note>original: *Marsilius Ficinus*</note>. But I reply that this is not so, because experience teaches us that iron itself has its poles, just as the magnet does. Through proper alignment <note>original: "adaption"</note>, iron will seek out and—by its own natural instinct—turn and direct itself toward the location of its own proper poles.

This is also the opinion of Peter Peregrinus <note>original: *Petrus Peregrinus*</note>, who, following the principles <note>original: "rules"</note> of Friar [Roger] Bacon, sought the arguments for magnetic direction from the poles of the heavens. Also, Girolamo Cardano <note>original: *Cardanus*</note> insists that the immediate cause of the variation in the stone’s power springs from the rising of the star in the Bear's Tail. Luca Gaurico <note>original: *Lucas Gauricus*</note> is also of their opinion, but he also joins the influence <note>original: "vertue"</note> of Saturn and Mars in this matter...

# Mosaicall Philosophy. Book 2.

...confessing at the same time that the main constellation in the Zodiac to which this Stone is subject is *Virgo*. *Albertus Magnus* says that the loadstone and iron are directed toward the Northern stars and follow them just as a plant called the *Heliotrope* <note>original: *Helitropion*; a plant that turns to face the sun</note> follows the sun. *Bessardus* holds a different opinion, making the pole of the Zodiac the source <note>original: fountain</note> of the loadstone’s virtue. Again, the *Conimbricensian College* <note>A group of Jesuit scholars at the University of Coimbra known for their influential commentaries on Aristotle</note> derives the cause of this from a part of the heavens not far from the Pole. But *Martin Cortesius* claims that this attractive virtue descends from a place beyond the Poles or the moving heavens. On the other hand, *Gaudentius Merula* tells us that the loadstone draws iron with the intent of directing it toward the North because it belongs to an order superior to iron, associated with the constellation of the Bear <note>Ursa Major or Ursa Minor</note>.

I must admit that beams which are expanded <note>original: dilated</note> are quick to rescue their "imprisoned" brethren and direct them toward their native home, but I cannot understand Merula's reasoning in this regard. Others make the heavens in general the source of this stone's virtue; for *Paracelsus* says that it is the stars, being full of the loadstone's power, which draw the iron toward them, and so on. This would seem probable because iron moves toward its poles even in the absence of a loadstone. *Fernelius* hesitates; for sometimes he admits the cause of this action is hidden <note>original: abstruse</note>, while in another place he credits the heavens as the author. *Scaliger*, soaring nearer to the point of truth, also assigns to it a celestial cause unknown to himself, asserting that earthly loadstones are derived not from the spheres or mountains of the stars, but from that essential power or essence that created them, which reigns in that part of heaven hanging over the northern <note>original: Septentrionall</note> point. And *Plato* seems to adhere to this opinion where he confesses the magnetic essence to be a divine power. 

And truly, they speak well, but in such a broad sense that their assertion, when examined closely, appears to their disciples (as I said) to be *explaining the unknown by something even more unknown* <note>original: *ignotum per ignotius*</note>. In such general terms, we might as well say that all things come from God. We will descend from our celestial speculations and look at the humble views of those who are too cautious and listen too much to the proverb, *Do not be high-minded* <note>original: *Noli altum sapere*; a Latin warning against pride or over-reaching curiosity</note>—or "Climb not too high"—and focus their attention downward toward the earth and its effects alone. 

Of this rank is *Fracastorius*, who, searching for the reason and origin of this attracting faculty, imagines that the far northern <note>original: Hyperboreall</note> mountains, which abound with rocks of this nature, draw these iron-like objects toward them. This fiction of his seems so plausible to various learned people that they follow it in their astronomical writings as well as their geographical tables, descriptions of the world, and sea charts or maps. If this were true, they would easily draw toward them all the ships that pass in the Northern Seas. *Olaus Magnus* and some others who follow his traditions say that the attractive force comes from certain northern islands which abound in that magnetic material. 

But leaving their fancy to the empty wind, I proceed to others. *Lucretius Carus*, a poet of the Epicurean sect, dreams that the attraction of iron is caused by an *outflowing of atoms*. For, he says, according to the opinions of the Epicureans, just as extremely subtle atoms emanate and flow out from everything, so do atoms fly out of the iron like *magnetic seeds* through a certain joining <note>original: coition</note> with the loadstone into the space between them. He claims that by the union or intertwining of both bodies, the iron is drawn, and so on. *Aphrodiseus*, *Joannes Costeus*, *Plutarch*, and even *Thomas Aquinas* incline toward this view. 

In reality, they ought to know that no attraction is made by an emission from the center to the circumference (that is, by expansion), but rather by sucking in and contracting from the circumference toward the center. Therefore, the emission of atomic seeds out of the iron can be no reason for its union with or movement toward the stone. Instead, it must be the loadstone that draws the beams or spirits out of the iron. For it appears that the iron does not draw itself to the loadstone, but is drawn toward it. *Thales* and *Anaxagoras* think that the loadstone has life in it because it attracts a substance like itself, just as living creatures do. *Lucretius* and *Orpheus* think there is a sympathy between the magnet and the iron like that between a male and female, and in this they do not err much. *Averroes*, *Scaliger*, and Cardinal *Cusanus* would have iron move toward the loadstone as if toward its original womb <note>original: *Matrix*</note>. *Galen* thinks that it draws by its "substantial form" <note>An Aristotelian term for the essence that makes a thing what it is</note>.

And now I must come to the opinion of my renowned Fellow or Colleague,

# Section 2. Mosaical Philosophy.

**Dr. William Gilbert**, known for his skill in magnetism and his deep research into both the theory and experimentation of this subject, believes that this attractive power <note>original: "virtue"</note> in the loadstone springs from formal actions, or original and primary powers. For he concludes that the magnetic force proceeds from a particular or singular form, differing from that formal and specific cause in mixed bodies mentioned by the **Peripatetics** <note>Followers of Aristotle’s philosophy</note>. Instead, he says it is a certain form which is the proper entity and existence of the starry globes and their homogeneous, uncorrupted parts, which he calls the primary, radical, and astral form—namely, the same kind of form found in the Sun, the Moon, and other celestial stars. 

He further asserts that, in a similar manner, there is such a form in the earth, which is that true magnetic power <note>original: "Puissance"</note> called the "first act" or "vigor." And this, he says, is not derived from the whole heaven, affirming that it is not created by sympathy through influence or hidden <note>original: "occult"</note> qualities, nor is it from any peculiar star. For he believes the loadstone has its magnetic power from the earth itself. This is the opinion of my learned former fellow-colleague, whose hard work and industry in researching the practical conclusions of this subject I must commend and extol. 

On the other hand, reason will not permit me to agree with his theoretical foundation or his idea of the root of the loadstone's power. For who can believe that the earth itself, much less the specific parts of it, can have any power radically from itself, when it is evident that both the earth and the heavens came radically out of the waters? And therefore, as the heaven was created before the earth, it must follow that the formal power of the earth descended entirely from heaven; consequently, the earth had no such property from itself. But I will discuss this more at length later. 

Among the heathen <note>original: "Ethnick"</note> philosophers, **Plato**, and among the Christians, **Scaliger** and **Fernelius**, believe that the cause of this attraction is divine and from above; however, they do not explain how or in what manner it works. Therefore, though they have spoken the truth in a general sense, by using such common words they seem to express that they do not truly understand what they are describing. 

Finally, I will conclude with the last opinion, which is the most lazy and insufficient of all, and is therefore worthy of being the final and most unworthy part—the "tail" or "waste" of them all. **Franciscus Rueus** expresses great doubt concerning the wonderful property of the loadstone. Because the limit <note>original: "pitch"</note> of his capacity can reach no higher than superficial things that can be perceived by the senses, he judges all effects beyond his reach to be evil magic <note>original: *Cacomagicall*; from the Greek *kakos* (evil) and *magikos* (magic)</note>. Consequently, he wonders whether the cause of these actions in the loadstone is an imposture or a subtle trick of evil spirits <note>original: *Cacodemons*</note>. And yet, this man is more to be tolerated than those who boldly assert that the actions and wonderful effects of the **Weapon Salve** <note>A controversial 17th-century "sympathetic" medicine where an ointment was applied to the weapon that caused a wound rather than the wound itself</note> are evil magic. For he does not speak as absolutely as they do; they seem to attribute all hidden effects to the Devil without any further doubt, thereby depriving God of His due credit. This man merely expresses a doubt as to whether it is so or not.

Sect. 2. Mosaical Philosophy.

...[the Word] did illuminate and create the waters in general; but the division of them—which was also made by the word **JAH** <note>A shortened form of the divine name Jehovah, often associated with the initial act of creation</note>—was fastened in formal ties by the properties of **ELOHIM** <note>The Hebrew name for God associated with judgment, law, and the material structure of the world</note>, or the life-giving Spirit of the Lord. And therefore David said in Psalm 33:6: *By the word of the Lord the heavens were made, and by his Spirit each formal virtue thereof* <note>original Latin: "Verbo Domini firmati sunt cæli, & Spiritu ab ore ejus omnis virtus eorum"</note>. 

For this reason, in all the acts of separating, creating, and forming—not only of the simple heavens and elements but also of the creatures composed of them, both in heaven and in earth—**ELOHIM** is always named by Moses. Specifically, this name is used when the darkness was sucked and drawn apart from the clear waters; when the gross or inferior waters were contracted away from the superior waters; when the thinner heavens were distinguished by thickening <note>original: "inspissation"</note> from the thicker elements; when the dry land was gathered together in the center by the freezing [coagulation] of the cold; and when the thinner air was condensed into starry bodies. For this reason, Aristotle says rightly that "The star is the thicker part of its sphere" <note>original Latin: "Stella sit densior pars sui orbis"</note>. 

All of this was the work of **ELOHIM**, who, after the heaven and the earth were made, did ordain and fashion by thickening <note>original: "incrassation"</note> the wandering <note>original: "erratick"</note> globe of **Saturn** and the fixed constellation of **Virgo**. Their total attractive and restrictive nature is contracted in the **Pole Star**, acting like the entire base of a pyramid tapering into the point of a cone. Therefore, by the contraction of this expansive, private virtue, the power becomes stronger; just as we see that a broad river gathered into a narrow strait between two rocks becomes more swift and violent, or as the glass-bead maker <note>original: "Bugle-maker"</note>, by blowing the whole flame into a single point, makes that point so powerful that it is able to melt glass. 

These two fixed constellations are assigned as principal ministers unto Saturn, being ordained for the distribution of his contracting <note>original: "stiptick"</note> influences, joined with a strong attraction <note>original: "concupiscible desire"</note> toward the nether world. Therefore, the astronomers have assigned them both the same nature because they perform the same act—namely, that of Saturn and Venus, as has been said. 

Wherefore, as it is said that "higher things are reported to rule lower things, so that just as things are acted here below, in like manner they were first effected above" <note>original Latin: "superiora dicuntur regere inferiora, adeo ut sicut fit inferius ita prius factum esset superius"</note>. Thus, of necessity, the North Pole in the air (or the sublunary element) is pointed at and marked out by the wind **Boreas** <note>The North Wind</note>. That same Pole in the water is characterized by the frozen sea; and in the earth, it is deciphered and manifested by the northern point of the **lodestone** <note>The magnetic compass needle</note>. These are all animated by these contractive, or restrictive, and cold, and dry celestial natures. 

These, in turn, have their power in the earth and waters successively from the Orders of the **Cherubim** and **Thrones** <note>Two of the nine choirs of angels in traditional Christian and Jewish theology</note>, who receive their attractive and restrictive power radically from the Attribute **ELOHIM Ruach** <note>The Spirit of God</note>. This attribute coagulates and thickens things by contracting and drawing the effects of **JEHOVA'S** expanding property—turning them from a dilated, transparent, clear form and light into a thick, opaque, and heavy nature. 

This is made manifest in the creation of frost, snow, ice, and hail by the northern act and property of God, which made the Psalmist say: *He sends out snow like wool, and disperses the frost like ashes; he casts down his ice like morsels; who is able to endure before his cold?* <margin>Psal. 147.</margin> <note>original Latin: "Emittit nives sicut lanam, & pruinas quasi cineres dispergit, dejicit gelu tanquam frusta, coram frigore ejus quis consistat?"</note>. 

From this, it appears that it is the contractive act of **JEHOVA**, in his property as **ELOHIM**, which immediately effects these things by means of his Northern <note>original: "Boreall"</note> organs. These are first angelic, then stellar or starry bodies (being animated by the angelic), and lastly, windy and elemental (which are animated by the starry influences). The essence of all these is in God and from God, or **JEHOVA**. He is one God in essence, which is expressed by the name **JEHOVA**, but in property, he is distributed into many branches. Accordingly, every branch has its peculiar illuminating boughs, and each illuminating bough expands itself by a subdivision of formal twigs, or life-giving beams, into an infinity of actions. These do not vary from the main source in essence, but only in property.

I told you before that the eternal Unity—everlastingly One in essence, dividing or transforming itself by property into a Trinity—shaped out or described ideally the archetypal or internal world. According to this example, he afterwards outlined or framed the typical or external world. Therefore, it must follow that if the typical or natural world was framed after the idea in the intellectual or mental world, then whatever parts or properties were made evident to our understanding in this world were also the same in the archetype; for *that which makes a thing such, is itself more so* <note>original Latin: "Quod facit tale est magis tale"</note>. Just as no house was ever built by a carpenter or bricklayer that wasn't first outlined in the idea of his intellect, then drawn on paper, and finally executed in solid form; so also *David* confessed that he had the plan for the Temple which *Solomon* built, first drawn out ideally by God's finger. 

Now, when God had in his divine counsel thus ordered and shaped an ideal world within himself to put it into execution—and, as it were, to make it appear to human senses—he emitted himself out of himself in the form of an eternal emanation called his Image. This was his wisdom, by which the universal world and every part of it was produced according to the ideal pattern within itself. This being the case, and because the divine essence cannot be divided in any way (even though it varies in property), it follows that every particular beam which shines out differently from that universal <note>original: "catholick"</note> emanation to create different things is one indivisible essence with the whole emanation. Therefore, he is said to *fill all, and to be all in all; and that the incorruptible spirit is in all things, and that he fills the whole earth.*

# Section 2. Mosaical Philosophy.

...the elements, and you shall find the starry and quintessential <note>original: "quintessentiall"; referring to the "fifth essence," a pure, heavenly substance beyond the four earthly elements</note> nature. Open these, and you shall understand the subtle alterity <note>original: "alterity"; meaning otherness or the state of being different</note> of the angelic spirit, in which exists the divine act or immediate beam from God. In this work, therefore, a separation occurs: in the first, there is a sensible aspect; in the other, we must behold with intellectual eyes. Thus, you may observe how everything is in each thing, and each thing is in everything. It was upon this principle that Hermes <note>Referring to Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure to whom many mystical and alchemical writings were attributed.</note> said (speaking mystically and not in the common sense): "He who constructs our furnace with the glass vessel to it, creates a new world" <note>original Latin: "Qui fornacem cum vase nostro construit, novum mundum conflat"</note>.

But what need is there for more words when we find all this confirmed by demonstration? For we know that the loadstone <note>original: "Load-stone"; a naturally magnetized mineral</note> is but a part of the Earth, and yet it possesses all its circles and both its poles. Indeed, it has that very nature in all respects between each pole and circle that the whole Earth has. Because of this, it is termed **Terrella** <note>original: "Terrella"; Latin for "little Earth"</note>, or a little Earth. In the same way, the whole Earth may be termed **parvus mundus** <note>original: "parvus mundus"; Latin for "small world" or microcosm</note>, since it contains the poles, circles, and astral—as well as elemental—natures of the great world, just as the great world represents the Archetype <note>The original divine blueprint or "idea" of the world in the mind of God.</note> which is intellectually carved out in the all-working Spirit of Wisdom or sacred Emanation.

Indeed, we can go even deeper into these miniatures: for if a piece of iron rod, which naturally points North and South, is broken off, that small piece will also have its North and South poles and its circles as exactly as the whole rod did. Nevertheless, the main rod still keeps its North and South points as before. The same thing happens with the loadstone, as experience shall hereafter make even more plain.

To come a little nearer to the explanation of this mystery, you must understand that this eternal, universal emanation is the essential and spiritual rock. From this rock, first the great world in general, and then all particular things within it, were carved or framed by generalities. First, they were framed according to the Ten General Emanations <note>A reference to the ten Sephiroth of the Kabbalah, which represent different attributes of God.</note> and their properties, which the pagans <note>original: "Ethnickes"</note> in some sense referred to as their ten general Predicaments <note>The ten Categories of Aristotle, which Fludd is attempting to reconcile with or replace with biblical philosophy.</note>. These, in turn, had their specialties or subordinate degrees of many ranks and orders of dignity. All of these were at last made apparent by the infinity of individuals which they produced according to their kinds, following those diverse beams of the multifaceted Will of God which this eternal emanation poured into them.

All of these particular beams—being more or less not divided in essence from the universal emanation, or the Spirit of Wisdom that made all things—are the spiritual **Corner-stone** on which every creature, whether particular or universal, formally and essentially consists. This Corner-stone is that internal essence in everything which gives life; it is also all and over all the things that it enacts with life. Therefore, the soul, whose center is this Corner-stone, is said to be in every part. I will stop speaking of its action in other creatures and will only insist on our main subject at hand: the Earth and her offspring, among which the feminine loadstone and its iron-rich <note>original: "ferruginous"</note> mass are chiefly reckoned. Divine Philosophy teaches us that the globe of the Earth is sustained by this Corner-stone, and consequently receives its many virtues from it.

# Mosaical Philosophy. Book 2.

<margin>Wisdom 1:7</margin>
...more or less, with a several distinct power <note>original: "Virtue"; here meaning an inherent spiritual or physical efficacy</note>, as a gift bestowed on it for its own sake. For the wise man [Solomon] testifies that *this essential spirit fills the whole earth.* Therefore, as no essential power which issues from it can be divided from it, so each particle of the earth must be endowed, more or less, with the property of the whole. This is because it moves entirely upon one spiritual line or axle-tree (as Job seems to declare), which possesses a twofold property. These properties differ according to the two principles proceeding from the Divine Unity: namely, His <term>Nolunty</term> <note>original: "Nolunty"; from the Latin 'nolle' (to be unwilling), representing God’s negative, contracting, or "dark" principle</note> or privative and contracting nature—for it operates by a privative, contractive, cold, and congealing disposition, which is more or less effective as it approaches each Pole (that is to say, the North or South)—and His <term>Volunty</term> <note>original: "Volunty"; from the Latin 'velle' (to will), representing God’s positive, expansive, or "light" principle</note> or positive, dilating, and dissolving nature. This is because this spiritual central Sun, in the middle point of the axis, emits its beams toward the circumference, just as the celestial Sun and its eternal Agent dart forth beams from the <term>Equinoctial</term> <note>The celestial equator</note>, which is the circumference of the middle point in the axle-tree, toward its Poles; yet it approaches no nearer the Poles than the limited Tropic of each Hemisphere. 

And this is the reason for that antipathy noted in both iron and the <term>loadstone</term> <note>A naturally magnetized mineral</note>. For if you divide the loadstone in the middle between both its poles (specifically at its Equator), and then afterward, if you try to place the middle part of one hemisphere—namely, the Northern point C—against the South Pole...

For one is the seat of the dilating property, and the other is the natural place of the contracting property; one is hot, the other cold; one is attractive, by sucking from the circumference toward the center, while the other is repulsive, by dilating its beams from the center to the circumference. 

On the contrary, sympathy in the loadstone occurs where like is fitly applied to its like, in both order and condition. For if you attempt to join the Equator of one hemisphere to that of the other, they will immediately close and unite with one another. Because of the continuation of the spiritual axle-tree, one pole draws the hemisphere next to it: namely, B draws the North Hemisphere C, A; and the North Pole C reciprocally draws the South Hemisphere B, A; and they both join at A. Also, the two poles agree together in harmony for the reasons mentioned above. Thus, if you put the North Pole to the South, they draw and attract one another and create a union. By this, every wise researcher <note>original: "Speculator"</note>...

...may discern the reason for sympathy and antipathy in all things, as well as the manner of attraction and dilation in every creature. One can see how each nature inclines properly toward its own kind, but flies or inclines naturally away from its contrary. All of this proceeds from the opposite properties within one radical essence, as I will prove immediately by a more familiar experiment.

In the <term>weather-glass</term> <note>An early type of thermometer or thermoscope that measured temperature through the expansion and contraction of air</note> which I described in my previous philosophical discourse, you may discern two points corresponding to the two poles: namely, the <term>matrass head</term> <note>The glass bulb at the top of the weather-glass</note> above, resembling the Northern Pole, and the water below, compared to the Southern Pole.
