Sect. 2. Mosaical Philosophy.

...celestial heaven, or sublunary spirit, which is between these two Poles—the middle of which the Equinoctial cuts in Figure 1, being midway between the two Poles. We find constantly that when the air included in the top of the <term>matrass</term> <note>A long-necked glass flask used in chemistry; here part of a "weather-glass" or early thermometer</note>, or bolt’s-head, is cold—namely, when the northern blasts are sent forth—it will be contracted, and consequently will suck or draw up the water. From this, we are taught the reason for the attractive nature, not only in the northern or septentrional winds, but also in the **loadstone** and all other things which draw and suck toward them by the contraction of the air. Specifically, they have that property from the power of God's Spirit, which blows from the north through His angelic organs. 

By this it is also made evident why one Pole sucks and attracts from the other in the loadstone: namely, by the continuity of the spiritual axle-tree <note>axis</note>, which is created and animated by one "corner-stone"—that is, an essential and central spirit—though it possesses two opposite conditions in which it works through many different degrees. Therefore, **Solomon** terms it *simple* or *one* <note>original: "simplex, or unicus"</note> in regard to its divine nature, and *manifold* <note>original: "multiplex"</note> in respect to the fact that it works and operates in a multifaceted manner. For just as it works about the poles of the axle-tree by attracting and sucking toward it through cold and drought, so about the Equinoctial—and increasingly as it approaches from the poles toward the Equinoctial—it varies in ten thousand proportions, more or less, in **dilatation** <note>expansion</note>, by reason of the manifold degrees of heat which this central Sun of life imparts to the air. 

This is not only manifested in the aforementioned weather-glass; for we find that the more the heavenly Sun, with its divine central agent, approaches us, the more the external air—being expanded by its heat—also expands the air contained in the neck of the matrass or bolt's-head and drives down the water. That is, it repels the cold of winter, which came in through showers of rain sent from the south toward its proper pole. 

So we see that just as the nature of the cold pole is to draw or suck toward it by condensation (which is effected by contraction, or made by a <term>Saturnine faculty</term> <note>In alchemy and astrology, Saturn is associated with cold, contraction, and weight</note>), so the nature of the hot Equinoctial and its adjacent parts is to expel its opposite by dilatation, which is effected by a thinning heat. This is the reason, as is already demonstrated, that the Equinoctial of the loadstone refuses to be joined to the pole, just as, on the contrary side, the pole reciprocally abhors the Equinoctial. Also, this is the reason that in the pole of the stone there is such great power of attraction, and that it sucks the iron toward it **at right angles** <note>original: "ad angulos rectos"</note>, that is, in a perpendicular manner. Then, the nearer the needle, piece of steel, or iron wire approaches the Equinoctial of the stone, the more its slanted angle in union or conjunction with the stone will increase. So when it comes directly to the Equinoctial, it will lose all angular contact and lie flat, as it were, on its belly, as you may see by this true observation following:

But because these demonstrations may seem somewhat intricate to common people—as they are ignorant of the central sun of the earth, which the Philosophers call the **Master-workman of nature** <note>original: "Archaeum naturae"</note>—and because it will be difficult for them to conceive what an axle-tree of the earth may be and what its poles are; and again, since the right use of the loadstone or practice with the weather-glass is unknown to many men, I will proceed to a kind of proof and explanation of this matter that is familiar to every person of whatever rank. It cannot be denied that Man, and all other creatures (whether vegetable or animal), are composed of a living soul, which is internal, and a body, which is external. We ought to judge the same of the earth, for it has an inward spirit by which it operates in diverse ways. And again, as there is no animal or vegetable that can exist without...

Mosaicall Philosophy. Book 2.

...without the air, because everything lives and exists by it through inspiration—for by that means they suck in the celestial influence. So also, the airy element feeds the inward spirit of the earth and conveys all the heavenly influences from above into her body, making her the mother of all minerals and vegetables. I told you before that all inferior things and their operations are the types or likenesses of things above. God animates the Angels, the Angels inform the stars, and the starry demons (or Olympic spirits) send down influences into the winds. The winds then inform the universal <note>original: "catholick"</note> element of the air in a fourfold way—that is, according to the nature of the four winds. This *fourfold information* gives a name to the four elements. 

Although in the universal air there is only one substance in essence, it varies in nature according to a fourfold condition, following the will and property of that one Spirit. This Spirit is the only efficient actor or agent in this metamorphosis, or *Protean transmutation* <note>A change in shape or form, named after the Greek god Proteus who could change his shape at will</note>, from one nature or form into another, even though he uses both angelic and starry instruments <note>original: "organs"</note>. He is said to ride upon the cherubim and to glide upon the wings of the winds.

<margin>Ezekiel 36 <note>The author likely intends Ezekiel 37:9, the vision of the valley of dry bones.</note></margin>
For this reason, the Prophet says, *“Come, O spirit, from the four winds, and breathe upon these slain bodies that they may live.”* He did not say, "Come, O spirits," but "Come, O spirit." By this, he argued that it is only one Spirit which blows essentially from the four winds. Consequently, this one Spirit in essence is only one thing, though fourfold in regard to its properties. Just as in this archetypal Spirit the whole world was ideally divided into poles and portions distinguished by spiritual circles, so also in all the regions of the world, he constantly observes the same character of position—namely, in the starry world as in the airy, and in the airy as in the water and earth. 

For in the heavens, the Northern Pole is pointed at and marked out with the starry character found in the tail of the *Great Bear* <note>Ursa Major</note>. In the air, it is manifested at that very point from which *Boreas* <note>The North Wind</note> or the North wind blows, which corresponds exactly to the Pole Star. Again, the fact that the earth observes the same order in the direction of her pole is confirmed by the turning of the loadstone and iron toward the North Star. Thus you see that it is only one Spirit in essence that works all in all. 

I proceed therefore to my demonstration, which is so familiar to every person that no one in their senses can deny it. I am sure no man can be ignorant that when the North wind blows, the air is by nature cold and dry. Therefore, it is converted into the condition and consistency of earth—namely, from a clear, transparent, light, subtle, dissolved, and expanded <note>original: "dilated"</note> state of air into a troubled, opaque (or dark), gross, heavy, and contracted substance. Experience teaches us that it is transmuted into snow, hail, frost, and ice; that is, from an airy spirit into an earthly and solid body, and from an invisible and mobile state to a visible and fixed disposition. In conclusion, the entire air is changed into a spiritual and corporal earth. This transmutation comes from that cold, dry, and attractive form which it borrowed from the Northern wind, or the "septentrional" <note>Northern</note> property of the Divine Spirit. This Spirit orders all things and alters them from one form to another by "the breath of his nostrils" (as the Scriptures allegorically speak) or by those windy emissions or angelic emanations which it sends from the four corners of the earth. So by his breath from the North, he exercises that property in the lower world by which he draws or attracts from the circumference toward the center. Thus, he congeals, thickens <note>original: "inspissateth"</note>, and hardens soft spirits by the contraction and squeezing together <note>original: "coarctation"</note> of those parts which were previously porous and expanded.

But some will perhaps reply and say: How is it likely that the emanation or emission of spirits from the gate of *Binah* <note>In Kabbalah, Binah represents "Understanding," the third Sephirah, often associated with the feminine principle and contraction</note> under the Attribute of **ELOHIM** <note>A Hebrew name for God associated with judgment and the material world</note>, or the streaming forth of the breath or blasts from *Boreas* and his two side-winds <note>original: "collateralls"</note>, can harden by contraction? How can they suck and draw in spirits from the circumference to the center when their emissions move straight from the North southward and make no reflection by which any such motion *from the circumference to the center* <note>original: "a circumferentia ad centrum"</note> should be made? 

I answer that this is accomplished in a wonderful way, worthy of consideration by the finest minds. We must first consider that the property of the Attribute **ELOHIM** was ordained before all beginnings to endow the negative or contractive nature of the eternal Unity's *Will* <note>original: "Volunty"</note>—namely, darkness. For when God will not show the light of his countenance, he reflects his light into himself; that is, he withdraws it from the circumference to the center and leaves only darkness for the creatures. This

### Sect. 2. Mosaicall Philosophy.

This property of God is antagonistic <note>original: "antipatheticall"</note> to those parts of the world, and to all creatures, that derive their life from a natural heat. That heat had its beginning from God’s benevolent emanation—that is, from the act of unity, through an emission or expansion <note>original: "dilatation"</note> from the center to the circumference (by which I mean, from unity into the many). It follows, therefore, that though the outward movement of winds from the north is straight, their essential property, proceeding immediately from God’s angelic instrument <note>original: "organ"</note>, is contractive and pulling from the circumference toward the center. This is because it is an emission which, by the divine Spirit’s flowing out and acting in the nature of *ELOHIM* <note>A Hebrew name for God often associated in this philosophy with rigor, judgment, and the creation of form</note>, is cold, dry, thickening <note>original: "coagulative"</note>, or congealing, and prone to stillness. It is therefore antagonistic and opposed to the nature of the air, because air is naturally hot and moist, and is animated by the expanding action which the universal <note>original: "catholick"</note> spirit sends or breathes out of the celestial Sun and other life-giving <note>original: "vivifying"</note> stars, such as *Jupiter* and *Venus*. 

For this reason, it follows that when the Northern <note>original: "Boreall"</note> spirits are sent forth into the air, the natural heat or life of the air flies or withdraws itself from its outer edges toward its center upon contact with these cold, antagonistic spirits. This happens partly by that contractive motion within itself, caused *by antiperistasis* <note>original: "per antiperistasin"; the phenomenon where a quality is intensified when surrounded by its opposite, such as heat concentrating in the center of a body when the exterior is chilled</note>, or by the meeting of its contrary, and partly by the mingling of a new earthly form. Thus, it is congealed and falls to the earth as if it were dead and immovable, in the form of snow, hail, frost, and ice. 

In the same way, we see that the airy life in other creatures, whose formal being consists of God’s expanding property, is forced to fly from the circumference to the center. This leaves the external parts chilled, cold, and prone to a deadly freezing or a lethal rest. We observe this not only in animals, but also in vegetables; their blood (as I may call it) or vital sap is congealed by the winter and northern cold, and remains, as it were, lifeless. It stays this way until it is resolved and melted again by the life-giving and expanding force of the following Spring <note>original: "Vernall"</note> and Southern <note>original: "Australl"</note> virtue, and the severe tie or icy knot of the northern nature is undone. 

For this reason, you may discern that there is but one universal <note>original: "catholick"</note> element, which is partly subject to the dark, contracting, and pulling property of God’s Spirit, and partly capable of receiving His positive, light-filled, expanding disposition. This common subject is the spirit or air of the sublunary <note>The earthly realm below the moon</note> world. Through less thickening or contraction, caused by the west winds, it is made into water; through more compression and constriction, caused by the northern and winter blasts, it becomes snowy or icy earth. Conversely, by less expansion and thinning, it is made airy or vaporous (caused by the spring season and south wind), and by a greater thinning and refinement <note>original: "rarefaction and exaltation"</note>, it is made into fire through the dominion of those spirits sent out from the east and the summer’s heat. Both of these main, twofold, divided properties belong to one and the same Spirit, as was stated before. 

Truly, this common demonstration can deceive no one, since even the unthinking <note>original: "unreasonable"</note> creatures are moved by a natural inclination either to sympathize and rejoice with the mercy and comfort of the one property, or to fly from and avoid the severer assaults of the other, which are antagonistic to their nature. But to return to our main business: it is manifest by what has already been said that the northern breath is contractive, attractive, thickening, and prone to darkness, immobility, and rest. The south wind (or rather the wind from the Equator <note>original: "Æquinoctiall"</note>) is contrary in nature to it, being ready to undo all that the north wind achieved—namely, to dissolve the congealed air (which was made into snow, frost, hail, and ice) back into water, and water into air; to make transparent that which was dark, and to make thin that which was previously thick. Therefore, between these properties there is no more sympathy than I have shown you exists between the Equator and the Pole of a magnet <note>original: "Load-stone"</note>. 

Again, the following testimony of true Philosophy clearly confirms that both these opposite natures proceed and spring from one and the same divine and universal Spirit, which operates all in all, everywhere, and consequently in earth as well as in heaven:

<margin>Psalm 147.</margin>
> *When God sends forth his word to the earth, it runs most swiftly; he produces snow like wool, and spreads the frost like ashes. He casts down the ice like morsels; who is able to stand against his cold? He sends forth his word and melts them; as soon as he blows his wind, the waters flow.* <note>original Latin: "Deo emittente sermonem suum in terram quam celerrimè excurrit, qui nives emittit sicut lanam, & pruinam quasi cineres dispergit, dejicit gelu tanquam frusta, coram frigore ejus quis consistat? Emittit verbum suum & liquefacit ista, simul ac efflat ventum suum, effluunt aquæ."</note>

# Mosaicall Philosophy. Book 2.

...dissolves all these; as soon as he breathes forth his wind or *Spirit*, the frozen <note>original: "congealed"</note> waters begin to flow and move. By this, it appears that the *Word* or *Spirit* of God congeals by one property and dissolves by another. Consequently, as God is entirely one in essence, it is one and the same *Spirit* that effects these fourfold alterations in the one universal <note>original: "catholick"</note> spirit of the world. These alterations are called distinct *Elements* by the *Ancients* because they could never yet thoroughly determine what the essential form of the *Elements* actually was.

<margin>2 Peter 3</margin>
But if they had well considered the four *Elements*—of which they spoke so much and, it seems, understood so little essentially—or if they had well conceived that heaven and earth were made of water, and by water through the *Word*, as *Sacred Philosophy* teaches us, then they would have known that the common physical substance <note>original: "substantial Subject"</note> of them all was but one created watery spirit. They would also have known that this spirit’s four-fold shaping <note>original: "information"</note> was effected by one increasing formal essence or *Divine Word*, acting upon and shaping that universal *Element* by a four-fold emanation. Thus, the will of one creating *Spirit*, working through four *Angels* of opposite natures, makes, disposes, or changes this one spiritual watery substance into this or that *Element* every day, according to the will of the *Creator*. 

All of this is evidently demonstrated by the *weather-glass* <note>An early type of thermometer or thermoscope used to show the expansion and contraction of air due to temperature changes</note>. For the air enclosed within it converts itself into the form of any of the *Elements* through contraction or expansion, and is altered according to the nature of the *Macrocosmic* blast or wind that blows. 

Now, whereas it may be asked: "From where, then, did the earth and waters that reside perpetually here below come?" I answer that they are the effects which the winds, by the will of God, or the *Spirit of God* <note>original Hebrew: "ELOHIM RUACH"</note>, originally produced. These were framed first out of the air—namely, by thickening it by one degree into water, and solidifying <note>original: "ingrossing"</note> it by another into solid and fixed earth. This appeared during the third day's Creation, where it was said that "Let the dry land appear out of the waters" <note>original Latin: "Aridum apparuerit ex aquis"</note>. 

The Divine Philosopher *St. Paul* confirms all this where he affirms that we ought to believe by faith that those things which are visible were first made of things invisible and unseen. Furthermore, if the two lower bodies (earth and water) did not resolve themselves little by little—though imperceptibly—into air, it would not be possible for the earth or the water to hold that abundance of water, stones, and sulfur caused by lightnings and such things which fall from the air. Yet we see that neither the air, nor water, nor earth are ever found to be larger than their natural, accustomed proportions. 

By this, therefore, I have sufficiently explained to you the attractive and contractive property of the *Northern Pole* in the air. This implies that as the *Northern* blasts are enemies to life—because they contract from the circumference to the center, which is contrary to the expansion of human life—all things reduced to a chill, cold, and *Northern* property (be they airy, watery, or earthy) draw strongly toward themselves. This is proved by the *weather-glass*: for the included air, being animated by the effects of a strong and persistent *Northern wind*, sucks and draws the waters upward—namely, from the equilibrium <note>original: "Æquinoctiall"</note> point of the glass toward the center of the *North Pole*, which is represented by the head of the flask <note>original: "mattras"</note>. 

By the same reasoning, congealed spirits in any earthly substance suck or draw from the exterior to the interior. We observe this when *Bole Armoniac* <note>A red, astringent medicinal clay from Armenia</note> sucks moisture into itself, and also when any other earth is thoroughly dry. In its own natural condition, because it possesses the quality of the *North*, it sucks and draws watery moisture strongly. However, this is because of its dryness; the attraction in the *lodestone* <note>original: "Load-stone," a naturally magnetized mineral</note> is different. 

Because the lodestone has the essential nature of its mother Earth and the virtue of the *North* in its *Pole*, it greedily draws the masculine, sulfurous spirits out of *Iron*. It does this with a feminine appetite because of the closeness and likeness of one nature to another. The *Pole Star* has the same regard for the *lodestone* as the *lodestone* has for the *Iron*, which is its like. For "Nature rejoices and delights in its own nature" <note>original Latin: "Natura Natura suâ gaudet & lætatur"</note>, as *Empedocles* truly testifies. Both the *Iron* and the *lodestone* are of one mine, one vein, and one nature, seeing that both are of an earthy and northern <note>original: "boreall"</note> disposition. Therefore, the *lodestone* and its formal internal spirits, being more burdened with impurities than the refined *Iron*, draw their likeness out of the purified *Iron* or *Steel* with a wonderful appetite (perhaps to be assisted in being delivered from that burden). In this action, it sucks the *Iron* toward itself...

# Mosaicall Philosophy. Book.

...of the magnet <note>original: Load-stone</note>, in the same way that the male or *Mars* naturally desires and is attracted to *Venus*. However, because the female, due to her coldness, most desires the company of the male, the spiritual beams of her affection seek him with the greatest intensity. Therefore, she draws and allures the beams of the male (who is of a hotter and thus more "perfect" nature) toward her. This is observed in iron, which I consider to be the male; for even though iron, on its own without the magnet's help, turns its poles toward the poles of the world by a natural inclination, we observe that it does so more slowly and with less appetite—acting more out of formal necessity than material desire.

I conclude, therefore, from what has been already said, that two similar things belonging to the nature of the Equinoctial <note>The celestial equator, representing balance and warmth</note> and temperate zone embrace each other through a sympathetic emission of beams from the center toward the circumference. Such is the love of those creatures that live by a positive emanation, such as animals with a hot disposition (whether dry or moist). They do not perceptibly pull one spirit into another; instead, they work through a union created by the meeting of their lights after they have emitted their formal beams. These relate to the property of the spirit that comes from the East and South winds, whose natures are to expand from the center rather than contract from the circumference. Conversely, two similar natures that share the property of the Poles and cold zones embrace and "hug" one another by contraction—namely, by sucking and drawing each nature from the circumference toward their center. We see this when a magnet is divided in the middle: it will draw and suck the other piece toward itself until both parts are perfectly joined at the point where they were divided. The attractive affection between iron and the magnet is also created in this way, as these are substances subject to the influence of *Saturn*, *Virgo*, and the Pole Star.

The alchemical <note>original: Chimycall</note> perspective does not vary much from these physical and astronomical assertions. If we observe the nature of the magnet in that context, we find it does not spring from a natural birth, but rather from a "monstrous" generation, as it is known to come from unequal and different parents, much like a mule. If we closely observe its composition, we find that its mother—the passive, physical mass—is a common, stony, and earthly *Mercury*. Its father—the active form—is a metallic or sulfurous "Martial" spirit <note>relating to the planet Mars and iron</note>. In conclusion, we see that their mixture is achieved in this way: the Mercurial liquid of a stony, earthly, or Saturnine nature (while still in its primary state or "shell") was a close neighbor to the *Mercury* of *Mars*—for these two natures are commonly found near each other. Because of this, it acquired a slight transformation, appearing to be joined by a tight and nearly continuous union. Thus, the composition exists halfway between a Martial metal and a Saturnine stone; it could be called a half-metamorphosed *Mercury*, or a kind of hermaphroditic Saturn-*Mercury*. When the sulfurous Martial spirits—the metallic forms—enter this mass, it receives and preserves them in its womb as their proper mother and passive container. By this means, the mass is solidified into a stony body.

Now, since every spirit—including that of the magnet—desires to be nourished by what is closest and most like its own nature (which is found only in iron), the internal Martial spirit of the magnet draws the body of iron to itself. In a hidden way, it seems to suck its nourishment from the iron. Therefore, I believe that the fixed salt in the iron or magnet is partly of a hot and dry Martial nature—and thus of a fiery, earthly condition—and partly of a cold, dry, contracting <note>original: stiptick</note>, and Saturnine quality, which it receives from its earth. Thus, two types of strange attraction converge in the magnet. And because *Venus* is said to be the female friend and companion to *Mars*, she adds a strong desire <note>original: concupiscible</note> to the attraction and restrains the angry and hateful <note>original: irascible and odible</note> properties of *Mars* with her feminine embrace. ### CHAP. III.

->*Of the excellency of Man in the Animal Kingdom, and of the admirable nature of the magnet in the Mineral.*<-

I may well presume to compare the magnet <note>original: Load-stone</note> in its disposition with man, considering the admirable virtues and dignity of the one in the animal kingdom, and the miraculous operations and mystical properties of the other in the mineral region. As for man (for the sake of dignity I will speak of him first), there is such a super-eminent and wonderful treasure hidden in him that wise men have believed that the perfect wisdom of this world consists in the knowledge of oneself—namely, to find out that secret mystery that lurks within him. 

For man is said to be the center of every creature, and for that cause he is called the Microcosm <note>original: Microcosmus</note>, or the "little world": "The center and miracle of the world" <note>original: Centrum & miraculum mundi</note>, containing in himself the properties of all creatures, celestial as well as terrestrial, and consequently those of the magnet. He is "the Temple of God" <note>original: Templum Dei</note>; "the Body of Christ" <note>original: Corpus Christi</note>; "the Dwelling-place of the Holy Spirit" <note>original: Habitaculum Spiritus sancti</note>, as the Apostle has taught us. Truly, it should not be imagined that God would choose an unworthy dwelling place. 

And therefore, in considering this and inquiring after so great a mystery, we need to proceed with our most exact discretion and judgment from the visible things of man to the invisible—that is, to penetrate with the sharpest edge of our wit by demonstration from effects to causes <note>original: a posteriori</note>, or from the external man into the bowels of his secret, mystical, and internal being. 

Therefore we proceed thus: Seeing that man is rightly reported by Hermes to be the "son of the world," just as the world is the "son of God"—being that he is framed after the image of the Archetype <note>The original pattern or divine model</note> (for which reason he is termed the "little world")—it will be necessary to understand that he is likewise divided into a heaven and earth, just as the great world was. Consequently, he contains within himself his heavens, circles, poles, and stars, no differently than the great world does. 

And also, as we find that the spiritual image of the heavens, with their circles and poles, are also outlined <note>original: delineated</note> in the earth and every part of it (as appears in the magnet <note>original: Loadstone</note> and iron), so the character of the inward man is deciphered and portrayed in the outward man, no differently than we may judge the shape of a sword by its scabbard, or the kernel by its shell. 

Concerning the research or inquiry after the world's poles in man, there has risen no small difference among the philosophers. Pythagoras, Plato, and Aristotle have decreed the eastern part of the world to be man's right hand; their reason is because the daily <note>original: diurnall</note> motion of the heavens, which proceeds from the First Mover <note>original: Primum mobile</note>, is carried out from east to west; and consequently the west must be his left hand or "sinister" portion. In placing man according to this position, his face must look unto the north, and his back toward the south. But

Empedocles disagrees with this opinion, claiming that the summer solstice <note>original: Æstivall Solstice</note>, or the Tropic of Cancer, is the right hand of the world. It follows, therefore, that the winter station <note>original: Hyemall station</note> of the sun, or the Tropic of Capricorn, must be the left. According to this direction, a man’s face must look toward the West. For my part, my opinion is opposed to both of their minds. Moved by reasons both theological and natural, I would instead align a man's face toward the East <note>original: Orient</note>. In this position, his back would face the West, the North Pole would correspond to his left hand, and the South Pole to his right. We can prove that this position is not only naturally, but also divinely, suited to the Microcosm <note>The "Little World," or human being</note> in this way: the Patriarchs, Prophets, and Apostles always turned their faces toward the East during their most devout prayers. This is an argument that this quarter of the world was designated by the Creator for the front part of man.

So what Pagnine <note>Santes Pagnino (1470–1541), a leading philologist of the Renaissance</note> calls the eastern angle of the world, Tremellius calls the face or front part of the world, and so forth. From this it appears (and, I think, without further controversy) that the direct alignment of man, according to the layout of the great world, is when his face is turned toward the East. For this reason, the two eyes of man are placed in the forehead <note>original: frontispiece</note> of his frame—as they are in all other creatures—so that after a long nightly darkness, they might behold the rising Sun with delight. By its presence, they might adore its Creator, who has the power to banish the gloomy night with his golden gaze. This makes the sun a visible symbol of the eternal Sun’s invisible beauty. Furthermore, as the Scriptures have taught us, the eternal Sun will appear on the last day from that easterly point to renew and purify the corrupt world by fire.

It follows, therefore, that a man's right hand or right part must face the South, just as his left hand faces the North. All of this is even more obvious because it agrees and harmonizes with philosophical reasoning. Since the liver is on the right side of a man, it most conveniently sympathizes with the southern nature. The liver generates warm, airy blood through its power and sends it through the channels of the veins everywhere throughout the "human earth" (the body) to make it grow <note>original: vegetate</note>. This is just as the southern wind produces warm or moist <note>original: madid</note> showers to water the earth, so that the plants and herbs growing on it may increase through growth.

The left side, or left hand, is rightly compared to the world’s northern quarter, or the Arctic Pole. Just as in that region the air, water, or earth is cold and dry, prone to freezing <note>original: congelation</note>, and has a contracting and astringent <note>original: stiptick</note> nature, so we find that the spleen (which lies in the left part of a man's body) is the container for melancholy—or frozen, cold, black, sour, and earthly humors. And just as the northern blasts of the macrocosm <note>The Great World, or Universe</note> often obscure, mask, or eclipse the fair sunshine of the East, bringing a dark gloom over the whole hemisphere, so it is in the "little world" of man. The gaseous <note>original: flatuous</note> fumes sent out from this "northern" spleen contract the heart. Instead of the healthy and bright passions of joy, mirth, and gladness—which the beautiful sunshine of life provides—it brings forth dark passions such as sadness, fear, despair, and the like. It even causes the heart to suffer from fainting spells <note>original: syncopes</note> and palpitations. Thus, you see that the two opposite poles of the little world correspond in effect, and in all respects, with those of the great world, measuring the southern pole from the Equator <note>original: Æquinoctiall</note>. But when the natural fire is extinguished, it takes on the properties of darkness. Yet, I would not have wise men think that because a living body is turned into a dead carcass, it is therefore void of all spirits of life. # Mosaical Philosophy. Book 2.

The variety of his property in the four winds is sometimes in motion from the center of the thing in which it is toward the circumference. In this way, he vivifies <note>original: "vivifyeth"; gives life to</note> and causes the creature to act and live through a southern or equinoctial faculty. Thus, I say, it operates from the center of the celestial sun to animate inferior creatures—namely, by calling forth their incorruptible spirits (which were repelled by the winter or Boreal cold into their center) from their center to their circumference. This is apparent in plants, which for that reason seem as if they were dead all through the winter season; the spirit of life leaves and forsakes the circumference <note>the outer surface or branches</note> of the plant and retreats to the center to hide from the assaults of cold, which is its opposite, as far as it can. But when it perceives its fountain of light approaching to send it help, the plants begin little by little to spring again from their center to their circumference. Being united with the external beams that have come to their aid, they expel dark privation and congealing cold from their "tabernacles" <note>their physical structures</note> and proceed to operate and act toward growth and multiplication; we see this also in the corn that is buried in the earth. 

In the same way, and no otherwise, the loadstone's martial nature <note>original: "Martiall"; related to the planet Mars and iron</note>—being originally contracted into its center by a Saturnine spirit <note>original: "Saturnine"; related to the planet Saturn, associated with cold, lead, and contraction</note>—is agitated and stirred up. With similar joy, it sucks into itself the formal beams of the iron, from whose martial sulfurous spirit they originally sprang. 

And even so, the spirits of the dead body—being driven by mortifying cold from the circumference to the center and resting there at repose without any action—make the body and every part of it fixed and immovable. But when they are applied to the living circumference of their own species or kind, they spring forth immediately in their watery spirits toward the circumference (as if they were almost famished in the center). They rejoice to meet with their like in the living man, whose own spirit dilates itself and issues forth from the pores in a streaming manner to assist them. These spirits, being partly congealed in the center of the dead member, suck them in with a greedy appetite along with the spiritual mummy <term>spiritual mummy: a vital force or "balsam" believed by Paracelsian physicians to reside in the body and remain for a time after death</term>, which is their vehicle, toward their central dwelling to endow it with life as it was before and to recreate it with their presence. But the oily spiritual mummy, being full of bright spirits resting upon the surface of the living man and thickened by the cold and mortifying contact of the dead flesh or part of the carcass, is immediately congealed and may be reserved for a private use. 

How can we better confirm this than by the contractive, restrictive, or congealing power of the smoky outgrowth issuing from the salt contained in the dead man's bones? For by applying the *Uznea* <note>original: "Uznea"; a type of moss or lichen found on the skulls of those who died violently, used in sympathetic medicine to stop bleeding</note> or mass which grows on the dead man's bones to the eruptions of blood or hemorrhages in a living man, the warm blood (as if moved by an antipathetic <note>natural aversion</note> affection) returns back again and is denied passage by the congealing and binding operation of these Northern-affected outgrowths.

But leaving these conclusions regarding the dead man's magnet and its virtues for a while: what would you say if there were a *microcosmical loadstone* <note>original: "microcosmicall Magnes"; a magnet derived from the human "microcosm" or body</note> that could be selected and gathered from a living man without any harm or prejudice to his life? Its virtues are remarkable, both in regard to its monstrous and unnatural generation—being composed of unlike parents and compacted of two substances different in kind, just as a mule is: namely, of an earthly mercury and choleric, sulfurous human spirits. Furthermore, its manner of attracting the spiritual mummy out of the living man is extraordinary. Indeed, what is far more admirable is that by the transplantation of it to either animal or vegetable kinds, it works in a strange fashion, either sympathetically or antipathetically. 

I know that this news will immediately be judged by some—who are more likely to judge wrongly than to rightly examine a matter—to be diabolical. And why? Because it passes beyond the sphere of their capacities. And yet I know this to be true, and I know those who have put it into practice, not without the wonder of many. Yes, I know this microcosmical magnet and its use; when it is tried by wise men and well pondered by them, it will appear as natural as its effects seem strange and its reasoning abstruse. But if what I have said before is well understood and seriously pondered, the cause of this will not seem so hidden that it should exceed the limits of nature. Of this kind of magnetic action, both sympathetic and antipathetic, I purpose, by God's grace, to discourse more at length in the third and last book of this treatise.

### CHAP. V.

*In this Chapter is expressed the secret cause why, and the manner how, both the Microcosmic <note>Microcosmic: Relating to the "little world," or the human being as a reflection of the universe.</note> and Macrocosmic <note>Macrocosmic: Relating to the "great world," or the universe as a whole.</note> Loadstone <note>Loadstone: A natural magnet; here used metaphorically for the attractive spiritual forces in humans and the cosmos.</note> operate at a distance, and that unto an unknown dimension or unlimited interval.*

Mr. Foster has sufficiently expressed the shallowness of his philosophy where he asserts that because the light of the Sun and stars cannot penetrate thick clouds and opaque bodies, therefore the formal essence of a man is not able to pierce and penetrate directly in its course without being stopped or hindered by castles, hills, woods, and such things. But had he been a little more profoundly educated, or deeply immersed in the depths of true philosophy, he would have known that the ethereal seed <note>original: "sperm"; meaning the life-giving, creative essence or influence</note> or astral influences are of a far subtler condition than the vehicle of visible light. Indeed, they are so thin, so mobile, so penetrating, and so lively that they are able to—and do—continually penetrate even unto the center or inward bosom of the earth without any manifest obstacle or resistance. There, they generate metals of various kinds according to the condition of the influence, as the ancient philosophers confirm. 

The subtlety of this spirit, Plotinus (following Plato’s mind), fully expresses in these words: <note>original: "Tanta est Ætheris tenuitas ut omnia corpora penetret universi tam supera quam infera, & cum ipsis conjunctus aut implicitus, ea majora minime reddat, quia spiritus iste interior cuncta opera eorum mole minima nullum prorsus augmentum recipiente, alit atque conservat."</note> *The thinness of the Ether is such that it penetrates all the bodies of the world, as well above in heaven as below on earth; and this heavenly substance, being joined and mixed with them, does not make them a jot bigger, because this inward spirit nourishes and preserves all bodies without adding anything to their weight or increasing their substance.* 

And by reason of this heavenly nature's purity or subtlety, the heaven (or *Caelum*) is called by the wiser philosophers and mystical poets the "husband" to the earth, which they term *Vesta*. Indeed, the very stars of heaven—among which the Copernicans rank the earth—are likened to his wife, since they are extracted out of the ethereal substance just as Eve was out of the side of Adam. For they are defined to be the thickest portions of their orbs, by reason of which they are accounted as the members of heaven; consequently, there is nothing so thin, subtle, and piercing as that spirit from which they are derived by condensation. 

This is the cause why the true Alchemists tell such wonders of their *Caelum* <note>Caelum: Latin for "Heaven" or "the Sky."</note>, which they call their Quintessence <note>Quintessence: The "fifth element," a pure, incorruptible substance thought to make up the heavenly bodies.</note>, arguing that by reason of its purity and subtlety, it is able to penetrate all things. And the philosophers say that it is their nature, <margin>On the Art of Chemistry.</margin> which they define to be: <note>original: "Vis quædam rebus infinita, omnia permeans entia, cunctas generans res, easque augens alensque & ex similibus similia procreans."</note> *A certain infinite power in things, which penetrates and passes through all things, engendering every thing, and augmenting and nourishing them, and procreating like things from their like.* 

And truly, if you will be pleased to really consider what I have spoken before, you will remember how I told you that the angelic virtue proceeded from the archetypal emanations and are the types of the divine Idea. Again, you will recall that the ethereal spirit was filled with the angelic influences, which had their essential root from God. So in truth, it is not the starry light which penetrates so deeply or operates so universally, but that eternal central spirit, with which His divine and irresistible essence penetrates all things, both in heaven above and in the earth and waters beneath. 

All this the mystical philosophers seemed to verify, though darkly, when they called Saturn (who was the father of Jupiter, or the head of the universal emanation) the "father of Heaven," arguing thereby that in the emission of the spirit of wisdom, He produced, created, or informed the heavens. This is according to the words of Job: <margin>Job.</margin> *You adorned the heavens by your Spirit* <note>original: "Cœlum ornasti Spiritu tuo"</note>. And David: <margin>Psalm.</margin> *By the word of the Lord the heavens were made, and by his Spirit every virtue thereof* <note>original: "Verbo Domini firmati sunt cœli & Spiritu ab ore ejus omnis virtus eorum"</note>. And St. Peter: <margin>2 Peter 3.</margin> *The heavens were first, and the earth of water, and by the waters, existing by the word of God* <note>original: "Cœli erant prius & terra ex aquis, & per aquas existentes verbo Dei"</note>. It is certain, therefore, that the whole essential act of the ethereal spirit is the divine emanation, or the bright incorruptible Spirit of the Lord; and therefore, by necessity, that spirit which is worthy to be the

For that reason, the world was called "natured nature" <note>original: "Natura naturata"; the physical world as a product of God's active nature.</note>, or the nature which was made "natural"—specifically by the presence of the Naturing Nature or Spirit of the Lord, which moved upon the waters and shared its fiery, informing vigor or essence with them. We must therefore, after duly considering what has been said, infer that if this influence is completely animated by the incorruptible Spirit of the Lord, then it must be endowed with the properties of that Spirit or Divine Nature. Consequently, it must be the most subtle, quick, movable, and penetrating of all spirits. In that respect, it will be able to pass through all solid bodies without resistance, and also to engender, increase, and nourish all things. Once it is incorporated or made specific to a creature, it procreates similar individuals from their own kind. Furthermore, in terms of our human capacity, it has an infinite extension and therefore cannot be limited. 

I intend to demonstrate all of this through experience or visual proof in the following manner: We find in practice that the loadstone <note>Loadstone: A naturally occurring magnet.</note>, by virtue of the subtle spirit that internally animates it, becomes so powerful in its attractive virtue that it can display and transmit the beams of its active power right across the hardest stones, the most solid and fine-grained wood, and through thick plates of copper, tin, silver, or gold. Yes, it even penetrates through impenetrable glass itself and other such compacted materials that have no visible pores or breathing holes <note>original: "spiracle"</note>. This is an evident argument that this spirit is of a far more piercing and subtle nature than the earthly air <note>original: "sublunary aire"</note>, since air is denied passage even through the thinnest paper, skin, or bladder. 

In the same way, man's inward or celestial spirit—which is the vehicle for this life-giving beam—is so subtle in itself that nothing is able to resist it when the inward mental beam aims at any mark, no matter how far away or inaccessible it may seem to a person thinking only of the flesh. Because this celestial or ethereal spirit in man is made after the pattern of the Divine Image which it bears, it must also resemble that Image in its actions. Now, the subtlety of the Divine act in

Section 2. Mosaical Philosophy.

We see that every astral influence <term>astral influence: the belief that stars emit a spiritual or physical power that affects earthly life</term> in a creature does, by a natural inclination and through sympathy, gaze toward the star or celestial fountain from which it sprang. Likewise, that star in heaven, with a paternal respect, sends down its influences to feed and nourish its corresponding "filial fire" or form in the creature here below. Both of them, through a mutual relationship, rejoice together at the spiritual presence of each other. Whereupon it is said: "Nature rejoices in nature, and contains nature; O nature of celestial truth, which by the Will of God multiplies natures" <note>original: "Natura natura letatur & naturam continet; O natura cœlestis veritatis, naturas Dei nutu multiplicans"</note>.

In the same way, each kind or species that is endowed with the same influence does, because of its likeness to another, send forth beams of one nature by a sympathetic consent. This creates a harmonious symphony in the meeting of their beams, by which they agree in a union of love. For this reason, the axiom of the philosophers mentioned before runs in this strain: "Nature is accustomed to procreate like from like" <note>original: "Natura ex similibus similia procreare solet"</note>. This is the cause why each specific form rejoices in its like and is ready to produce its own kind, and does not usually pass the limits of its kind. For example: a man's nature produces a man, a horse a horse, a fennel seed fennel, a bean a bean, wheat produces wheat, and so on.

Also, the nature of each thing created in this way is most attractive to the nature of its like. It sends forth the amiable and sympathetic beams of its affection to meet with similar beams emitted from its like; so that both of them easily consent and rejoice in each other, and by the joining of these beams, they endeavor to cause a union. For this reason, the lodestone <term>lodestone: a naturally magnetized piece of the mineral magnetite</term> rejoices at the sight of its like. If one lodestone meets with another, each will gaze at the other through their Saturnine, sulfurous spirits and embrace each other. By their application, they will centrally suck and draw one to the other with a sympathetic embracing.

Also, because iron is subject to the very same constellation and has its central star in all points corresponding to the lodestone (for which essential "blood-relationship" they are both found in the same terrestrial vein), they are both observed to entertain and hug one another so lovingly. Experience tells us that the "feminine" lodestone embraces the "masculine" iron like a lustful lover <note>original: "luxurious harlot"</note>—and it is the lodestone that draws, not the iron that moves to the lodestone, as **Averroes**, **Scaliger**, and **Cardinal Cusanus** have erroneously suspected. They claimed that the iron moves to the lodestone as if to its beginning or the womb from which it came. If that were true, the North Pole in the iron would, of its own accord, move more swiftly toward the Pole Star (which is the fountain of both their central influences) than the magnet would; yet experience proves the opposite is true.

Now, to confirm the infinite extension of these central beams between two similar bodies, let us first understand some theory so that we may better move toward practice.
<margin>Al-Kindi, *On Stellar Rays*</margin>
"The beam," says **Al-Kindi**, "which proceeds from the center of the star to the center of the earth, is proved to be strongest in its specific operation" <note>original: "Radius quia centro stellæ ad centrum terræ procedit fortissimus esse probatur in operationis suæ specie"</note>. By this, he signifies at what an immeasurable distance the hidden starry beam, or beamy influence, works with and in its image on the earth. For he says elsewhere: "It is manifest that the starry beams make and engender various individual creatures in this world" <note>original: "Liquet quod Radii stellares diversa constituunt individua in hoc mundo"</note>.

Again, regarding the central stars (or starry influences) of lower bodies and the extension of their beams, he speaks thus: "The elementary world <term>elementary world: the physical world composed of the four elements (earth, water, air, fire)</term> is the image or pattern of the starry world, so that everything it contains includes the form or likeness of the starry world. It is evident that everything in this world emits its beams in its own manner, just as the stars of heaven do; otherwise, it would not fully take on the figure of the starry world. Indeed, this is made manifest to the senses in some things: for fire sends forth the beams of its heat to nearby places, and the earth sends the emanations of its cold" <note>original: "Mundus Elementarius est exemplum mundi Syderei... ignis enim radios caloris ad loca proxima transmittit, & terra radios algoris"</note>. We affirm, therefore, as true, and say that everything which has actual existence in the world of elements emits beams in every direction, which fill the entire elementary world in their own way. Furthermore, the distance of one thing from another makes a difference in the effect of those beams on the things of this world.

And again, that just as the mentioned star in heaven darts forth its beams even to the very center of the earth—and therefore has so large a sphere of activity <term>sphere of activity: the area or range within which a force or influence is effective</term> that it searches every place of the vaulted world—even so, and in the same manner, those starry sparks <note>original: "scintillis"</note>, or radiant sparks, which it sends down into its subject creature (being of the same essence as its fountain, and therefore continuous and indivisible with it) likewise search every angle or corner of the sublunary <term>sublunary: the region "below the moon," meaning the Earth and its atmosphere, which were thought to be subject to change and decay</term> region. Indeed, it penetrates even to the very celestial fountain from which it is derived, as shall be more clearly demonstrated hereafter; for every portion or small part of a large loadstone <term>loadstone: a naturally magnetized mineral (magnetite) used as a compass</term> has its poles and circles, just like the whole.

It is therefore made apparent by this that the action of each elementary thing is carried out just as well by the separation of their bodies—that is to say, at a distance <note>original: "ad distans"</note>—as when they are joined together by mutual contact. However, the action of elementary things when they are separated from one another is performed by a fitting application and infusion of their radiant influences into each other. This would hardly be believed because the action is so hidden <term>occultness: the quality of being hidden or secret; referring to natural forces like magnetism that cannot be seen with the eye</term>, if experience did not guide us through the observation of the loadstone's attraction of iron to itself at a distance. 

We also observe that the images of things are seen from far away in mirrors or optical glasses. It was no small trick of the Pythagoreans <term>Pythagoreans: followers of the ancient Greek philosopher Pythagoras, who believed in the mathematical and musical harmony of the universe</term> and some other of our Christian philosophers to communicate their thoughts to friends in far countries by reflection made through prepared mathematical glasses <note>likely referring to mirrors or lenses used for signaling or optical experiments</note> within the circle or compass of the moon.

They ascribe bounds to the action of this mystical nature as they please, or according to what their external senses observe. For example, because the loadstone draws the iron only from half the distance of a table, therefore <note>original: "Ergo"</note> they think and conclude that the life-giving act of its power penetrates or extends no further than that distance in the air. Consequently, being led by their physical eyesight, they limit the loadstone’s spiritual extension according to this external and visible action. 

But if they would properly close their physical eyes during this inquiry and look—as true philosophers ought when searching for such a hidden action—with the vision of their mental intellect, they would find that the extension of the radiant spirit in the loadstone is equal to that of its own celestial star, since they are both of one essence. The same is true for the spirit in the iron; every spark <note>original: "scintill"</note> or spark of fire has the properties of the whole, as was said of the loadstone. However, there are many things that may hinder the visible effect in the loadstone—namely, the heaviness <note>original: "ponderosity"</note> of the iron's body, which prevents the stone from drawing it beyond the circle of its noticeable emanation. A similar antipathy is noted between the natures of the *Catoblepas* <note>original: "Catablepa," a legendary Ethiopian animal said to kill with its gaze.</note> and the weasel, for weasels are like poison to them. <margin>Ibid, 12.</margin> The cock has an antipathetic abhorrence for the fox. Again, *Dioscorides* <note>Ancient Greek physician and botanist.</note> reports that the <margin>Dioscorides.</margin> yew tree <note>original: *Taxus*</note> is so venomous that if anyone even sits under it, he is harmed by it, and it often costs him his life. And *Caelius Rhodiginus* says that the adder is afraid of a naked man. It is well known and confirmed by many authors that the *Catoblepas*, being a very <margin>Caelius Rhodiginus, Book 15, chapter 25.</margin> small animal, kills with the beam of his gaze <note>original: "aspect"</note> from a thousand paces away. Also, one blear-eyed person is able to infect another from afar by the secret emission of his contagious beams. We see that onions draw tears from a person at a distance <note>original: *ad distans*</note> by the emission of their beams. Again, we observe that just as a healthy and sound person commonly embraces his like through a sympathetic affection, so also a corrupted person, through antipathy and from a distance <note>original: *ad distans*</note>, poisons and infects those like him. But to return again to our magnetic focus, which is as much spiritual as physical: I say there is such a spiritual relationship of sympathy between creature and creature that the beloved allures and draws toward it the spirit of the lover in an admirable manner of attraction. I have seen this marvelously demonstrated by a water spaniel of my own in *France*. For as I rode post <note>traveling quickly using a relay of horses</note> to *Lyons*, and on the way had lost my valise or mail-bag <note>original: "male"</note> in which my letters of exchange were, I sought to return back again; however, I found my post-horse was of such a temperament that he would by no means turn and go back. Then I was forced to send my dog back to look for it. After he had been absent half an hour, he brought the pouch <note>original: "bouget"</note> in his mouth. This is strange, considering that I was on horseback and that he could not discern any footprints of mine; nevertheless, he came to the bag I desired, and finding my scent on it, he brought it back. 

But to come more pertinently to the business: a friend of mine in my company lost his dog at night. We came into a private house where the dog had never been before; while we were in a room with the door fastened, about half an hour later the dog arrived and violently scraped and bounced at the door to find his beloved master. By this it is evident that the beams of his affection did not forsake his master’s beams during the master's absence; these beams guided him so directly to the unknown place that he found him. Is it not also a wonderful sympathetic emanation that the pigeon called the "Carrier" makes toward the place or dovecote where he was bred and fostered? For that reason, the bird so dearly affects and loves that place that though he is conveyed 500 miles from his nursery in an enclosed basket, yet he will fly directly back again with a letter about his neck. This is an evident argument that the bird is justly and straightly guided by the emitted beam of his affection, which is continued in a spiritual manner with the place he most delights in. Indeed, as we see from experience, there is a great **antipathy** between the contracted spirit of a slain body and the murderer. The living spirit of the dead, having been contracted into its center by cold after death, moves again from the center to the surface <note>original: "circumference"</note> through an angry, antipathetic passion, as if to resist its deadly enemy. This causes the congealed blood to flow and move, as if it would meet and assault the murderer’s own emitted spirit once more. 

Therefore, we must certainly confess that where one spirit joins in sympathy with another of the same nature, the power must be greater and the action performed over a larger distance. This is clearly shown in the secret operation of the **magnetic cure**, which takes effect between the weapon or ointment and the wounded person. I have spoken much of this in the heated encounter between **Mr. Foster** <note>William Foster (1591–1643), an English clergyman who published a famous attack on the weapon-salve titled "Hoplocrisma-Spongus," claiming the cure was magical or diabolical.</note> and myself, in the book where I was provoked to "squeeze his sponge" <note>Referring to Fludd's 1631 response, "The Squeezing of Foster's Sponge," where he defended the practice as natural philosophy.</note>. The argument of Mr. Foster rests on the supposed impossibility of a healing virtue operating at such a large distance as is claimed for the ointment—or rather, the impossibility of the living blood's "exciting spiritual beams" or influences flowing out toward the dead or congealed blood. If such an impossibility were true in the animal kingdom (which is the most expansive and least restricted by physical bonds), I wonder why it would not be far more impossible and unfeasible in mineral bodies. Because minerals are firm and solid, they are more likely to hold onto their influential beams than bodies that are loose and porous. Furthermore, the animal body is hot and fiery, and therefore more ready to expand and send its virtue further; the mineral, however, is cold and thus less active and powerful in projecting its beams. 

Yet despite this, experience teaches us that the **loadstone** looks toward the North Star, sending out its spiritual gaze toward it. Likewise, the star sends its beams to its northern mineral target from an immeasurable distance. Since this is so, why (I ask you) should the "animal star"—derived from its heavenly fountain—not also send its beams to the frozen and cold blood held in that "oily earth" (by which I mean the weapon-salve), or to the blood's invisible spirit drawn into the iron by its attractive, sulfurous nature? 

Experience teaches us that even if no physical blood is found on the iron, the wound is cured by a similar sympathetic gaze if the part of the weapon that caused the wound is anointed. Country surgeons <note>original: "Chirurgions"</note> have tested this: when they did not dare to probe the wound, they found by experience—namely, by putting the weapon into the fire—that the specific part of the sword or weapon that caused the wound would reveal itself by changing color, unlike the rest of the blade. In this way, they could see how deep the wound was by observing which part of the weapon had penetrated. 

This is a clear argument for the entry of bloody spirits into the weapon. Consequently, it proves that there are essential spirits that emanate or issue forth from the blood, leaving the body entirely. This also demonstrates, contrary to Mr. Foster, that if the thicker spirits of the blood can pierce close-grained steel, then its finer and more subtle spirits can penetrate all other things like an influential force without any resistance. But let us approach our purpose more closely and move our argument from mineral demonstrations to those of the plant kingdom <note>original: "vegetable"</note>, so that we may compare like with like in our animal subject. 

I will therefore focus on a grain of wheat. Though it is dead and rotted in the earth, it is **awakened** <note>original: "suscitated"</note> by the beaming influences of the sun. For "like draws like" by a magnetic power, and like rejoices in its like. One thing is awakened, revived, quickened, or called out from its rest or center by its own "alluring" or embracing "like." By this means, the beaming spark or atom of solar influence within the grain—which sits idle and does nothing in its center—is stirred up by its external "like" (the sun) to act and work toward its own delivery out of the elemental mire or the slimy bond...

...me to send her urine <note>original: "water"</note> once more; and he told me that a lady had been with him on behalf of the aforementioned noble patient the day before. In this regard, we compare the mixture of urine, ashes, and saffron used in this cure to the weapon-salve used for healing wounds. The awakening <note>original: "exfuscitating"</note> of the congealed spirit in the salt of the urine is like the reviving and stirring <note>original: "exagitating"</note> of the spirit in the dead blood, or the blood sucked up by the porous substance of the weapon. What shall we say about the wonderful effects seen in the transplantation of the blood's spirits from humans into other animals or plants? Truly, those well-versed in the mysteries of natural, microcosmic (relating to the human body), and macrocosmic (relating to the universe) magic know that the spiritual Mummy <margin>#</margin>—the seat of which is in the microcosmic blood—may be sucked or drawn out of a person's body by a <term>magnet <note>original: "Magnes"</note></term> extracted from the same subject and transplanted into a beast, tree, or herb. Additionally, *Johannes Rumelius Pharamundus* <note>a 17th-century physician and writer on hermetic medicine</note> claims that he has cured several people of the gout. He did this by cutting off the hair from their feet and thighs and paring their nails, then thrusting them into a hole bored into the very heartwood <note>original: "pith"</note> of an oak tree. He would then close or ram the hole shut with a peg or pin made from the same tree, afterward sealing and covering it with cow dung. Then, he says, if the gout does not return within three months, the oak tree will be strong enough to magnetically draw the disease to itself. However, if the gout returns within three months, it indicates that the oak's magnetic power is insufficient. 

Therefore, he proceeds in this manner: he bores a hole in another oak as before, but keeps the pieces of wood that came out during the boring. He bruises these pieces and stitches them into a bag, applying them to the painful limb; he does this exactly three days before the new moon. Then, at the very hour of the new moon, he removes the bag, takes out the bruised wood, puts it back into the hole in the tree, and rams it in with a peg or pin from the same oak. If, despite all this, the gout is felt within three months, he then cuts off the hair and nails of the feet, ties them to the back of a crab, and throws it into running water, and the person with gout will be cured. 

This Doctor of Medicine claims in a book he published in German that he has cured many people using the first experiment, many others by using the first and second together, and finally, many desperate cases by using the first, second, and third. He says that this method of cure is usually certain for cases of gout caused by "sulfurous" factors; however, it often fails for those cases arising from a "mercurial" or salty nature <note>Paracelsian medical theory categorized diseases based on the balance of the "Three Primes": Sulfur, Mercury, and Salt</note>. Therefore, leaving this magnetic method of cure, he turns toward a more external...

I described how, when it is placed in plantain water, the plant closes itself; and if a portion of that water is drunk by a woman in labor <note>original: "Travell"</note>, even if the herb in the water is moved to another house, the flower or herb will gradually open itself at the exact moment the woman is giving birth, just as her womb opens. This is a clear argument that the beams emitted from these two things sympathize with one another. 

In conclusion, it is most evident that since the spiritual astral <note>original: "Astralicall"</note> virtues in every inferior creature descend from the celestial stars and are of one continuous nature with them—just as the sunbeams here below are not divided or separated from their source of light—it follows that they emit their beaming influences toward one another, just as the stars do in heaven from which they are animated. So, if two stars in heaven are "friends," they both sympathize with each other in the flow of their emanations; but if they are "enemies" in heaven, they will avoid <note>original: "antipathize and decline from"</note> one another when their beams meet. Regarding the distance they maintain in their mutual actions, we must imagine it extends as far as their beams are able to reach one another. 

And I want those men who only deal with physical <note>original: "sensible"</note> affairs to know that the actions of these creatures through their "aspect" toward one another operate secretly <note>original: "occultly"</note>, even though the effect does not always manifest itself to our senses. However, they should also understand that the closer the natural affinity between the stars in heaven—and consequently the things below that are subject to those spirits—the more powerful the sympathetic effects will prove. This is because their beams will meet directly, without any swerving or deviation.

### CHAP. VI.

->*That the devil does make use of natural things to carry out his strategies among men, without which he can achieve nothing truly, but only through illusions <note>original: "prestigiously"</note> or delusions; and whether those natural things are therefore "cacomagical" <note>relating to evil magic, from the Greek "kakos" for evil</note> and should be avoided by mankind simply because their secret effects sometimes align with the will of the devil.*<-

<margin>Psalm 121:5</margin>
We read in many places in Scripture that the devil makes use of God’s creatures to bring about his secret devices and strategies against mankind. For example, to impoverish and ruin the fortune of the patient Job, Satan used the winds and called down (as the Text says) the fire of God from heaven to consume his cattle. God forbid that for this reason we should consider these creatures of God to be "cacomagical" or diabolical, just because God allowed them to act to fulfill the devil’s will. God also made him a "Prince of the Air," giving him the power to stir up tempests in the seas and storms in the atmospheric heavens <note>original: "elementary heavens"</note>; for this reason, the air is called by some "The Synagogue of Satan." 

What! Must we therefore abhor the air and winds because the devil sometimes performs his mischievous feats through them? In truth, as Aristotle rightly said, the air is cleared and purified from all corruption by the movement of the winds; for if it were not stirred and moved by the winds, it would rot, just as stagnant water does. Furthermore, if we were to flee from and loathe the air, how could we live, since the airy spirit is the spiritual food of our life? 

We also read in the Scriptures that God causes the Sun and Moon to rise indifferently upon both the good and the bad, and that the Sun and Moon harm or hurt some while being comforting and favorable to others. Therefore David says, *The sun shall not harm you by day, nor the moon by night.* <margin>Psalm 121:5</margin> The Moon, called *Hecate* <note>a Greek goddess associated with magic, the night, and the underworld</note> by the poets, is the goddess of witches, for it was to her that the famous enchantress Medea made her prayers <note>original: "orisons"</note> to further her purposes. And yet the air, water, and earth are seasoned with her moist <note>original: "humid or madid"</note> virtues, and plants, and even animals, acknowledge her as the patroness of growth <note>original: "vegetation"</note>. She makes the seas swell, and then, by a different position or "aspect," the seas are lowered in their pride, and fluids <note>original: "humours"</note> become scarcer in every living or growing thing. Indeed, we find that all malignant watery spirits are subject to her influences...

### Sect. 2. Mosaic Philosophy.

For he is a seasoned veteran <note>original: "old beaten Souldier"</note> in astrology and knows the effects of every heavenly arrangement. Therefore, he can take advantage of their strongest influences upon animal, vegetable, or mineral creatures that are subject to them. He knows the proper times when these influences are poured down upon them and is an expert in their virtues. These virtues are only at their peak of effectiveness and power when the influential point of their specific constellation strikes them, stirring up their central spirits to reveal the full extent of their hidden <note>original: "occult or arcane"</note> natures and conditions. 

At that very moment, he collects the herb or stone, or uses the animal's parts <note>original: "members"</note>, or teaches sorcerers to do so without them knowing the mystery of how the constellation's alignment or timing connects with the natural creatures being gathered. Consequently, when they try to use those same medicinal plants <note>original: "Simples"</note> at another time, they find them weak and ineffective because the spirits of every herb, animal, or mineral are weakest when the star—which is their nursing celestial mother—has the least power or dominion in heaven. 

The true astrological philosopher knows by experience that all of this is true. By gathering a medicinal plant <note>original: "Simple"</note> at the moment when its governing constellation—whether fixed or wandering—is at its highest dignity and power in the heavens, he finds a wonderful effectiveness in it, in both its hidden and obvious properties. Conversely, if it is collected at a time when its heavenly patron is weak and feeble, its powers will appear faint and almost dead. 

This makes it very clear that it is the natural creatures themselves—acting through their own essential natures—that produce these sympathetic or antipathetic effects. The devil simply uses these natural effects to carry out his schemes, just as a physician, philosopher, or natural magician does to achieve their own goals. 

What should we say then? That anyone who uses or works with these same creatures—be they animals, vegetables, or minerals—is an evil magician <note>original: "Caco-magician"; from the Greek "kakos" meaning evil</note> and their work is diabolical just because the devil sometimes uses their subtle and hidden <note>original: "abstruse"</note> actions to make a name for himself among fools? Is it not God who works such effects in these, His creatures? Did He not, by His Word, bestow such virtues on them at their creation and continue them through the generations? 

Why, then, is it not just as possible for Man, who is framed after God’s image, to know the true time for collecting these creatures and their uses and virtues, as it is for the devil? Is it because, forsooth, since the fall of **Adam**, man is blinded with ignorance and cannot distinguish light from darkness? We can gather from Scripture that **Adam** knew the virtues of the stars and of every specific earthly creature subject to them. Otherwise, he could not have assigned a proper name to each one that agreed with its nature. 

But if the descendants of **Adam** are blind and cannot distinguish colors, and are therefore also ignorant of these hidden treasures of God, how, I ask you, did the devil gain such deep insight into them? After all, he fell much further than man did because of his rebellion and is clouded by a darker veil, which is why he is called the "Prince of Darkness." 

Oh, you might reply that the devil is a spirit without a body and is therefore able to discern the hidden things of God in nature sooner and better than man, who is a coarse, physical creature. And again, you might say that man dies in every age, but the devil has great experience due to his long existence. 

I answer: even though man dies and does not live long, and even though his understanding is clouded because of his forefathers' fall, and though he is clothed in a dark and cumbersome body—he still has the revelation of the Truth. He possesses a discovery of the hidden mysteries of natural things, first given by God and passed down to him through succession—that is, by a mystical <note>original: "Cabalisticall"</note> tradition from our forefather **Adam**—and by the revelation of God’s Wisdom, or the Holy Spirit, which He has bestowed upon the Elect.

Because he has the knowledge to choose every **medicinal plant** <note>original: "Simple"—an herb used on its own for medicine</note> when it is at its full force and season by observing the connection between the stars and the plants, must man be forbidden from sharing in their natural virtues or becoming skilled in collecting them without it being considered the help and revelation of the devil?
