That would be like saying God created things only for the devil’s use, rather than to serve man in every necessity according to his free will—especially since it is said that He gave man power and made him lord over all His creatures. Even if an animal, plant, or mineral medicine causes harm and proves poisonous in some cases, it proves life-saving <note>original: "salutary"</note> in others. There is no wind so bad that it does not blow someone some good.

The **Colloquintida** <note>bitter apple, a powerful purgative</note>, **Scamony**, **Euphorbium**, **Squirting Cucumber** <note>original: "Cucumer asininus"</note>, **Spurge** <note>original: "Titimall"</note>, **Bear’s-foot**, **Spearwort** <note>original: "Flammula"</note>, **Garlic**, and similar things in the vegetable kingdom prove poisonous in some respects, and yet they may be applied in a healthy way to the human body. Also, **Arsenic**, **Orpiment** <note>a yellow arsenic ore</note>, **Antimony**, **Mercury** <note>original: "Quick-silver"</note>, and similar substances in the mineral realm kill when applied maliciously and without proper refinement. The **Toad**, the **Viper** or **Adder**, the **Spider**, the **Scorpion**, the **Spanish Fly** <note>original: "Cantharides"</note>, and similar creatures in the animal region are deadly poisons to mankind; and yet they may be so prepared that they prove to be wholesome medicines and become antidotes <note>original: "counter-poysons"</note>.

But besides all this, just as there is nothing in the world that works more effectively through **Sympathy** and according to nature than one healthy and sound nature does with another, so truly is there nothing that operates more **Antipathetically** <note>through natural opposition or repulsion</note>—contrary to nature or destructively—than when the corruption of a poisoned or infected spirit interacts with a healthy spirit of the same **species**. The reason is that the infected spirit craves and desires, through an earnest exchange of its "beams" <note>radiations of vital spirit</note>, to receive help and relief in its distress from healthy spirits, seeking out their light for relief. We see this during a time of contagion <note>the plague</note>: the spirit emanating from the infected person greedily attaches its infected beams to the emanating spirit of a healthy person of the same kind. Through this connection, the fiery venom of the one poisons and contaminates <note>original: "co-inquinateth"</note> the healthy nature of the other, and this only happens within its specific kind. For commonly the plague that affects humans does not stick to the spirit of beasts, such as sheep and the like. In the same way, the **murrain** <note>an infectious disease in cattle</note> in beasts does not infect the human spirit; a similar specific nature is always most ready to embrace and connect its beams with its own kind. For this reason, it is evident that just as a spiritual **Mummy** <note>the vital life force or essence of a person</note> can be obtained from a healthy man—which is wonderfully healthful and life-giving to mankind, so much so that for its universal applications it may be considered a **Panacea** or universal medicine to preserve health;

So also, through a strange corruption of a man's spiritual **Mummy**, a venom can be drawn out of him, more destructive or malignant to mankind than anything else found in the world.

There was also a certain hermit who lived not far from Aix in Provence—the story is still fresh in the mouths of everyone there—who infected the whole City with a similar filter <note>original: "philtre"—a medicinal or magical potion</note>. Others, like leprosy, epilepsy, and the "French-Pox" <note>original: "French-Pox"—syphilis</note>, infect by immediate contact. We find that what was created wholesome and healthy in man has become contaminating and venomous through disorder. 

What, therefore, shall I say? Must we conclude that we must abandon our own nature because it can be made infectious and deadly to us? No! At her arraignment <note>original: "arreignment"; a legal trial</note>, she confessed that by the property of a stone which was taken from her, she could discover anything. Specifically, if a thing were true, the stone would sweat, and if it were false, it would not sweat; it would also reveal other things to her by changing colors. And again, when they desired to see some demonstrations from her, she said that if they would let her have her stone, she would show them some. But they, fearing that she would escape by that means, dared not let her have it, and instead burned her at **Queensferry** <note>original: "Queens Ferry"</note> in **Scotland**. 

Some are instructed by him <note>Referring to the devil or a demonic tutor</note> to take a metal and prepare it under its proper constellation, and to engrave on it the characters of the star and the angels belonging to it at a time when the star is most potent in heaven and well-aligned with other planets. They then find these plates to have a strange effect in many magical operations. What then? Just because the devil knows the virtue and properties of these natural things and can instruct his ministers in the evil use of them, does it follow that **Adam**, **Solomon**, the wise **Magicians** of the East, and many other good and godly persons do not also know their virtues, their proper times for collection, and their manner of application for good? 

What if they see a just cause to use them in an opposite way, yet still without overstepping the bounds of natural and lawful magic? The true subject of such magic is the Spirit of Wisdom, which is the basis or foundation of true Natural Philosophy. What do we make of the means **Moses** used when he brought the plague of boils <note>original: "the botch"</note> over all **Egypt** by dispersing ashes? Some will say that this was done supernaturally; let them but look into the hidden secrets in the nature of other animals, vegetables, and minerals, and they shall find mysteries as great as these contained naturally within them, setting aside all suspicion of dealing with the devil. 

Was the reverend father **Albertus Magnus** a <term>Cacomagician</term> <note>original: "Cacomagician"; from the Greek "kakos," meaning an evil magician or sorcerer</note> because he describes the abstruse, hidden, and mystical virtues of animals, plants, and stones? The same was done by **Hermes**, **Plato**, and many other profound philosophers. Or must these be the pupils of the devil because they know the times and hours for gathering materials and the manner of their preparation, even though they kept those secrets to themselves? No, truly, for they received this knowledge from tradition—namely, from mystical and profound philosophers or natural wise men, such as **Solomon**, **Hermes**, and the wise men called **Magi** (the natural magicians of the East) who revealed these secrets to those who were worthy, passing them down from one age to another.

<margin>Invisibility</margin>
Was it not a wondrous property in **Gyges’s** ring that it could make him walk invisible by its natural power? And yet, the "blind buzzards" of our age—such as **Mr. Foster** <note>William Foster was a parson who famously attacked Robert Fludd’s theories on the "weapon-salve," accusing him of witchcraft</note> and his accomplices—insist that all these miraculous effects in creatures proceed from the devil. In doing so, they deprive the Omnipotent Spirit of God and His Nature of their rightful credit. This is despite **Solomon** plainly confessing that all knowledge of the secret times for choosing materials, the mystical natures of the stars, and the hidden virtues and properties of man, beasts, plants, roots, and all other things (known or unknown) proceeds from the Spirit of God. Therefore, he concludes with these words: *For wisdom, the worker of all things, taught me* <note>original Latin: "Omnium enim opifex me docuit Sapientia"; from the biblical Book of Wisdom 7:22</note>. 

In these words, he implies two things: first, that the Spirit of Wisdom teaches and reveals to man the hidden mysteries of Natural Philosophy, which consists of the discovery of natural virtues both in the heavens and on earth. Second, that it is the same Spirit that created those virtues in every specific thing—namely, in the stars above, and in the animal, vegetable, and mineral kingdoms below. 

This being the case, what can the devil do (being only a created being with reason, just like man) to create these essential virtues by which he performs his feats, any more than a man can? Why should we attribute to him what rightly belongs to the all-creating and acting Spirit within the creature? If a person wishes, they may attribute the *wickedness* of the action to the devil, who instigates man to evil and teaches him the means to carry out his bad intentions. That, truly, belongs to the devil. For he was created to be a destroyer, as the prophet **Isaiah** <note>original: "Isaias"</note> testifies to us; and to achieve this, he makes use of God’s natural creatures. 

<margin>Job 1.</margin>
For instance, he used "the fire of God from heaven" to destroy **Job’s** cattle, and he used the corrupt air to kill the Israelites with the plague <margin>2 Samuel 24</margin> because of **David’s** sins. It has never been observed that he could do anything against man on his own, except through temptation. Rather, he operates to destroy or cause sickness by using natural, "antipathizing" <note>Antipathy refers to a natural repulsion or destructive relationship between two substances or spirits</note> means that God created for a more direct use. However, for some of his sorcerous students, he is also pleased to show and reveal a counter-poison, which they may use by a stronger, sympathetic...

<margin>Nicolas Rémy, *Daemonolatreiae*, Book 1 <note>original: "Nichol. Pennigius Demonolo. lib. I." They said that the black powder kills when strewed on food, rubbed on the body, or sprinkled on clothing; the ash-colored or reddish powder causes diseases; but the white powder cured those diseases. 

And *Odella Boncuriana* <note>Odilla Boncourt</note>, being arraigned on January 18, 1586, said that it was the manner of the witches of her faction to strew a poisoned powder in the path of those they wished to harm. *Francis Perine* confessed on November 4, 1588, that the devil gave her an herb to be laid in the path of *Riberiannus* (who had beaten her for stealing some of his pears); this caused him to suddenly fall sick. *Francis Follers*, *Marget Warny*, and *Jacobit Equine* confessed on January 15, 1584, that they had ointments with which they anointed rods and whips. If they touched someone’s garments with these, that person died not long after. They also said that if they anointed their own hands with this magical ointment, merely touching someone’s clothes would cause them to die within a short time. 

Thus you see how the devil cannot work except through natural poisons. Nothing proceeds merely from himself except for deceptive appearances <note>original: "prestigious apparitions"; here meaning illusions or tricks of sight</note>—namely those things which seem real but are actually no more substantial than a painted image is compared to a living person.

Because of this, they warn operators to beware of its fumes. However, when it appears in the heating process <term>decoction</term> between white and black, it leaves the patient in a state between death and health—that is, a sickly constitution. The white stage, which signifies the perfection of maturity, causes health, cures infirmities, and prevents the harm that the black and ash-colored stages bring. 

So you see, the devil can do no more by himself than a man is able to do. Furthermore, regarding the strewing of destroying powder, the same thing was carried out by man's own wicked invention in **Milan** in the year 1629. As for the ointment which kills by immediate contact, "the Jew" and "the Cardinal" <note>likely a reference to a contemporary scandal or historical anecdote involving poisoning</note> knew that wicked craft—namely, how to abuse God's creatures just as well as the devil. Whomever the ointment touched, it killed. Again, the Hermit achieved the same result by anointing door hammers, and he had his own antidote <term>Alexipharmacon</term> or counter-poison for it, just as the devil does. 

You may see, then, that a wicked-minded man who abuses God's good creatures—altering them from the true purpose for which God created them for the benefit of mankind—may be rightly ranked with the devil. He may justly be termed a "devil incarnate," in that he can achieve many devilish ways to destroy without the devil's help, just as effectively as the devil can without flesh and bones. 

I conclude, therefore, that it is a great absurdity—indeed, a gross foolishness or madness in ignorant men—to so lightly judge and censure the hidden great works <term>Magnalia</term> or occult mysteries of God in nature. It is wrong to claim they are inventions of the devil, even when their effects are bad, and much less when they are good and healing <note>original: "salutiferous"</note>, such as the **Weapon-salve**. It is commonly known to God and all truly understanding men that it is the animal, vegetable, or mineral creature that produces the effect—one by abuse, and the other by its true property and virtue (that is, the use for which it was created by God). For God created all creatures good, and consequently for a good use; it is the malice of the devil that diverts them from their true use. But death entered into the world by the envy and malice of the devil, etc. For know this, that before the fall of **Adam**, all things were strictly and rightly understood <note>original: "taken"</note>, and consequently not mistaken. But after he had tasted of the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil, his physical eyes were opened, and the creatures were interpreted and distinguished as either good or evil, and were used for both purposes. For from that hour, the mysteries of iniquity and righteousness began to reign in the world, and evil began—in the very first actions after the fall—to push aside goodness. Vice first prevailed against virtue, and natural means were employed by the first fruits of wickedness; specifically, a plant-based object <note>original: "vegetable creature"</note>, or a piece of wood, was used by the envy of unrighteous **Cain** to knock out the brains of his righteous brother **Abel**. Conversely, this same type of plant-based object was used in another sense as a piece of wood—namely, in the form of a cross (signifying the opposition made in this world between good and evil)—as an instrument of Christ's death, without which there was no assurance of salvation.

We see, therefore, that all hidden <note>original: "occult"</note> operations proceed from the secret virtues in natural things. These were discovered by God's Spirit for mankind's benefit, just as they were understood by the keen observation of Satan. To good men, I say, they were revealed by the good Spirit to do good and prevent evil—for unless the evil is known, an antidote <note>original: "counter-poyson"</note> will hardly be found. To bad men, they were provided to execute mischief and iniquity. I will list some of these secret virtues in each of the three kingdoms of living things: Animal, Vegetable, and Mineral.

First, regarding the Animal kingdom: The owl is said by **Albertus Magnus** <note>a 13th-century German Dominican friar and philosopher known for his work on the natural sciences</note> to have many notable virtues. For, he says, if its heart and right foot are placed upon someone who is sleeping, they will immediately tell whatever they have done, or anything you ask them; and he says that this has been tested by some of his fellow friars and found to be most true. And again, if one simply puts it under their armpit, no dog will bark at them. Also, goat's blood is reported by him to turn glass into a soft and pliable <note>original: "malleable"</note> state if the glass is boiled <note>original: "sod"</note> in the blood and vinegar; it becomes so soft that one may handle it like paste, and if it is thrown against a wall, it will not break. Furthermore, if one makes an ointment of the same mixture and anoints his face with it, things will appear horrible and terrifying to him. If this same mixture is put into a fire in the presence of someone who has <term>the falling sickness</term> <note>epilepsy</note>, and a magnet <note>original: "Loadstone"</note> touches them, they will immediately fall into a fit as if dead, and if some cold water is given to them to drink, they will recover. He also says that if a candle is rubbed with camel's blood, everyone in the room will seem to have camels' heads. Thus he continues in his history with descriptions of admirable wonders effected by the hidden properties of beasts, plants, and stones.

If **Mr. Foster** <note>likely William Foster, a parson who famously attacked the use of the "weapon-salve" as demonic magic</note> and his followers say that all these are lies, I reply that it was a learned philosopher and famous theologian who reported them. No doubt, if he were alive today, he would tell Mr. Foster that he should learn to understand the <term>hours of elections</term> <note>choosing the best time for an action based on the positions of the stars</note>, the stars that have dominion over the earth, and the times of their strength <note>original: "exaltation or fortitude"</note> upon the earth—and lastly, over which creatures in the three kingdoms they have their specific influences. For my part, I know of wonderful secrets in man and beasts for which <term>Peripatetic philosophy</term> <note>the traditional philosophy based on the teachings of Aristotle</note> can provide no explanation. For example: that the dried guts of a pike (or jackfish) should powerfully stimulate urine; that sucking the blood from a mole whose nose is cut off for that purpose will cure epilepsy, and that after taking it, the person becomes exceedingly sick (as experience has taught us through the cure of a Lady in **Kent**); also, that if the mole is burned into a powder, it should by its hidden nature expel colic. Further, that the heart and liver of frogs are proven treatments for epilepsy; that a snake's skin can speed up and hasten a woman's labor; that a woman's menstrual blood <note>original: "menstrues"</note> can cause leprosy; and that a dried toad or a spider applied to the nostrils of someone bleeding will stop <note>original: "stench"</note> the blood, as I have often tested myself.

As for other hidden miracles in stones, metals, herbs, and animals, the true scholars of **Solomon**—I mean **Hermes**, **Plato**, **Albertus Magnus**, **Dioscorides**, and others like them—are full of such accounts. Doubtless, they would not be so foolish or indiscreet as to publish lies and write of impossible things, claiming them to be true within their own knowledge, and thereby lose the reputation they have gained.

### CHAPTER I.

*Herein is expressed how, by comparing the Mineral Loadstone and its attractive powers <note>original: "Virtues"</note> with those of the Animal and Vegetable kingdoms, we may discover and bring to a demonstrable light the wonderful effects that lurk in both.*

Since it is a thing most worthy of observation among wise men that there is nothing in the celestial sphere <note>original: "Orbe"</note> which does not have its like in the terrestrial; so truly, there is nothing in the mineral kingdom which does not have its like in the vegetable; and again, the likeness of the vegetable sphere is found in the animal—I mean in love and hatred, in attraction and expulsion, in union and divorce. 

But because in the mineral kingdom there is found nothing in all the world so near in power <note>original: "virtue"</note> to the action and life of the animal as the Magnet or Loadstone; since it visibly affects its iron-like <note>original: "ferruginous"</note> counterpart, it seems to woo and desire it, and attracts it eagerly, and lastly unites itself to it in a marvelous manner, even as the female and male do in the animal kingdom. For this reason, every similar particle in the mineral or vegetable kingdom that works in the same way is justly termed Magnetical. 

Upon this, the well-experienced Doctor, Paracelsus, when he writes of the mystical Mummies <note>In alchemy and early medicine, "Mummy" (mumia) refers to the vital life force or spiritual essence of a living thing, rather than a preserved corpse.</note>, both physical and spiritual, and of the attractive means or manner to extract them from both the living and dead bodies, he—for the better instruction of his scholars and those he terms "the children of Art" <note>original: "filios Artis"</note>—expresses examples drawn from the Loadstone and the Iron. For by these, he sufficiently explains the manner of extracting the said Mummy and consequently reveals, in his own fashion, what the Microcosmical <note>i.e., relating to man as a "little world" that mirrors the universe.</note> or Animal Magnet is, by means of which it is extracted from the body. Namely, he suggests that it is a physical or substantial thing, as he seems to justify in these words: "The spiritual Mummy does not work except through physical means" <note>original Latin: "Spiritualis Mummia non operatur nisi per corporalia media."</note>. 

By "physical means," he suggests those secret Magnetical bodies which suck the spirit forth from the living animal and make it operate, as well at home by an immediate contact as abroad—namely, at an unlimited distance—by a natural and convenient transplantation. He, therefore, who is wise and profound in these mysteries of Nature, and to whom the Sympathetic Concordance <note>The harmony or "agreement" between things of a similar nature.</note>, hidden properties, nature, powers, and origin of the Loadstone and the Iron are well known, will know that their example may fitly be applied to man. For by it, he may easily discern the Microcosmical Magnets and understand the manner of their extraction of the spiritual Mummy out of man, and withal conceive the proper end and usage thereof. 

Therefore, so that these things may be better expanded and clarified <note>original: "enucleated"</note> for the well-wishing Reader, I think it fit in the first place to touch a little on the same string of that one harmonious <note>original: "symphoniacall"</note> Concordance that concerns the nature and origin of the Loadstone and the Iron (which we have more fully mentioned in the preceding Book of this our discourse), so that we may with greater ease understand what the Microcosmical Magnets are.

# Section 2. Mosaical Philosophy.

The physical and passive mass clearly appears to be a common Saturnine <note>original: "Saturnine"; associated with lead, coldness, and heavy stone</note>, stony, and Mercurial substance; and its "father," or active form, is a metallic or sulfurous Martial <note>original: "Martiall"; associated with iron, heat, and the planet Mars</note> spirit. Now, I ask you to observe briefly how these two are mixed: 

When the Saturnine Mercurial liquid of the stony nature was still in its "first matter" <note>the raw, undifferentiated state of a substance</note>, it was near the "Mercury of Mars" (for these two are most commonly found together)—namely, the Magnetical nature and the iron mine. Because of their close alliance and proximity in existence, only a light and easy transformation was required to unite them into one body. Therefore, it seems to possess an intermediate nature between a metal and a stone. It may well be called a "half-transformed Saturnine Mercury." When the spirit of the Martial sulfur enters this as a metallic form, the Mercury receives it as its passive mother and preserves it within itself. It then thickens <note>original: "coagulated"</note> into a stony body, which is called the Calamite <note>an archaic term for a loadstone or magnetic needle</note>, **Magnet**, or Loadstone.

Since every spirit primarily desires and seeks to be nourished by what is closest and most similar to its own nature, and since that nature and spirit is found only in iron, these two are observed to come from the same mine or the same earthly womb <note>original: "matrix"</note>. Indeed, the most perfect iron or steel is extracted from the body of the Magnet. This arises from the fact that the Martial and Saturnine spirit of the Loadstone sucks and attracts the body of iron toward its center, drawing out its formal beams as if they were spiritual food. But because the iron body will not easily abandon its internal spirit, it follows that spirit and is pulled toward the Magnet. 

In turn, the iron, finding similar spirits in the Loadstone, desires just as strongly to possess them through an equal attraction or desire. Thus, a conjunction or union is made between them, no differently than between a husband and wife. However, because the Loadstone is fuller of the Saturnine stony Mercury than the iron (which has been purified of it by fire), the Loadstone is closer to the property of the male. Therefore, the iron does not suck the Loadstone as greedily as the Loadstone sucks the iron. 

It is an old, confirmed principle <note>original: "axiom"</note> that Matter desires and longs for Form, and as eagerly draws and allures it as the female does the male. That the iron represents the male is apparent in the strength it adds to the Loadstone; for if the Loadstone’s pole is capped with steel, it animates the stone far beyond its own natural power. This "arming" of the stone causes it to draw a much greater weight of iron than it was otherwise able to. If we consider this correctly, we may more easily understand what that "microcosmic Loadstone" might be—the one able to extract the microcosmic spirit without any damage or weakening of the body.

If, therefore, we wish to attempt this excellent feat, we must do it using a physical Magnet taken from the Microcosm, or Man. Its production and generation must in every respect agree with that of the macrocosmic or earthly mineral Loadstone mentioned before. I intend to describe this to you only through indirect language <note>original: "circumlocution"</note> and not in plain terms. I do this so that so great a secret—this key to unlocking the healing <note>original: "balsamick"</note> cabinet of man’s Mummial nature <note>the vital life force preserved in the body</note>—may be hidden from the unworthy, yet remain sufficiently clear to the worthy and religious Philosopher through obvious clues. If such hidden mysteries of nature were discovered by the common crowd, there would be no difference between a wise man and a fool. Therefore, Solomon taught us, *It is the part of a wise man to hide the matter* <note>original: "Quod sit sapientis celare rem"</note>. 

The wise Philosophers in their writings expressed the secrets of nature so carefully that they might hide them from the ignorant and incapable masses, yet speak plainly to the "children of art" and sons of true learning. But this is not all. I want you to understand that the property of this magnetic microcosmic work is so universal that it shows the way to infect the Mummial spirits of man with a venomous and harmful nature, just as easily as it shows how to extract them in a wholesome and sympathetic condition for healing uses. 

For that reason—specifically because evil-minded people, such as witches and sorcerers whom the devil has instructed in the abuse of this mystery, as well as wicked men (whom I call "devils in the flesh") might do great mischief in the world if this were publicly revealed—I think it wisest not to name the internal microcosmic Magnet openly. Instead, I will express it only in more general terms.

# Mosaic Philosophy. Book 2.

I want every wise person to understand that the magnetic nature of all things—both antipathetic <note>original: "antipathericall"; repelling or conflicting</note> and sympathetic <note>original: "sympatheticall"; attracting or harmonizing</note>—consists only in the sulfurous <note>original: "sulphureous"; in alchemy, sulfur represents the active, fiery, and soul-like principle</note> power of the vital spirits. Because these spirits are imprisoned within matter, they are inclined to attract things like themselves by contracting from the outer edges <note>original: "circumference"</note> toward the center. 

Likewise, the animal, vegetable, and mineral salt—which is the direct container for this sulfurous spirit—uses the action of the spirits within it to suck and draw similar substances from its surroundings. This is due to its pure, Saturnine <note>associated with lead, cold, and weight</note>, and Mercurial <note>associated with fluidity and spirit</note> earth. Through this process, they grow and multiply, both in their airy, volatile salt (which is condensed like snow or frost by "Saturnine" or cold northern conditions) and in their ethereal or heavenly fire. 

Furthermore, the sulfurous spirit flies back or reflects its beams into its central salt after it has moved toward the body's surface due to "northern" influences—specifically external cold. This is visible in the fiery or heavenly "seeds" contained in the air inside a weather-glass <note>an early type of thermometer or barometer</note>. When the north wind blows, the air in the glass contracts because the expanded spirits of the "heavenly sulfur" (the celestial fire within the air) flee from their cold opposite. The spirit retreats to the center of the air, surrounding itself as if with a cloud or building a "house" to resist the harshness of the northern blasts. For—as I will show later in my magnetic demonstration—the sulfurous Equator is an enemy to the cold Mercurial poles.

Similarly, in the human body, when a "northern" or numbing <note>original: "stupid"; here meaning dulling or paralyzing</note> fear takes hold, the sulfurous spirits contract. This leaves the outer appearance pale, bluish, and wan, as the internal spirits of the body are pulled toward the center. This movement is antipathetic <note>repulsive</note> and is caused by an unnatural emotional state. On the other hand, when these internal sulfurous spirits are at liberty, they expand and spread out into the open air, since there is no obvious magnet to pull them into a smaller space.

To conclude, therefore, the microcosmic magnet <note>a magnet representing the human being as a "little world" or microcosm</note> must be generated from the sulfurous spirits of the microcosm within its own salt (which is its "form" or essence), and from a foreign Mercury. Because this Mercury is nearby and similar, it is very compatible—almost like a relative by adoption—and serves as its "passive matter." 

From these two microcosmic parts—the active essence and the passive matter—our secret Magnet is created. Through this magnet, the "spiritual Mummy" <note>original: "Mummy"; in Paracelsian medicine, this refers to the vital life force or "balsam" of a living body, not a preserved corpse</note> is extracted from a living person. This process can achieve wonderful cures or cause deadly harm, whether from a distance <note>original: "ad distans"</note> or through direct contact. 

Furthermore, this same internal magnet or "attractive salt" in a person (the seat of the sulfurous, life-giving spirit) will perform the same healing effects and many other rare experimental feats if it is transferred into the blood through "transplantation" <note>moving the vital force from one body to another</note> from a living person via an efflux <note>original: "effluxion"; a flowing out of energy or spirit</note>, or through nails and hair separated from the person and given to another subject. 

There is also another microcosmic magnet taken from a dead man. By using this, the spiritual "Mummy" can be drawn out of a living person and used for health, either through direct application or by transplanting it into a plant, herb, or tree, as will be explained more fully later in this book. 

However, since it is best for the common reader to demonstrate these things "after the fact" <note>original: "à posteriori"; reasoning from effects back to their original causes</note>, I will begin my explanation with the physical elements and move upward toward more subtle, complex, and hidden things—as if I were climbing from earth to heaven in steady steps. Therefore, I intend first to show you the magnetic effects produced by the physical contact of two different bodies of the same nature. But before I begin discussing the "Mummy" taken from a human corpse, I believe it is necessary to first discuss the mystery of the dead carcass itself, so that we may proceed in an organized way.

# Section 2. Mosaic Philosophy.

## CHAPTER II.

*That there are four sorts of corporal Mummy, of which only one is useful and necessary for healing purposes. In this Chapter also is set down an experiment, with certain visible demonstrations, confirming the magnetic or attractive power of the balsamic spirits, which are in the useful Mummy.*

Those who have deeply considered and respected both the external and internal nature of man have perceived that the human <note>original: "microcosmicall"; referring to man as a "little world" that mirrors the universe</note> Mummy <term>Mummy: in 17th-century medicine, "mummy" referred to the vital essence or "balsam" found in human remains, believed to hold magnetic healing properties</term> is of two types: corporal or spiritual. I intend to speak of the first in this present chapter; the second shall be handled later, and at length. Regarding the corporal Mummy, it is either naturally sympathetic <note>original: "sympatheticall"; attracting or harmonious</note> or unnaturally antipathetic <note>original: "antipatheticall"; repelling or harmful</note>. We find by experience that the natural Mummy is only medicinal and health-giving <note>original: "salutiferous"</note> after its proper preparation, which is achieved chiefly by its own magnetic property; the rest are more likely to cause diseases and infect healthy people than to provide any healing relief or comfort.

For, just as there are four kinds of corporal and substantial Mummies according to the nature of the four elements, they are also distinguished by those elements whose natures they have taken on. Three of these are corruptible and bringers of death and sickness—namely, the earthly, the watery, and the fiery—and only the one which is airy is useful to man's life and friendly to his nature. 

Regarding those three kinds of Mummy which cause corruption, the reason they prove corruptible is this: we must first hold it as a general rule in Philosophy, that "the thing corrupted takes on the nature of the thing corrupting it" <note>original: "Quod corruptum corrumpentis naturam in se induit"</note>. For example, if the dead corpse of a man is corrupted in the earth, it is changed and passes into the nature of the earth, becoming useless <note>original: "inutil"</note> for man's health—and indeed more destructive than constructive or wholesome. Again, if the corruption happens in the water, then the corrupted flesh or dead body will acquire a watery and slimy <note>original: "musseluginous"</note> disposition, which will also prove very inconvenient or unprofitable for the preservation of the vital spirits. And lastly, by the excessive violence of fire, the spirits in the Mummial body will be consumed, wasted, or exhaled. 

Now, the reason why these corporal Mummies in those states are unsuitable for the preservation of health is because those three elements destroy and corrupt the body so much that they force its earth, its water, and its fire to return to their first matter. Consequently, while the earth and the water are ordained to be the containers of two life-giving elements—namely, fire and air, which can only be preserved in a body that is not corrupted—it must necessarily follow that in those three Mummies, those life-giving spirits must vanish and fly away for want of a natural body (which has now become corrupted and destroyed, and therefore unnatural). Since nothing is required in the true Mummy more than what is fit and proper for the preservation of life—indeed, for life itself, which is the air—and since air is banished and expelled from those three Mummies, nothing can be extracted from them but sickness, death, and destruction, and consequently harmful effects. Thus, if a healthy, murdered, or strangled body rots under the earth or in the water, it is not fit or proper for the wholesome use of the human body. 

The very same consideration should be given to bodies that died through infirmities and diseases; although they are not visibly corrupted by the three external elements mentioned, it nevertheless happens that a certain invisible corrupting influence and impression is made by the external elements upon the internal ones. From this comes that internal <note>original: "intestine"</note> war in man's body, by which the elements kill and corrupt one another, but in different ways—namely, differently in one body than in another—depending on which element or elemental change is said to have dominion or rule over the other. This is the reason why such a variety of diseases haunt the human body: for example, Dropsy <note>original: "Dropsie"; edema or swelling caused by fluid</note> comes from the strong influence of water; the Hectic or burning Fever <note>original: "Feavor"</note> comes from fiery attacks; and Leprosy from the dominion of earth, and so on. Therefore, wherever any such elemental corruption happens to the body, the wholesome spirit of the corporal Mummy, along with its dwelling place <note>original: "habitacle"</note>, is utterly destroyed, and the spirit is forced to de-

But if a healthy body—that is, one not having any infirmity—is killed only by the element of air (meaning through strangling or by hanging), then no impression of the previously mentioned elements will be found in the physical mass of the man's carcass. For that reason, it will remain uncorrupted and will not suffer any elemental decay <note>original: "resolution"</note> so long as it is preserved in the air. ### *The Proposition.*

If this healthy kind of airy Mummy, with its vehicle or magnetic instrument, is taken, chosen, or selected rightly, it will—by reason of the absence of actual life and the dominance of cold—take on the condition of the Northern pole. <note>In this philosophy, the North Pole represents cold, contraction, and attraction, while the Equator represents heat and expansion.</note> Consequently, for that reason, those airy included spirits (which were of a hot, equinoctial nature while the body was living, and therefore more expansive from the center to the circumference than attractive) are now made by death to act from the circumference to the center. If they are stimulated by spirits like themselves which are equinoctial and lively, then they become attractive of the equinoctial Mummy—namely, by contracting themselves into the center. Consequently, this airy microcosmic Mummy must be endowed with the magnetic property of the Northern pole; therefore, by applying it directly to its like (the living man), it will greedily suck and attract his like nature. Having drawn it in, it will retain it. So it may, by a due preparation, be made sympathetic and reduced into a singular medicine for man's health and preservation. Or it may be so contaminated and made "antipathetic" <note>repellent or harmful</note> with the impure and infectious Mummy of a sick living creature, that it may free the infirm person by extracting the poison which infected them, and then infect a wholesome and sound body to which it might be given internally.

### *An Experiment upon this.*

I collected a portion of this "Northern" Mummy—namely, the flesh of a man strangled in the air, in which the spiritual Mummy was centrally contracted by cold—and I applied it topically <note>original: "typically"; likely a typo for "topically," meaning applied to the surface of the body</note> to the part of my body which was nearest to it in natural position. I found it, upon contact, to be freezing cold, as if it were ice and Northern. After it had remained on for a certain time, I found that as its frozen and northernly-contracted spirits were stimulated by the equinoctial heat of my body, they drew off my mummial and life-giving spirits greedily. At some times, and as if in fits, I felt them in their magnetic operation sensibly, and in a somewhat painful <note>original: "dolorous"</note> fashion, tugging and pulling at the adjacent parts close about it. In conclusion, after a certain time, I took it off and found it much altered in smell and appearance because of the quantity of my spirits which it had attracted. Both of these mummial spirits, so magnetically joined together, I extracted and prepared after my own manner for the use of my own body. But because my assertion will perhaps be given little credit, I will prove the feasibility of it, and the probability of every part of this, by many and various examples or *demonstrations*.

## II. Demonstration.

That the dead spirits in a body will not attract dead spirits to themselves, nor will the living spirits in a body magnetically suck living spirits to themselves (except very moderately), is argued by the operation of the loadstone in this manner.

### Problem I.

The Southern pole of one loadstone flees from and avoids the Southern pole of another with a certain hatred. They will by no means be joined together in friendship but avoid contact with one another through a natural antipathy. But if the Northern pole of one is applied to the Southern pole of the other, they will stick and cling together by a strong attraction.

Concerning the strengthening and increase of spirits in the dead and powerless—or Northern—Mummy, through contact with Southern or lively Mummy (flesh): it is magnetically argued to be both possible and probable. If you are presented with two magnets—each fitted with two steel iron "teeth"—one being strong and the other weak or much smaller, but with equal diameters between the teeth; then, if you place the teeth of opposite poles together, the stronger will seize <note>original: "apprehend"</note> and lift up the weaker. ### Problem 4.

There is a magnetic attraction from the equator of the loadstone <note>original: "Load-stone"; a naturally magnetized mineral</note>, but it is far different from that of the northern pole, both in its force <note>original: "violence"</note> and in its manner of attraction. The equinoctial <note>equatorial</note> attraction is naturally milder, acting as a middle ground between the two poles. Yet, in substance, it is all one earth, though varying in how its form is expressed. For example, a piece of iron will stand less perpendicularly, and the attraction will be weaker, the closer it approaches from the pole toward the equator. Furthermore, all those who have written the history of magnetism ascribe the greatest force of attraction to the northern pole of the magnet, as shall also be declared and proved more extensively hereafter.

I will conclude with a demonstration taken from the similar "mummy" <note>In this context, "mummy" or "mummia" refers to the residual vital energy or life-force remaining in raw flesh or a corpse.</note> of beasts; and it is this:

### *The fourth demonstration, which is Animal.*

It is a common practice, and widely used, to take a piece of raw beef and apply it to the nape of the neck to draw away "rheums" <note>original: "rheumes"; watery discharges or excess humors</note> or fluids from the eyes. I was informed by a person of credit and learning that when a simple fellow, who was troubled with sore and watering eyes, was advised to apply raw beef to the back of his neck to draw back and divert the humor, he misunderstood the instructions. He applied the raw, cold beef directly upon both of his eyes; and it was his misfortune that it attracted so strongly that, instead of drawing out the fluid, it pulled out his very eyeballs <note>original: "eye-holes"</note>. 

Also, a worthy gentlewoman of my acquaintance told me that she had raw beef applied to her neck to divert the fluid from her eyes. ### The first Experimental History.

My mathematical master, famous for his knowledge in the art of engineering (who lived with Cardinal St. George in Rome), assured me that if anyone had a withered or wasted member—such as a dried arm, leg, or foot, which physicians call an **atrophy of the limbs**—and if he cut the nails, hair, and scrapings of the skin from that member, and then drilled into a willow tree with a tool <note>original: "auger, or wimble"</note> down to the pith; and after that, if he thrust those pared nails and cut hair into the hole and stopped the hole tightly with a peg or pin made of the same wood; observing also that this action must be performed when the Moon is waxing <note>original: "increasing"</note> and the auspicious planets are in such "multiplying" signs as Gemini, while Saturn (who is a great drier) is low in the sky <note>original: "depressed"</note>, the limb that was so wasted shall gradually grow healthy again <note>original: "re-vegetate"</note>, just as the tree (in which the bodily waste is enclosed) shall daily increase, grow, and flourish. We may rightly compare the mass of these superfluous growths to a smaller loadstone capped with steel. When it is "transplanted" into the plant, its force of attraction becomes greater. Just as iron added to the pole of a loadstone—even if the magnet is weak—fortifies it and enables it to attract a much greater weight (because the iron gives it strength), in the same way, if these magnetic growths are grafted into the body of the "magnetic tree," then that tree will suck and draw its like—namely the spirit of the defective limbs—more strongly toward it. This makes the limbs become "vegetative" (full of life) and allows them to increase and grow, whereas before they pined and withered. For the spirit, drawn and continued by extension <note>original: "dilatation"</note> from the limb to the life-giving nature of the tree, takes on that same nature. Through this continuity, it animates the fading spirits in the limb to increase, grow, or prosper. There is a strong union in a loadstone armed with steel, and it can pick up a heavier weight than if it is not so armed.

The reason is that **united force is stronger** <note>original Latin: "vis unita est fortior"</note>; for the iron adds force to a loadstone that is weak, as is confirmed by this problem.

## CHAPTER VI.

*In this chapter, it is proved that plants contain magnetic spirits within themselves. By means of these spirits, they noticeably attract forces from the animal, vegetable, and mineral kingdoms. This is first stated in two propositions and supported by various experimental demonstrations.*

### The First Proposition.

There is a magnetic virtue in plants, just as there is in animals and minerals, which operates and acts attractively both on its own kind in the vegetable kingdom, and also on those in the animal and mineral kingdoms.

### The First Experimental Demonstration.

The evidence for this is manifold. Through what has been related in the previous chapter, the magnetic relationship or union formed between the plant and the animal has been sufficiently expressed, and it shall be more fully clarified <note>original: "enucleated"; to explain something in detail, like removing a kernel from a nut</note> hereafter. ### 2. Proposition

The unique order, sympathy, or antipathy of vegetable parts among themselves is described and symbolically set forth by the relationship or respect shown toward the lodestone <term>original: "Load-stone"; a naturally magnetized piece of the mineral magnetite</term>. By this, it is argued that the vegetable and mineral kingdoms—and consequently the animal kingdom—observe one sympathetic or harmonic proportion, both in their sympathetic order and their antipathetic irregularity during disorder.

### A Problem for the confirmation of the aforesaid Proposition

In all magnetic things, whether they are vegetable or mineral (and consequently animal), nature always tends toward a convenient unity, both in nature and position. Contrariwise, where their parts do not incline toward a conjunction according to the course of nature, there occurs a disturbance and, as it were, a diversity between part and part.

One must then turn C toward D, and they will agree well and be combined together.

### CHAPTER VI.

->*How the sensory reality and feasibility of the magnetic method of cure by the weapon-salve <note>term: "weapon-salve" — a medicinal ointment that, according to sympathetic magic/science of the time, cured a wound when applied to the weapon that caused it.</note> is produced and demonstrated to be natural. To better achieve this, we will first set down our main proposition regarding this kind of cure, and afterward clarify and clearly demonstrate it by evident proofs, derived especially from the properties of the lodestone <note>original: "Load-stone"</note>.*<-

->The Proposition.<-

If, after a wound is made, a portion of the wound's external blood (along with its inward spirits), or of its internal spirits alone that have penetrated into the weapon—or any other object that has probed the depth of the wound—is conveyed from the wound to an ointment at any reasonable, though undefined or unknown, distance; and if that ointment's composition is balsamic <note>term: "balsamic" — having the healing and preservative qualities of a balsam or resin.</note> and specifically agrees with the nature of the wounded creature, and is adapted and, as it were, transplanted or grafted into it in a proper and convenient manner; then the ointment, thus "animated" by those spirits, will immediately become magnetic. It will then align with a magnetic gaze or regard toward the radiant spirits that stream forth invisibly from the wound, being directed there by those spiritual bloody spirits in the weapon or other object that received or included them. 

The living and "southern" <note>In Fludd’s system, "southern" represents the active, warm, life-giving pole of vitality.</note> beams streaming and flowing from the wound will concur and unite themselves with the "northern" <note>In Fludd’s system, "northern" represents the cold, contractive, and "fixed" pole.</note> attraction of the magnetically animated ointment. This union stirs the "northern" and congealed or fixed bloody spirits contained in the ointment to act "southerly"—that is, from the center to the circumference. Through this reciprocal action, union, or continuity, the living southern beams will act upon and revive the chill, fixed, or northern beams that animate the ointment with magnetic power. The quickened spirits of the ointment, animated by the spirits of both sources and directed by the spirits first transplanted into it, impart their balsamic and healing <note>original: "sanative"</note> power to the spirits in the wound, which were first magnetically attracted. These spirits then, by an inseparable harmony, transfer that healing back to the wound itself. 

This is the reason for that sympathetic and antipathetic relationship observed by experience to exist between the ointment and the wound. Thus, if the entire part of the weapon that made the wound is covered and anointed with the ointment, and the ointment is well wrapped and kept warm, the wound will find comfort and be at ease. However, if a part of the ointment is scraped away or wiped off from the weapon, it has often been tested that pain or ache <note>original: "dolour"</note> will immediately follow and afflict the wound. Moreover, if the anointed place is kept moderately warm, the wound will also remain in a stable state; but if it is uncovered and left in the open, cold air, then the wound will also be disturbed and bothered by the cold.

### The fifth Member of the Proposition, with the Proofs.

<margin>5.</margin>
Fifthly, the magnetic act and operation of celestial, astral (starry), and influential spirits are not to be limited, nor are they to be impeded or hindered in their motion, if we look into the mystery of this business with intellectual eyes.

For your better understanding, we must distinguish this Member into two separate articles or branches. The first must show that the extension of the emanations made from two astral or starry spirits cannot be limited by human understanding, even if we might guess at it based on an external effect. The second shall prove that such influential starry beams, or quintessential emissions—such as those sent forth from the magnet to the iron, or from one magnet to another of like nature, and consequently from all other magnetic bodies of similar essence—cannot be hindered by the placement of any solid or well-compacted bodies between them. This is true despite what some <term>Fool-losophers</term>, rather than <term>Philosophers</term>, have rashly claimed in their writings.

<note>Fool-losophers: A pun by the author (Fludd), mocking his intellectual opponents who lacked true spiritual or chemical understanding.</note>

Regarding the first point, which concerns the imaginary termination or bounding of beamy or formal extensions (emanations) from magnetic bodies within a settled or known limited sphere of activity: the impossibility of such a limit (despite what our <term>Peripatetic Philosophers</term> have imagined) is argued by the following problematic demonstrations.

<note>Peripatetic Philosophers: Followers of Aristotle's philosophy, whom Fludd often criticized for being too reliant on physical senses and logic rather than spiritual insight.</note>

### Certain Problematic Demonstrations, confirming the contents of this Member's first Article

### 1. Problem.

The vigor in heavenly bodies, by which they move themselves, argues that there is a soul in them. For that reason, they are esteemed by the wisest philosophers to be endowed and animated with a divine act or spirit by which they move. Since this is the case, the extension or application of their beams must also prove uncertain and therefore without limit. This is because their spirits, after the emanation is made, meet sometimes in the air, sometimes in the water, and sometimes—without resistance—they pierce even to the center of the earth to operate upon the mineral kingdom. They bestow upon the earthly subjects under them that very formal act and virtue by which they operate in their sharp penetration. Therefore, these inferior creatures of a similar nature are able to send forth and extend their astral or beamy virtues as far, and apply their beams at as unending a distance, as their stars in heaven are observed to do.

### 2. Problem.

It is rightly said, then, that the magnet moves the magnet, and both dispose of one another by their primary form, which they receive from their starry fountain. And therefore it was no absurdity for the wise man, <term>Thales of Miletus</term>, nor yet any madness in <term>Scaliger</term>, to assign a soul to the magnet, seeing that by it, the magnet is centrally incited, directed, and carried or moved circularly. ### *An Addition.*

By this, it might be argued that the action of one loadstone upon another, or upon iron, appears by its effect to be limited within a certain range <note>original: "dimension"</note>. The loadstone and iron, among all other bodies known to us, are the most similar in nature and condition to the earth itself. They contain a substance that is most pure, similar <note>original: "homogeniall"</note>, and closely related to the earth. Therefore, these three—loadstone, iron, and earth—agree in nature together.

### *Application.*

By this it appears what a close relationship exists between the body of man (which we rightly compare to the earth), the blood that flows from the veins of the earth (referring to the magnet <note>original: "Load stone"</note>), and the ointment filled with a bloody spirit which was extracted from blood. For the fat, the *Usnea* <note>original: "Uznea"; moss grown on a human skull, used as a primary ingredient in the weapon salve.</note>, and the "mummy" <note>original: "Mummy"; a medicinal preparation made from preserved human remains, believed to contain life-force.</note> were derived from blood. The Scriptures tell us that the soul of the flesh—and consequently of the fat and bones—is in the blood. By this we may see that although these three differ in physical substance, they agree in the sameness <note>original: "homogeneity"</note> of their spirit.

Therefore, it is no marvel that there is a continuity between the spirit of the blood in the body and that which has been moved <note>original: "transplanted"</note> into the salve. Neither should we wonder at the natural connection between the bloody spirits and the ointment, or that such a sudden union should be made between them. It immediately becomes a magnet, specifically adapted for its healing and health-giving <note>original: "Balsamick and sanative"</note> operation. The wound is guided and directed by these bloody spirits which are moved into it; after being activated, these spirits turn the rays of their nature toward their own kind. They are as close in spirit and property to the wounded man's blood as a piece of iron or a magnet broken off from the whole is to the original source, matching the spirit of the "father" from which it sprang.

So we also see that although the macrocosmic air <note>The air of the world at large.</note> seems to vary in nature according to its position (for the Northern air is cold, while the Southern or equatorial air is hot), it is still only one spirit, no matter how it is divided into this or that cloud. And again, the internal or formal spirit that gives life to the four winds in different ways is only one and the same indivisible spirit (as the Prophet *Ezekiel* tells us). In like manner, it is one and the same identity of spirit that acts in the wound, the transferred blood, and the ointment—all three being, as it were, <margin>Acts 17.</margin> but one blood. This is as the Apostle taught the *Athenians*: that all men came from one blood, and consequently from one spirit in the blood. I prove it also by this Problem.

## 6. *Problem.*

Attraction occurs in the primary bodies, and these are closest to one another and share a mutual agreement <note>original: "consent"</note> because of their identical condition. For this reason, the magnet draws the magnet, iron draws iron, and the earth draws them all; and again, each of them draws another.

### *Application.*

From this, we gather a reason why blood draws blood, and one body draws its own kind, and why the ointment—being animated by the same nature—attracts its like to itself. Therefore *Paracelsus* rightly says: *Any body that is given the living mummy of another man internally immediately becomes a magnet.* <note>original: "Quodlibet corpus, cui Mummia viva in alio homine propinatur, illico fit magnes."</note> And therefore we may rightly say, since experience has made it manifest, that every "microcosmic" ointment <note>An ointment relating to the human body, viewed as a miniature universe.</note> that has absorbed or contained the spiritual "mummy" of another man's blood is immediately made a magnet. By the prompting <note>original: "incitation"</note> of the mummified spirit it contains, it greedily thirsts and longs for its own kind. For that reason, it draws and allures blood to it, thereby sharing its life-giving property with the thing it attracts. I could say much more to prove the reason for the strong attraction of this ointment once it is animated with a living man's spirits, but I would be too long-winded; I will touch upon it in the following sections. For that reason, I will leave this part and proceed to the seventh.

## *Certain Problematic Demonstrations, to confirm this part of the aforementioned Proposition.*

To better explain our purpose, we must divide this section into three Articles or Parts. ### *Demonstrations confirming the contents of this first Article.*

Regarding the first Article of this Part, which identifies the transplanted spirit as the cause for the ointment becoming magnetic, we prove it thus:

#### *1 Problem.*

<margin>Gilbert, *On the Magnet*, book 2, chapter 25.</margin>
Experience has taught us, and *Baptista Porta* confirms, that if a weak Loadstone is hidden in steel dust for a time, it will become stronger and more powerful in its attraction; likewise, the steel will be improved by the loadstone's nature. But *Paracelsus* provides a closer example in his account, saying that by heating the Loadstone and extinguishing it in an oil of *Saffron of Mars* <note>original: "Crocus Martis"; a chemical preparation of iron oxide.</note> (which is made of the best Carinthian Steel) repeatedly until it will absorb no more, it will so strengthen this Loadstone that it will have ten times more attractive force than it had before.

#### **Application.**

By a similar logic, the weak spirits in the transplanted blood, being absorbed by the animal ointment—which has the same relationship to the spiritual "mummy" <note>original: "Mummy"; the vital essence or life-force extracted from human remains.</note> within it as the oil of *Saffron of Mars* has to the weak spirits in the Loadstone—will be revived and restored in their magnetic vigor. Being mingled with its oily counterpart, it will make a compounded Magnet, which will draw its similar spirits much more strongly than it could before. Again, just as the small or weak Magnet recovers its force by being buried in the dust or iron-rich earth that matches its nature, so also the bloody spirits, being interred in the oily "earth" of their own nature, unite themselves to the ointment. They do this by attracting their likeness from the source of the blood and the healing spirit from the ointment. This creates an emanation that forms a fit Magnet, which communicates its healing nature to both. By attracting the spirit of the wounded limb, it makes itself medicinal. Thus, through a continuity and integrity of spirit, it bestows—via immediate spiritual contact—the healing spirit of the *Usnea* <note>original: "Uznea"; a medicinal moss grown on human skulls.</note> and other oily ingredients into the wound. Do we not observe that water passing by a heap of salt takes on the entire quality of the salt, even if the stream is long, communicating that nature from one end to the other? Even more so, the air will carry the nature of a place it passes by to a great distance, and yet all that animated air remains continuous; therefore, this is even truer for that subtle celestial spirit which inhabits the air.

#### *2 Problem.*

<margin>Gilbert, *On the Magnet*, book 2, chapter 4.</margin>
Iron, when touched by a magnet, recreates other iron by touching it, and instructs it in magnetic motions.

### 3 Problem.

<margin>Mark Ridley in his *Treatise of the Magnet* <note>original: "Load-stone"</note>, chapter 16.</margin>

The Apothecary is still living and will be ready to confirm this. The same is better confirmed by this next problem.

## 5 Problem.

<margin>Ridley, chapter 19.</margin>
If a magnetic needle, after being touched by a loadstone <note>A naturally magnetized piece of the mineral magnetite.</note>, is made red-hot in a fire, it will lose all its polar power <note>original: "puissance"</note> and its ability to point in a specific direction. ### Application.

## 7 Problem.

If two magnets, each "armed" with two steel teeth, are set before us—one being strong and the other weak or much smaller, but with equal diameters between the teeth—then set their teeth together so they meet from contrary poles. The stronger magnet will take hold of and lift the weaker one. Once the weaker is united and incorporated with the stronger, the power it receives from the stronger allows it to lift the larger magnet from the ground and hold it firmly, even though the larger magnet is much heavier than the weight the small stone normally lifts.

### Application.

Through this mineral example, we are taught (by converting measures of weight into proportions of spiritual vigor) that the frozen and removed blood-spirits—when "capped" and "armed" with the ointment, whose nature is as close to the spirits as the blood itself—become a magnet so powerful that it can attract the larger and stronger nature of the living blood. This is achieved by applying the "Northern" nature of the smaller magnet (the blood in the ointment) to the "Southern" nature of the larger magnet (the living person). By this means, a natural union is made in the mineral kingdom, as is proved by this problem.

### *The Eighth Part of the Proposition, with its Proofs.*

The eighth part of this proposition is that in all magnetic operations, there must be a reciprocal application or influence <note>original: "aspect"</note> between the lover and the beloved, like that between the matter (the feminine) which desires and the form (the male) which is desired. Through a similarity or continuation of formal spirits, like is united to its like, which then acts upon the matter. ## The Ninth Part <note>original: "Member"</note> of the Proposition, with its Proofs.

The ninth part of the proposition is that the strong attractive faculties of every magnet are of a Northern condition, or Boreal property, and consequently have their chief attractive faculty from the North Star <note>the Pole Star</note>. Therefore, in the manner of the lodestone <note>a naturally magnetized mineral</note>, it draws from the circumference toward the center. Furthermore, all things that are desired or loved—insofar as they are "formal" <note>possessing an active, shaping essence</note>—participate in the equinoctial faculty, which sends out beams by expansion <note>original: "dilatation"</note> from the center. Therefore, their union through contact creates a mixture of temperament that sits between the North Pole and the Equator. This mixture is partly attractive and partly expansive, much like a person’s vital spirit, which acts in contraction <note>systole</note> and expansion <note>diastole</note>; such is the act of magnetic union <note>original: "coition"</note>.

### *Demonstration.*

Now that the greatest attractive power <note>original: "virtue"</note> comes from the North, I will demonstrate it in many ways. ### The Eleventh Part <note>original: "Member"</note> of this Proposition, with its Proofs.

The eleventh part is that the alteration of the air affects both extremes equally. This is clear evidence of a continuous unity in spirit between the transplanted blood in the ointment and the wound itself. Whatever reaction <note>original: "passion"</note> the disturbed or harsh <note>original: "unclement"</note> air causes in one is felt by the other. This is no different than if a thread were tied at both ends of a vessel or frame <note>original: "Gallem"</note>: when one end is touched, the other end "sympathizes" or reacts in the same way by connection. This is an evident argument that the air is the <term>medium</term> (the substance through which something is transmitted) or vehicle in which the spiritual influence travels. This formal, celestial, or influential spirit carried within the air communicates with the disturbances of its airy vehicle through immediate contact. Consequently, it is changed bit by bit into either a "Northern" or "Southern" state <note>original: "disposition"</note>. Therefore, due to the cold of the external air, it pulls spirits away from the wound, leaving it disturbed and painful <note>original: "dolorous"</note>, as the wound is deprived of some of its natural heat by that attraction. Thus, sympathy is turned into antipathy, as is seen when the ointment is removed from the weapon where the wound was inflicted, either totally or in part, as mentioned before.

This is the case with the blood of the wounded, and also with the <term>Uznea</term> <note>A moss found on the skulls of those who died violently, used in sympathetic medicine.</note> and <term>Mummy</term> <note>Prepared human remains used as a medicinal ingredient.</note> in the ointment, which share the same species of spirit, even if they are not from the same individual.

You see therefore, Learned Reader, how plainly this matter, or the aforementioned proposition, has been demonstrated, both by the loadstone and by the natural processes of the great world, and the practical use of the weather-glass; which I term...

### *The Second Proposition*

It has been observed in the cure of wounds by the weapon-salve <note>An ointment applied to the weapon that caused a wound, rather than the wound itself, believed to heal the patient through "sympathy."</note> that if there happens to be any loss of blood from another part of the wounded man during the time of the cure—such as a nosebleed, passing blood in the urine, or from another wound—or if he has sexual intercourse with any menstruating woman in the meantime, the force of the ointment will be diverted, and its effectiveness will be of little use. The reason I can give is that the "Southern" bloody spirit <note>The author uses "Southern" to refer to the warm, active, and radiating spirit of the blood, contrasting it with the "Northern" cold/attractive state.</note>, which, reigning in the veins, emitted and directed its beams toward the ointment, was easily attracted and absorbed by the ointment. But when that spirit is diverted and turned another way, and is attracted by a contrary magnetic subject, then a "divorce," as it were, will be made by the second magnet between the emanating spirit and the attractive force in the ointment. I will maintain and demonstrate this to be true by this magnetic experiment:

### *A Problem to confirm the Proposition from Gilbert, Book 2 of "On the Magnet," chapter 31* <note>original: "Gilb. lib. 2. de Mag. cap. 31." Referring to William Gilbert’s famous 1600 work *De Magnete*.</note>

Two lodestones <note>term: magnets</note> or pieces of magnetized iron, which are properly sticking together, will break apart upon the arrival of another fresher and stronger lodestone or magnetized iron. The newcomer will easily drive away the other with a contrary face and will command it; thus, the effort or the "desire" of the first two which were joined will end.

### *Application*

Thus you see how fittingly these two concur: namely, the previously described actions of animals with those of minerals. I end this chapter with this assertion: spirits that receive their refinement <note>original: "subtiliation"</note> and action from natural heat act vigorously as long as they remain within the perceptible orbit of light’s heating <note>original: "calefacting"</note> beams, being stirred up from the center to the circumference <note>original: "a centro ad circumferentiam"</note>. 

But if the said spirits depart or wander out of the orbit of light and are surrounded by the cold action of darkness, then they contract themselves from the circumference toward the center. Thus, resting in the center, they cease to act unless they are incited or provoked by the power of heat, which thins them and, through this refinement, makes both extremes alike. This is proven by the weather-glass <note>term: an early form of thermometer or thermoscope that used air expansion to measure temperature</note> and by blood issuing out of the wound, etc., as was said before. 

Therefore, I will boldly conclude that the spirits of the blood—conveyed either in the body of the blood, or sucked up into the wounding weapon, or in a stick, knitting needle, probe, or such-like—may be called forth, extracted, or revived and united to their source. This is done partly by preserving the blood from the harshness of the external air until it is separated by the comfortable, warm heat of its own kind, and partly by the lively union or concurrence and conjunction of its like through a favorable and healthy connection.

In the end, they were able to say so little and demonstrate even less to prove this manner of cure to be natural; because of this, they gave way without protest to the rash and reckless <note>original: "temerarious"</note> judgments of such self-conceited persons who would claim this kind of cure to be only evil magic <note>term: "Cacomagical"</note> and diabolical. These critics insultingly attempt to maintain this view only because great, apparent philosophers who wrote in defense of this subject could say so little, and to so small a purpose, to the contrary. I will speak a few words concerning some other histories which are, and may be, referred to this same manner of cure.

# CHAPTER VII.

## *How it is possible, by natural and sympathetic operation, that a disease in the blood may be cured only by the transplantation of its waste products at a far distance into a vegetable soil; not growing the disease, but comforting the infected nature by killing the disease.*

### The Proposition.

It is possible that an infectious disease in the blood and body may be cured by transplanting the watery waste of the blood—namely, the sick party's urine—at a far distance into the ashes of a vegetable which is suited to comfort nature and to kill and destroy the infection that weakens it.

->*An experimental history to confirm this.*<-

<margin>+ Ash Tree</margin>There is a nobleman of high rank, very wise, religious, and held in the highest esteem, who commonly cures yellow jaundice at a distance of sometimes (as he has related to me) a hundred miles. He does this only by means of the sick party's urine sent to him, and the method is this: He takes the ashes of a certain tree commonly known among us here in England—the ash tree—and mixes the urine with it. He then has his servant mold it into a paste, which is divided into lumps and shaped into 3, 7, or 9 balls. In the top of each ball, he makes a hole, places a blade of saffron into each hole, and then fills the hole with the urine. Next, he places these balls in a secret place where no one may disturb them. Immediately, the jaundice in the patient—whether they are far from or near to the medicine—will little by little fade and wear away. This experiment has been tried on over a hundred people, both poor and rich, many of whom were those physicians had given up on. Not only he, but also the noble ladies his daughters (who, for God’s sake, have helped many poor people in this way), affirm this to be true. 

And I can affirm this much myself: in the year 1637, I was called to the wife of a surgeon <note>original: "Chirurgion"</note> after other doctors had treated her with little success. She was severely infected with this disease. Having used some medicines to little purpose, at her request, I sent her servant into the country to that nobleman to ask for his help. But while the urine was being sent, the woman was persuaded by some "sincere fools" <note>Fludd likely refers to religious critics who viewed sympathetic magic as demonic or superstitious.</note> that it was witchcraft. This made her nearly mad and prone to raving, and she treated her servant harshly upon his return. Therefore, I immediately sent a messenger to ask his Lordship to undo what he had caused to be done because of the woman’s ingratitude. He sent me word that he would, but said, "It will be in vain, for it will cure her, no matter what I do now." And indeed, she improved immediately upon it. 

Also, there was a noble lady, the daughter of a lord, who was heavily infected with the same disease. Finding that usual medical remedies <note>original: "Physick"</note> did her little or no good, I sent her urine to the noble Earl, who did his best. But when I found that the disease still persisted, even though her urine improved in color, I rode there myself to inform that noble personage of the medicine’s small effect. He asked me to send it again. The sick lady sent her urine a second time and immediately began to improve; within a few days, she was perfectly well. There is another person who, to my knowledge, has cured forty people of this disease by boiling their urine away over a gentle fire—things (God knows) far removed from either superstition or witchcraft.
