### *Certain Problematic Demonstrations to confirm the probability of this Proposition.*

->1 Problem.<-

When the nails and hair of a sick person are taken and placed into a hole bored into an oak tree, and the oak is stopped up with a peg of the same wood, it cures an atrophic <note>original: "Atrophiaticall"; referring to a limb wasting away due to atrophy or lack of nourishment</note> or wasted limb, as has been proven before.

->Application.<-

And therefore, the effect is much greater with the serous <note>the thin, watery part of the blood</note> matter which is separated from the blood. This is because the essential "vegetable" <note>In this context, "vegetable" refers to the "vegetative soul" or the basic life-force that governs growth and nutrition</note> salt of the blood—within which are some sparks of life—is mingled with it. By virtue of these sparks, there is a continuous sympathy or connection between the salt and sulfur in the balls of ash and the infected blood in the patient. 

For (as I proved in the preceding chapter) the spirit in the urine is as continuous with the spirit in the blood as the spirit of the wounded man was with the blood on the weapon-salve ointment. Thus, through a continuity and a "union of consent" <note>a harmonious connection where two things act as one</note>, the curative power of the vegetable ashes operates spiritually upon the infected blood in the body just as it does upon the urine. This is the reason that as the salt in the ashes works on the salt in the urine, both of them communicate their forces by mutual consent to the blood because of that same continuity. Just as the virtue of the plant mixed with the saffron kills and poisons the infection in the urine, so also—by the mutual consent between the two infecting extremes, namely the blood and the urine—the infection in the blood is observed to gradually die, wither, and decay. But I will provide a magnetic Problem to confirm the possibility of this proposition.

->2 Problem.<-

Two loadstones <note>original: "Load-stones"; naturally magnetized minerals</note> properly joined at opposite poles will be disrupted by the arrival of a stronger loadstone or magnetized iron. The newcomer will easily drive away the other magnet which faces it with a contrary side, taking command over it, and so the connection or union of the original two will cease or end.

->Application.<-

In the same way, the union that was made between the infected spirit (with its corrupting fluids) and the corrupted blood is separated. That which is unnatural is forced to flee and depart from that which is natural by the help of another force which is more potent than the unnatural one. This stronger force is less homogeneous <note>less similar in nature to the disease</note> and is suited to rectify and purify the impurity in the natural blood by the union of its spirit, thereby killing and destroying the corrupter in the urine.

I do not need to say much more to prove this, as the preceding chapter fully confirms it by referring to the loadstone and the weather-glass in every part of this proposition. Just as blood is transplanted from a wounded person’s "fountain of blood" and, as it were, grafted onto the ointment, so also is the urine—containing bloody spirits—transferred from the "bloody fountain" in the jaundiced <note>original: "icteritious"</note> person and planted or placed in a bed of healing ashes. From there, it operates on the living blood no differently than the blood or spirits in the ointment do in the veins of a wounded person.

I will now proceed to the microcosmic magnet, which is taken out of the living man. I intend to describe to you briefly, and in general terms, the wonderful effects of sympathy which it produces by the extraction of the spiritual Mummy <note>a vital, spiritual essence or life-force thought to reside in the body and its waste products</note> out of the human body, and by its proper transplantation and application.

# CHAP. VIII.

*Wherein the secret Magnet, which is extracted from the Microcosm <note>original: "Microcosm"; the "little world," a traditional term for a human being as a miniature reflection of the universe</note>, or Man yet living, is mentioned in general terms; along with the manner of its attraction or extraction of the spiritual Mummy from man, its application, and its antipathetic as well as sympathetic operation.*

I will now in few words relate to you a history of the hidden manner of healing by transplantation. If it is rightly considered, it far surpasses that of the weapon-salve <note>original: "Weapon-salve"; a medicinal ointment applied to the weapon that caused a wound to heal the patient through sympathy</note>. For it does not only cure at a distance, as that does, but it performs that feat by the vegetative spirit of the plant. And yet I hope that my story shall in no way sound to wise men's ears as cacomagical <term>evil or "black" magic</term>, but only as naturally magical, and therefore ordained by God to be used in the right way for man's good and healthy benefit. For toward that end did the Spirit of Wisdom teach those who were inclined toward wisdom (as Solomon witnesses) both those things which are occult and hidden, as well as those that are manifest and apparent to man's senses. And because good things may, by abuse, be converted to evil and unlawful purposes—just as a sword can be used to kill as well as to save, as shall be told to you hereafter—therefore it is God's will that these mysteries should be hidden from the unlearned, or at least from those of the common people who are wickedly minded; He ordained them to be revealed to those who are honest, wise, and discreet. But leaving all preambles, I will come to the point and proceed with the same style and method in which I began.

## *The General Proposition.*

There may be extracted out of a living man, without any harm to his health, a Magnet which, by a specific application of it to convenient parts of the body, will draw or suck out (according to the pleasure of the applier) the animal, vital, or natural spiritual Mummy <term>a vital essence or life-force extracted from a living organism, used in Paracelsian medicine</term> out of one and the same living man. This is done without any detriment to his person. When that Mummy is rightly transplanted with the Magnet that absorbed it and made "vegetative" (growing), it will operate as well by internal administration as at a far distance, or by a spiritual emanating relationship. After it is duly ordered and adapted, it can serve both for health and preservation, or for infection, damage, and the destruction of mankind.

## *An Explication of every Member of this Proposition.*

This Proposition consists of many members: the first touches on the generation, condition, and preparation of the Magnet. The second concerns the manner of application for the extraction of the spiritual Mummy. The third opens the fashion of a manifold transplantation of that Mummy after it is extracted. and lastly, it covers both the uses and the abuses of it. Regarding all these articles or members, they follow in this order.

It may therefore easily be conjectured and guessed by those who are wise in their understanding what it is, by comparing the animal magnet with that of the mineral. For as the mineral magnet is not of a natural but a "monstrous" birth—for it is not fathered by like and equal parents, but is begotten in the manner of a mule—its mother (or passive physical mass) is a common Saturnine <note>original: "Saturnine"; associated with the planet Saturn and the metal lead; cold and heavy</note> and stony Mercury; but its father (or active form) is a metallic, sulfurous, Martial <note>original: "Martial"; associated with the planet Mars and the metal iron; fiery and active</note> spirit. So also this, our Microcosmic Magnet, consists of a sulfurous Martial spirit, being as it were its formal father; and of a strange or foreign Mercury, which is nevertheless a near neighbor in position and condition to the human Mercury, acting as its passive or mercurial matter. As for the mine from which it is extracted, it is the living man, and it is taken...

### The Method of Applying this Magnet to Extract the Spiritual Mummy

As for the manner of its application, it is this: we take the Magnet so prepared, and if we wish to extract the animal's mummial spirits, we must apply it to those places which are best suited for their evacuation. To conclude, if you would make a general medicine which should address the animal, vital, and natural parts all at once, then your Magnet must be applied to them all; and after it has sucked a sufficient proportion, then you ought to preserve it to perform your Transplantation.

### The Process of Transplanting the Spiritual Mummy

Regarding the act or manner of Transplantation: Paracelsus <note>original: "Paracelsus"; a Swiss physician and alchemist (1493–1541) who argued that the body has a natural healing power that can be manipulated through chemistry and sympathy</note> says that the extracted spiritual Mummy does not work toward health and preservation except by mineral, vegetable, and animal means. Therefore, it is necessary that the spiritual Mummy attracted or extracted out of the body by the power of the Animal Magnet must be introduced into a "vegetative nature" (a plant). By this, the Mummy—not being vegetative itself—may, by a kind of adoption, be introduced into and endowed with a vegetative nature or condition.

We ought, therefore, to mix a portion of this soaked Magnet with a certain proportion of its "mother-earth," and sow in this composition the seeds of such herbs as are proper for this or that disease, or for this or that poorly functioning principal part of man's body, or whichever infirm member is contained in his region. 

For example:
*   For the lungs in the vital region, when the disease is **tuberculosis** <note>original: "Ptisick" (phthisis); a wasting disease of the lungs</note>, sow **linseed** or **juniper**. 
*   In the natural region, when it is **dropsy** <note>original: "Dropsy"; an old term for edema, or swelling caused by excess fluid</note>, sow **pimpernel** or **wormwood**. 
*   For the bruising or crushing of parts, sow **St. John's Wort** <note>original: "Hypericon"</note> or **plantain**. 
*   For tumors or wounds, sow **smartweed** <note>original: "Persecaria"</note>, or the greater or lesser **comfrey**. 
*   In "salt diseases" <note>likely referring to diseases involving sharp pains or discharges</note> such as toothache, pain in the eyes, and heavy **menstruation** <note>original: "Menstrues"</note>, sow **spotted smartweed** <note>original: "Persecaria maculata"</note>, and so forth. 

The herbs must grow in this mixed earth, and do so in the open air. As the herb or plant grows, it will sympathetically and magnetically extract the soaked mummial spirits out of the Magnet. By that means, it will cause the Mummy extracted from every particular member, according to its condition, to be fit to cure the infirmity of its specific member.

2.  But if the disease is "moist," then you must burn the herb with the magnetic earth. 
3.  Again, if the disease is more temperate—namely, between the extremes of water and fire—then hang the herb in the air or in smoke to dry, and the disease will languish little by little as the herb fades.

# The Second Part of this Book, which handles the practice of Antipathy.

## CHAP. I.

*In this chapter, the author explains how the same internal spirit in a creature can produce both antipathetic and sympathetic effects. It also sets down the reason why a spirit infected and corrupted with a poisonous condition is most venomous and contagious to its own kind.*

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'A' featuring ornate floral patterns and a bird perched within the scrollwork.</image-desc>

As it is certain that like naturally affects its like—for nature rejoices at the presence of its own nature, and nature corrects and strengthens its own nature if it is sound and full of life-giving and wholesome spirits—so also nature, if it is poisoned and infected by a venomous nature, will quickly corrupt and defile <note>original: "inquinate"</note> a sound and wholesome nature by uniting with it. Through such an unnatural and depraved union, antipathy takes the place of sympathy. 

Now, I will briefly relate to you how this is possible in nature. Just as nature magnetically attracts its own like, if the "like" it draws in is defiled with corruption, the attracting spirit—no matter how sound it is—will quickly taste the bitter with the sweet (namely, the poison). Thus, it will become just as corrupt as the spirit to which it is naturally similar <note>original: "homogeneall"</note> and in which the infection lives. It is forced, unaware, to entertain strife, conflict, and antipathy in its own home <note>original: "tabernacle"</note>. 

We see this when a healthy spirit in an animal, thirsting for its natural spiritual food which hovers hiddenly in the air, draws in an enemy by mistake: a pestilent and corrupt vapor <note>original: "fume"</note>. This vapor oppresses and inflames the spirit with a rotting fire. The healthy spirit did not intend to draw in poison; it merely sought its own kind, which happened to be poisoned. 

Furthermore, every spirit burdened with any unnatural or repellent condition desires to shake off that conflict and return to the peaceful sympathy it enjoyed before. Finding itself unable to do so alone, it tends to cling to good and healthy spirits for relief, since "a united force is stronger" <note>original: "vis unita fortior"</note>. If more healthy spirits of its own kind were joined to it, it might more easily conquer and expel its adversary. 

We also see this in a "blear-eyed" person <note>At the time, it was believed that eye infections or "evil looks" could transmit disease through invisible beams or spirits emitted from the eyes.</note>. By casting their infectious beams toward another person for relief from a reasonable distance, they become like a flame that sets fire to the healthy spirit they encounter. Spiritual poisons are like the secret flames of a malignant fire. Therefore, as spirits are joined and multiplied through union—like oil added to oil—the infectious flame increases and feeds equally upon them both. Just as the sound spirit desires the company of its like for comfort, the corrupted spirit also desires the sound spirit to help it against its enemy. Thus, corruption is drawn in by both, and antipathy is forced to reside <note>original: "roust"</note> among them. It does not leave them until it has penetrated and gnawed into their very bowels and poisoned their innermost parts. We must note that no poisoned spirit takes hold of another spirit faster than one that is of the same species <note>original: "specifick"</note>, and...

<summary>This page concludes the discussion on sympathetic healing and introduces the concept of Antipathy, explaining how spiritual corruption and disease spread because spirits naturally seek out their "like," even when that "like" is infected.</summary>

Sect. 2. Mosaical Philosophy.

...and of a homogeneous <note>original: "homogeneal"; of the same kind or nature</note> nature. For that is the reason that one man's spirit, being infected with the Plague, multiplies it chiefly within its own kind; just as the murrain <note>a plague or infectious disease affecting domestic animals</note> rages chiefly in the spirits of sheep and does not meddle with the spirits of men. Do we not commonly see that a similar nature, when altered by decay, is most deadly to its own kind? Thus, worms expelled from the body and dried to powder will, by inward administration, kill worms. Spittle that is expelled from a person with lung disease <term>Pulmoniack</term> cures, after preparation, a wasting disease <term>Ptifick</term>. The prepared spleen of a man is an enemy to the swelling and growing <note>original: "vegetable"; referring to the growth-oriented "vegetative soul" in Early Modern biology</note> spleen. The stone of the kidney or bladder, through calcination <note>reducing a substance to powder by heat</note>, cures and dissolves the stone. The touch of a dead man's hand cures hard, fibrous tumors <term>schirrous</term>. The scorpion, being bruised or its body soaked in oil, cures the wounds of the scorpion; as does the oil of the viper—along with lozenges <note>original: "trochises"</note> made of its flesh—cure the bites of the adder or viper. Dead and congealed blood, and the salt growth from a man's bones, is naturally opposed to flowing blood. In conclusion, there is nothing more powerful to check or correct an impediment in a spirit than applying the same specific spirit that has been altered from its nature by a contrary force. 

So also, there is nothing that infects a sound nature sooner than a nature similar to itself which has been corrupted. That is the reason that the infirm and corrupted Mummy <note>In alchemical medicine, "Mummy" refers to the vital essence or "balsam" of a body, not necessarily an Egyptian corpse.</note> of one man is so apt to rot and corrupt the Mummy of another, as we may discern by these words of Paracelsus: <margin>*De Philof. Tract. 3.*</margin> "The corrupted Mummy also corrupts the sound body that it touches and joins with; and that corruption of the sound body is the health and wellness of the other body from which the Mummy was taken" <note>original Latin: *Corrupta Mummia, corpus etiam sanum quod attingit, & cum quo unitur, corrumpit; ea autem sani corporis corruptio, est corporis alterius, ex quo Mummia sumpta est, valetudo & sanitas*</note>. For example: If a man is leprous and I extract the Mummy from him using the Microcosmic Magnet <note>A Paracelsian term for the body's natural power to attract or repel vital spirits</note> and give it to a healthy man, it will return the leprous person to health; but it will foully infect the healthy man who took it with the same disease, as shall be explained to you later in more detail. 

But before we come to the core of this business, it is most fitting that I make an apologetic transition. I do this lest some people—having more envy and indiscretion than depth in true natural Magic <note>original: "Magia"</note>—unworthily accuse me of evil magic <term>Cacomagy</term>. They might do so only because they are altogether ignorant of the mysteries of those lawful acts in nature which were taught to Solomon and revealed to the wise men of this world for the benefit of mankind by the good Spirit of God. These acts are not to be avoided simply because evil men may convert them to evil effects and divert them from their true uses for which God ordained them. Rather, a skillful natural magician, such as a true physician ought to be, should first know the good uses of such hidden mysteries in nature so that they might employ them more effectively for the good of mankind; and then, they should not be ignorant of the abuses that may be produced by them, so they may better prevent and stop all such wicked effects that naughty men would produce to the damage and destruction of God's creatures.

->*other natural things, are to be known and well understood by the*<-

They are smothered, as it were, with the blind and foggy smoke of ignorance. They will say that if the sympathetic effects of the spiritual Mummy are allowable for a physician, the antipathetic properties are odious and in no way to be endured. Nay, they will say they are evil magic <term>Cacomagicall</term> because the devil instructs...

### Mosaicall Philosophy. Book 3.

...instruct his ministers about the abuses of this microcosmic <note>relating to the human body as a "little world"</note> kind of corruption; and therefore, for this reason, they claim the very knowledge of such a thing should not be introduced. These objections, I know, will these senseless and unreasonable babblers make regarding the knowledge of such a mystical business. But if their words were accepted by the wise, what would become of Solomon's skill in natural logic? Or why should he (who was esteemed the wisest among men) be so mistaken as to aspire to the knowledge of all things whatsoever, and to understand the enemies of man's nature as well as its friends? <margin>Wisdom 7</margin> For it is said of him that he knew the natures of living creatures, the fierceness of beasts, the thoughts of men, the differences of plants, the virtues of roots, and all other things that were occult <term>hidden or secret</term> and secret. 

Nay, why should he say that Wisdom, the mistress of all work, taught these things to him? Are there not plants, animals, and minerals that are pure poison and venomous to man's nature, as well as those that are benign and health-giving <note>original: "salutiferous"</note>? He knew (says the text) the natures of all living creatures or animals; and why so, if what those scoffers mutter were true? Why should he know or look after the properties of such things which are poisonous and harmful to mankind? Are there not the asp, the viper, the adder, and that decaying worm termed *Seps* in Latin, or *Pourrisseur* <note>original: "Purrifur"; French for "one who causes rot"</note> in French because of its rotting venom? Also the serpent called *Dipsas* <note>a legendary snake whose bite was said to cause intense thirst</note>, which infects the spirit with an immeasurable thirst; the *Amphisbaena*, the *Basilisk*, the *Dragon*, and the *Hollio*? Among creeping creatures, are there not the spider, the scorpion, the toad, the lizard, the salamander, the *Cantharides* <note>Spanish fly</note>, and an infinite number of other earthly and watery animals, venomous and wonderfully destructive to mankind? 

He also knew the differences and virtues of plants. But these reckless <note>original: "temerarious"</note> judges say: What reason had Wisdom to show and discover to him the abominable effects of the herb called **Aconite**? This plant is so destructive to man and beast that the poets imagined it grew along the shore of the venomous river **Acheron** in hell. Or **Hemlock**, which was the instrument of death among the Athenians (for with its juice they poisoned condemned persons)? Or **Henbane** <note>original: "Jusquiame"</note>, or the **Poppy**, from whose juice the sleep-inducing **Opium** is derived? Or the **Toadstool**, **Scammony**, **Euphorbium**, **Colocynth** <note>original: "Colloquintida"</note>, **Bears-foot**, **Spurge** <note>original: "Titimal"</note>, **Asarabacca**, **Groundsel** <note>original: "Grunfell"</note>, **Flammula**, and an infinity of such vegetables? Also among the minerals: **Antimony**, **Quicksilver** <note>mercury</note>, **Arsenic**, **Realgar** <note>original: "Rosalgar"; arsenic sulfide</note>, **Verdigris**, **Litharge**, **White Lead** <note>original: "Cerusse"</note>, **Vitriol**, and an infinity of others? 

My answer is: all these things, though in themselves they are venomous, yet being rightly handled and used by wise men, they are made extremely medicinal. And I would have them know that God created all things good; but it is the Devil and his instruments who, by employing them poorly, make them odious and detestable to man's nature. For just as by their right use and application they may produce sympathetic effects, so by their abuse they produce nothing but antipathetic actions and rebellious conflicts with man's nature. 

God, I say, ordained them for a good use, namely for man's health; but the Devil applies them destructively and maliciously, <margin>Wisdom 1:14, 2:23</margin> which the aforementioned wise natural magician, Solomon, also confirms in these words: *God created all things that they should exist and be; and he made all the nations of the Earth sound and durable, so that there was not a destructive medicine in them. Also God created man to be immortal; but it was by the malice of the Devil that death entered into the world. And the wicked imitate him and are of his seed.* 

By this it is plain that it was the Devil and wicked men—who are his instruments and indeed true devils incarnate—who adapt for a wicked use that which is indeed good and righteous in itself. What more shall I say? Because the Devil applies a good thing to a bad use, must that thing forever be abhorred and avoided by wise men? And must, for that reason, the good use of it be excommunicated from human society and forever after be reputed as **Cacomagical** <term>pertaining to evil magic</term>, damnable, and diabolical? 

As for example: because the Devil and his adherents—I mean witches and necromancers—apply the **Mummy** <note>a medicinal preparation made from the remains or the vital essence of a human body</note> of man, both physical and spiritual, toward their pernicious and destructive inventions, must all those who use the same for a good and health-giving intent be esteemed as evil magicians? Is it a sign that the physician who cures diseases by it has, for that reason, a commerce with the Devil? Or must a Christian physician, because he is acquainted with...

Sect. 2. Mosaicall Philosophy.

Does it follow that because a person knows the evil that natural things can cause through an unnatural or incompatible <note>original: "antipatheticall"</note> application, they must put that evil into practice to harm someone's health? Truly, if things are considered correctly, the knowledge of both the good and evil within creatures is well-suited to the science of a physician. Unless he is acquainted with the evil as well as the good, how is it possible to cure the harms caused by the bad? For unless the cause is known, the effect will hardly ever be cured.

As for example, if the nature of the spiritual "potion" <note>original: "philtre"</note> that infects someone is not discovered, how can a cure be performed, or the cause be extinguished and removed? The true magician <note>In this context, Fludd refers to a "natural magician" or a scientist who studies the hidden forces of nature.</note> does not study the venomous nature of simple plants or substances <term>Simples: medicinal herbs or single-ingredient drugs</term> to do harm with them, but to discern the counter-poison that should prevent the mischief they cause. Just as the scorpion cures the scorpion's sting, and the viper cures the viper's harms. Must every man who has a sword necessarily kill or do mischief with it? May he not use it to defend another from being killed or harmed? 

So also it does not follow that a physician must poison his patient simply because he knows the poison and the manner in which to correct or fix its malice, which has deprived his patient of health. Unless the poison is known, the *Alexipharmicon* <note>original: "Alexipharmicon"; a Greek term for a remedy against poison or infection</note> or counter-poison will hardly be found. If the Hermit of *Aix* (whom I mentioned before) had not known the specific antidote to cure those he had poisoned and infected with the plague, many of those he later cured would have died with the rest. 

If there are "devils in the flesh" <note>original: "devills incarnate"</note> whose delight is to destroy—just as some men who wear swords delight in quarreling and killing, and others who know the good use of fire employ it wickedly (like the man who destroyed *Diana's* temple at *Ephesus* with it)—God forbid that such natural things as fire and iron should be abandoned or not used correctly because they cause harm when abused. There are saints on earth as well as devils; these saints, being familiar with the wicked inventions and devices of these devils and their master, *Satan*, are able to challenge and combat them with their own weapons. 

Scholars learn the art of sophistry and fallacy from *Aristotle*, not so that they should deceive, but so they can prevent deceit. Likewise, the honest, most skillful, and faithful physician peers into the mystery of the most spiritual poison, not with the intent to poison or do evil, but so that he may attempt the cure with greater assurance and vigorous effectiveness once the cause is known; for when the nature of the poison is well understood, the cure will be more certain. The venomous wound of the viper (as I have said) is cured by the *Theriac* antidote <note>original: "Theriacall"; an ancient herbal compound used as a universal antitoxin, often containing viper flesh</note>, which includes the flesh of vipers in its composition. The oil of scorpions, or even a crushed scorpion itself, cures a scorpion's sting through a magnetic attraction to its own kind. 

Since all this is true, why should the wise physician not look into the nature of spiritual venoms as well as the spiritual counter-poisons that exist in humanity? For we find that the venom that wounds is—by reason of its shared nature—the most perfect magnet to suck and draw its likeness toward it. If I can cure or remove corruption or venom with the healthy "Mummy" <term>Mummy: in Paracelsian medicine, the vital life force or spiritual essence believed to reside in the human body</term> in a person, because its shared nature has accidentally absorbed it, is it not appropriate to know the one as well as the other?

I must confess that there are "devils in the flesh" on earth—I mean abominable ministers and children of Satan—who, having abandoned themselves to their master and head, commit (as I have told you before) many insults and treacherous plots using the blood, hair, bones, skin, and physical Mummy of the human body. But above all, the wickedness of certain thieves, executioners, and others of that necromantic faction is abominable before God and man. They deserve to be whipped out with iron or wiped away with fire from every good commonwealth. By their diabolical tricks, they use a person's last breath as they die to serve their wicked goals, as if these spirits were made obedient to their wills, thus disturbing the quiet rest of the dying person's spirit. Regarding these kinds of wicked persons, *Paracelsus* speaks thus:

<margin>Concerning the Treatise of Philosophy, 1.</margin> 
> "Through these three types of Mummies, many things have been performed and accomplished everywhere, especially by those who prepared them themselves, such as executioners, bailiffs, thieves, and so on. These individuals have not only taken life from men and turned those whose throats were cut into 'Mummy,' but they also captured the spirit of the slain—which they called the human spirit. They subjected or enslaved that spirit to themselves at the final moment of death and tormented it with various burdens. From this, the art of Necromancy was born." <note>original Latin: "Per triplices hasce Mummias multa passim præstita & confecta sunt... Hinc ars enata est Necromantia"</note>

### CHAP. III.

->How Sympathy may by accident or disorder be changed into Antipathy. Here also certain magnetic demonstrations, convenient to prove each Proposition concerning this subject, are expressed.<-

I purpose in this Chapter, which touches the effects of Antipathy, to proceed after the same method which I observed in my preceding discourse on Sympathy. Therefore, in the first place, I will propose to you certain grounds, which for that reason I call Propositions; and then afterward I will demonstratively maintain them in many ways.

### 1 Proposition.

->As by sympathy in natural spirits, each member may be corroborated and fortified; so by their antipathy, members may be debilitated, corrupted, and infected.<-

### An experimental Example or Demonstration.

<margin>#</margin>
If the spiritual Mummy extracted out of man is mingled with venomous things and so allowed to rot, or else is mingled with the Mummies of sick or infected persons, or with the poisonous menstrual blood <note>original: "menstrues"</note> of a woman, and then a herb is planted, or the magnet so soaked <note>original: "imbibed"</note>, and is preserved in a continual state of growth <term>vegetation: the process of growing or being maintained in a living state</term>, it may be a cause for the disease to continue. 

Also, if one gives the herb or fruit which tastes of a sick man's Mummy to a beast that is of a stronger nature than the sick person, then the beast will be infected with that disease, and the sick person will be free of it. From this experiment, many terrible <note>original: "egregious"</note> abuses could and would be carried out by wicked men if this manner of diverting the creature's virtue from good to bad were known to them; for by it, they may spread fevers <note>original: "agues"</note> and the plague <note>original: "pestilence"</note> over a whole country. For the plant will suck out the spiritual Mummy of such persons as are infected with such venomous diseases, because of its growing activity.

<margin>#</margin>
Also, if the spiritual Mummy is extracted by means of this microcosmic magnet <note>A "microcosmic magnet" refers to a substance or device intended to attract the human vital spirit, reflecting the human as a "microcosm" or miniature world.</note> out of a body infected with leprosy, and is applied or in any way administered internally to another person who is healthy and sound, it will infect the healthy person and cure the infected one, as has been proven by some.

### 2nd Proposition.

The antipathetic <term>antipathetic: based on a natural repulsion or opposition between things</term> "Mummy" <note>original: "Mummy" – in early modern medicine, this refers to the vital essence or physical remains of a human body used in treatments</note> of a sick person may be extracted and then infected or infused into another person who is healthy.

->*A demonstrative Example.*<-

This is confirmed by the previous proofs and is further maintained as follows. If someone sows seeds or herbs related to the three principal organs <note>likely the heart, liver, and brain</note> in the Mummy of a dead corpse, or in the Mummy extracted from a sick or infected person, and the fruit of these plants is then given to a person or animal, the disease will be transplanted onto that person or animal. By this method, wicked men may also infect and poison others. However, because these evils are horrific to a religious soul, I dare not further describe the effects of antipathy in spirits, which can be achieved by the abuse of God’s blessings. I will therefore move to another kind of antipathetic practice, which focuses on the preservation of humanity rather than its destruction.

### 3rd Proposition.

If two pieces of living flesh that are wounded are applied to each other, they will sympathize and be united, assimilated, and made into one continuous piece of flesh. As one prospers, the other will do the same—provided that the person from whom the added flesh was borrowed remains in a healthy and "vegetable" <note>original: "vegetable" – here referring to the biological power of growth and life, the "vegetative soul"</note> state. But if the "animal tree" from which the graft was taken—meaning the body from which the flesh was lent or cut—withers or dies (that is, it ceases to grow and act), then that borrowed flesh will also fall into discord and conflict with the living flesh of the borrower. Consequently, "antipathy" will spring out from that union which was previously "sympathetic." Unless the dying flesh is amputated or removed from the living flesh on which it was grafted, it will cause the living flesh to gangrene and decay along with it.

->*An experiment to confirm this.*<-

This is well-proven and supported by that experiment in Italy mentioned previously. When a certain nobleman had lost his nose in a wound, he followed a physician's advice and made a wound in the arm of one of his slaves. He then pressed the arm against his wounded nose so that the flesh of both was bound fast together. They remained in this state until, through a sympathetic bonding and union, both pieces of flesh became one. Then, a piece <note>original: "gobbit"</note> of the slave's flesh was cut out of the arm and shaped into a nose for the nobleman; the slave was then freed <term>manumitted: released from slavery</term> and given money for his trouble. It happened some time later that the slave died. Although he passed away far from his master, the borrowed flesh on the master’s nose withered and turned gangrenous. The antipathy between these two pieces of flesh, though united into one substance, became so great that if the dead flesh had not been immediately cut off, it would have corrupted and destroyed the rest of the nobleman's face.

->*A Problematic Demonstration from the Loadstone.*<-

One loadstone <term>loadstone: a naturally magnetic mineral</term> attracts another when in its natural position, but when positioned unnaturally, it drives away or resists the other. The proof of this problem has been demonstrated using a loadstone divided in small boats, as well as by two pieces of iron floating on corks.

### The Application.

So, if the spirits of the two pieces of flesh are unnaturally inclined toward each other and turned from their sympathetic union into an antipathetic duality or separation—a discord in their natures—then, after some unequal clashes, general corruption will follow. For, as was said before, *the corrupted thing most easily takes on the nature of the corrupter* <note>original: "Corruptum corrumpentis naturam facillime induit"</note>.

### 4 Problem.

If a spiritual Mummy <note>original: "Mummy"—here referring to the vital life force or balsamic essence of a living person</note> is corrupted by some foreign or strange infectious nature, yet in comparison to the natural Mummy of the healthy and wholesome body that is infected, the healthy Mummy of a body that is *not* infected will magnetically attract it. However, it will do so less affectionately and more slowly because of the strange venom clinging to it, which causes a mixture of antipathy <term>antipathy: a natural repulsion or opposition</term> with sympathy. 

The reason for that slowness in repelling the antipathetic attack is that the healthy and uniform <note>original: "homogeniall"</note> Mummy partly attracts its sympathetic "like" through its "desiring" faculty <term>concupiscible: the power of the soul to seek out what it perceives as good</term>, and partly expels its contaminating "unlike" through its "defensive" property <term>iraſcible: the power of the soul to resist or avoid harm</term>. But because this antipathetic "unlike" substance clings so tightly to the infected "like" substance, the resistance and expulsion happen only slowly. Thus, the healthy spiritual Mummy becomes as corrupted and infected as the other, and by that means, sympathy is turned into antipathy.

### An Experiment to confirm this.

There are many proofs to support this. For instance, when a corrupted spiritual Mummy is carried through the air from someone infected with a pestilent fever or smallpox, the infected Mummy—being of a similar nature <note>original: "homogeniall"</note>—unites itself with the healthy person’s spirit, and in that regard, they embrace each other. 

But the healthy Mummial spirit, sensing and tasting the different <note>original: "heterogeniall"</note> or infected nature clinging to its "like," slowly expels or resists it. This is because it both desires its like (and thus attracts it through sympathy) and hates its unlike (and thus expels it through antipathy). This process is performed slowly, which is why the "expulsive crisis" <note>original: "expulsive crisis"—the critical moment in a disease when the body attempts to throw off the infection</note> does not happen immediately after the poisonous infection is received. Nor will sweats, fluxes, or nosebleeds—which are signs of the resistance and expulsive power of contagious antipathy—suddenly appear. This outcome is achieved sometimes by the healthy spirit’s victory and sometimes by its failed attempt.

This is because the magnet affects and draws its "like" or best-beloved most strongly when the object is not weighed down or mixed with materials of a contrary nature that do not agree in sympathy with it.

### 2nd Problem.

Experience teaches that magnetic bodies are repelled more sluggishly than they are allured or drawn toward one another. For that reason, the healthy Mummy strives to be divorced from the infected one. This is proved by this practical demonstration drawn from the properties of the lodestone.

I could, judicious reader, have written a whole volume of experimental propositions with their logical proofs regarding the infinite abyss of sympathetic and antipathetic effects in the three kingdoms—namely, Animal, Vegetable, and Mineral. I imagine, and my mind suggests to me, that no matter how careful I am in my writing or how much effort I put into my phrasing, my best endeavors will still appear faulty in the picky eyes of some men, though perhaps they will be acceptable enough to others. 

I consider it sufficient, therefore, that I dare to be bold regarding the fundamental subject of essential philosophy, given that it has Truth itself to maintain and defend it, without needing any decoration from the gilded tresses of superficial speeches or verbal explanations. ### CHAPTER VII.
*That God (contrary to Aristotle's assertion, and the opinion of various other pagan <note>original: "Ethnick"</note> philosophers) does not act out of necessity for the creation and continuation of His creatures, but by His own will and benign inclination.*

We properly term that "Necessary" which can be no other way; on the other hand, we consider something as much "voluntary" as "fortuitous" (happening by chance) if it could have happened differently. Now, a great dispute has arisen and sprung up among the pagan <note>original: "Ethnick"</note> philosophers regarding whether God acts in this world voluntarily, or out of necessity, or as if by compulsion. The greater part of them are firmly of the opinion that God acts in this world—both in the generation and preservation of things, as well as their decay <note>original: "corruption"</note>—by necessity, and not by any voluntary motion. By this logic, it must follow that He was forced to do or effect what He does from all eternity by some other nature which was either co-eternal with Him or existed before Him; or else that He was stirred or pushed forward against His will to create this or that by some creature which He Himself made.

I will expressed to you in few words how erroneous and far-removed from the center of truth all of this is. For first of all, what (I ask you) is of greater antiquity than God, since He existed before anything else? In geometry, what comes before a point, or what is smaller in measure? Or which among all the numbers of arithmetic has as ancient a standing as the number one <note>original: "unity"</note>? Therefore, it must follow that God is free and voluntary in His actions, since He existed of Himself without regard for any other principle—whether preceding or co-eternal—from the very beginning. He was therefore sufficient in Himself, and of Himself, to work and act by Himself from all eternity.

<margin>1. Johannes Velcurio, Book 1, Chapter 5, Commentary on Physics.</margin>

But the principal reasons for the aforementioned pagan opinion are two-fold: first, because God acts and operates by His own essence and not by any acquired power <note>original: "vertue"</note>; and second, because the effects in the world seem to be necessary. From this, they conclude that these effects cannot come or proceed from any "contingent"—that is to say, accidental or voluntary—cause. 

Regarding the first point, it seems to me they argue against themselves; for as He acts by His own essence or substance, it is evident that He is moved of His own accord, and consequently not by any external compulsion or internal necessity. Moreover, within the expanse of the One <note>original: "unity"</note>, there can be no compulsion or forced action, because the One cannot be acted upon <note>original: "Unity cannot suffer"</note>. Again, it is not possible that He should be urged to work by any external or foreign efficient cause; because, remaining primarily fixed and steadfast in Himself and of Himself, He works as the original fountain of all things by Himself, emitting His formal...

### The fifth Book of this present Section.

#### The Argument of this Book.

After the author had expressed the original nature of the two essential properties, namely Heat and Cold, and had proved their main effects to be Rarefaction and Condensation—by which the Heavens and Elements were framed—he now proceeds in this book to the mystery of meteorological impressions <note>atmospheric phenomena like rain, wind, and clouds</note>, which are the first degree of composition. He shows that their structure is the act of the Divine Spirit, carried out in the universal <note>original: "catholick"</note> element of the world's lower region. Consequently, they do not proceed from such accidental and external grounds or beginnings as the Peripatetics <note>followers of Aristotle</note> falsely suspect. For this reason, he has compared the meteorological doctrine of Aristotle with that of the Holy Scripture. Finally, by bringing the pagan philosophy concerning these airy impressions to the Lydian trial <note>a test of purity; a touchstone</note> of Truth, he finds them to be false, counterfeit metal—indeed, mere dross <note>waste material or impurities</note> in comparison to the golden Truth.

He acts first through his angelic instruments <note>original: "Organs"</note>, then by the stars—especially the sun in heaven above—and the winds beneath, upon the general sublunary <note>below the moon; earthly</note> waters or elements. # ## Sect. I.
# ### Mosaical Philosophy.

...which are seen in the air, are called *Meteors* <note>original: *Meteora*</note> by the Greeks, not because of their natural essences, but because of the highness of their position. Others term them more naturally "Impressions," because they are shaped and imprinted above in the universal <note>original: "catholick"</note> element called Air.

But in respect to their essential consistency, they are properly called "bodies that are imperfectly mixed or compounded" <note>original: *Corpora imperfectè mixta aut compofita*</note>. This is either because of their unexpected generation—since they are produced and appear suddenly and with little warning—or else because their composition does not appear to happen according to a change of substance or alteration of quality. Or, it may be because they are not as precisely composed as other living <note>original: "animated"</note> bodies which are perfectly mixed. Lastly, these impressions are so named because they have not attained any perfect form; nor does there seem to be in this kind of composition any great alteration of parts, seeing that the members of the element so altered are confused with one another. 

Regardless, it appears that such names are assigned to this kind of impression according to the fancy or whim of this or that philosopher, when in truth they are the "great works of God" <note>original: *magnalia Dei*</note>. I mean to say, they are a mystical body framed and fashioned by the finger of God out of the depths of the universal earthly <note>original: "catholick sublunary"</note> element to carry out His will upon the earth, for either judgment or mercy, as shall be more fully expressed hereafter. So, in this sense, they may rightly be termed the characters or signs of God’s kindness and mercy, or His vengeance and severity upon the earth. 

My purpose, therefore, in this report on meteors <note>original: "Meteorologicall relation"</note> is to direct you into the path of true wisdom, so you may better analyze and decipher such a great mystery as the meteorological act of the Spirit of God. By that means, I hope to lead you out of the mire and puddle of pagan <note>original: "Ethnick"</note> philosophy, in which we Christians—even to our everlasting shame—stick fast and, like brutish pigs, willingly wallow. To achieve this better, I will compare the absurdities of the false Aristotelian <note>original: "Peripateticall"</note> philosophy with the infallible truth of the Holy Text. Thus, every Christian, weighing the contradictions between the two in the balance of justice, may open their intellectual eyes and sincerely follow what is good and forsake the bad. They may betake themselves to the truth and fly from that which is deceptive <note>original: "prestigious"</note> and false, and may by that means at last discern with open eyes the main difference between the wisdom and philosophy of this world—which in truth is mere foolishness <margin>(for the Spirit of God has pronounced it so)</margin>—and that of God, which is the real and essential truth. 

Thus, you may discern in a few words the manner and order of my method in this book. I do not intend to be overly tedious to you, but to briefly finish this wisdom regarding meteors, which, because of its own worth, deserves to be recorded in an everlasting monument of a much larger volume, and to be polished or burnished over with the luster of a more elegant style and refined manner of speech.

## Mosaicall Philosophy.
### Book 5.

I will express what the pagan Peripatetics <note>original: "Peripateticks"; followers of the philosophy of Aristotle, who walked while teaching</note>, and their Christian followers, have determined and do determine concerning them.

The Peripatetic philosophers are of the opinion that the wind is a hot and dry exhalation, being difficult to ignite, which arises out of the earth and soars up into the middle region of the air. From there, it is immediately repelled downwards by reason of the coldness of that region; and as it strives upward again, partly due to its lightness and partly because of other ascending exhalations it meets in its violent and forced descent, it moves laterally in the lower region of the air. It ventilates and agitates this air so that, for want of motion or stirring, it should not putrefy <note>original: "putrifie"; rot or become stagnant</note>. This is the sum of their opinion concerning the generation of the winds. I will therefore insist upon this Peripatetic or Aristotelian definition, or rather description, of the winds.

First, because the false Christian philosophers, as if they were incited by a kind of unbridled madness, do not hesitate to defend and, by their best endeavors, uphold this opinion in their public schools and private studies, as well as in their writings. They do this with such assured obstinacy as if it had been divinely revealed to the world, or pronounced by the sacred Oracle of truth itself.

Secondly, because the place where this imaginary exhalation is said to be engendered, and from which it is derived, is considered by them to be the earth; and the seat to which it desires <note>original: "coveteth"</note> to ascend is (according to their doctrine) the middle region of the air. Due to the cold temperature there, it is not permitted to enter or penetrate, but the medium or mean <gloss>forth</gloss> in which it moves naturally upward—and by compulsion or against nature, downwards; and lastly, by jostling or struggling together with other ascending exhalations and the forcibly descending fumes laterally (that is to say, toward the right or left hand)—is the lower region of the air.

Thirdly, because they seem to assert, as it appears by this definition, that the agent, mover, or efficient cause of this exhalation—both downwards and laterally—is double or twofold. Namely, the cold of the middle region of the air, which forces and presses downwards toward the earth that scarcely imaginable fume; and the other is the troop of other ascending exhalations, or subtle smokes, which successively rise out of the earth. These, in their motion upwards, meet with that fume which is forced to descend, and they strive and, as it were, wrestle with it; consequently, by that means, they make a noise in the air which is called the Wind. And this is the Peripatetic philosopher’s windy fiction, which in the conclusion, after a due examination, will prove to be but a bubble, or vain puff of wind; that is to say, merely words without any substance. Now the final end or cause why their nature has ordained these windy motions in the air is (as their definition testifies) that by this manner of ventilation, the air may be preserved, cleared, and purged from all putrefaction and corrupt disposition. But whoever will give credit to this ethnic <note>original: "Ethnick"; pagan or non-Christian</note> definition, especially if he is a true lover of wisdom, I counsel him first to examine every particular part of it, and having made a diligent inquiry therein, let him see and discern whether they agree with the laws of true reason and wisdom.

In the first rank and order, therefore, let us mark or observe whether in the former part of his description there is any probability of truth to be found. By it, we are told and taught that the material substance of the wind is a hot and dry exhalation, arising and surging out of the earth. But by Holy Scripture (which all true Christians ought to believe before all things), we are taught that the wind has its original or beginning from the *Spirit or breath of JEHOVAH*. <margin>Exod. 15.8.</margin> *By the blast of your nostrils* (says Moses) *the waters were gathered together; you blew with your wind and the sea covered them* <note>original Latin: "A flatu narium tuorum coacervata sunt aquæ, flavisti vento tuo & aperuit eos mare"</note>. And Job, <margin>Job. 37.10. 28.25.</margin> *God brings forth the ice by his breath; when he blows, the frost and ice are created* <note>original Latin: "Glaciem edit Deus vento suo, flante Deo concrescit gelu"</note>. *God gives weight to the wind* <note>original Latin: "Deus facit pondus vento"</note>. And the Prophet David, <margin>Pfal. 104.4.</margin> *Who makes his angels winds, and his ministers flames of fire* <note>original Latin: "Qui facit angelos ventos, & miniſtros flames of fire"</note>. And hereupon such learned personages and Doctors, as are profoundly experienced and have dived into the mysteries of true nature, do aver that the external part of the Angels is air, or the subtle humid nature of the world; and that their internal or formal portion is a hidden divine fire. And for this cause, St. Denis <note>Dionysius the Areopagite, a Christian theologian and philosopher</note> calls the Angels,

angels, *Agamasha*, <note>original: "Agamafha"; likely referring to a Hebrew or mystical term for angelic "mirrors" of divine light</note> that is to say, clear mirrors or looking-glasses, which receive the splendor or light of God and represent his image. And therefore the Prophet, in the place mentioned above, describes both the hidden and invisible wind and that which is fiery—which manifestly appears in the form of lightning—to be an angelic spirit, animated by the divine fire or bright emanation from God. All this being rightly considered, we must either confess that the "Spirit of the nostrils" or "mouth of Jehovah" is a hot and dry exhalation, subject to preternatural passions and arising out of the earth (which would appear too profanely uttered out of a Christian's mouth), or that this member of the <term>Peripatetical definition</term> <note>referring to the Aristotelian school of philosophy</note> is most false and erroneous. But this shall be discovered more plainly in my inquiry and laying open of the other parts.

The second member of this definition suggests to us that the place where that exhalation (the material cause of the wind) is engendered and derived from is the earth; but the place or seat toward which it tends (it says) is the middle region of the air; and the medium and space in which it moves—upward, downward, and laterally—is the lower region of the air. In this assertion by this <term>Ethnic Philosopher</term> <note>original: "Ethnick Philofopher"; referring to the pagan philosopher Aristotle</note>, I will make plain and prove evidently that various gross errors and palpable absurdities will be found. But so that we may better conduct our inquiry and hunt after the truth of the matter—for the sake of a more exact examination—it will be necessary for us to divide this clause into three parts. In the first, we ought seriously to consider whether the matter of the winds is extracted out of the earth or not. In the second, whether that substance only soars up and makes its way to the concave surface of the middle region of the air alone. In the third, whether the place in which the wind moves is only the lower region of the air. 

To the first question or doubt we say: either the sacred Bible (which is the fountain of truth) is false, or this part of the second member must be most erroneous. For, Saint John says, <margin>John 3:8</margin> *Spiritus ubi vult spirat, & vocem ejus audis, sed nescis unde veniat, aut quo vadat*: "The wind (or spirit) blows where it wills, and you hear its voice, but you do not know from where it comes or where it goes" <note>original Latin: *Spiritus ubi vult spirat, & vocem ejus audis, sed nescis unde veniat, aut quo vadat*</note>. When this is rightly pondered by wise men, they must conclude that either Aristotle saw further into the mysteries of God and nature than the Evangelist—who was a true and sincere Christian philosopher and <term>theosopher</term> <note>one who achieves knowledge of God through spiritual ecstasy or direct intuition</note>, and then Saint John must be proved a liar in his doctrine, which would be a great impiety for any Christian to imagine—or else the assertion of Aristotle must clearly be found false and in all things contradictory to the truth. 

Aristotle says that the matter of the wind moves from the earth and ascends into the middle region of the air, and from there is repelled downward. But Saint John says that the wind moves not by constraint—that is to say, by force or any accidental compulsion—but voluntarily, and according to its own pleasure and appetite. For his words are, *Spiritus spirat ubi vult*: "it blows where it wills." And although the voice and noise of it are familiar to the ears, yet nevertheless it is not known from where it comes or where it goes. 

This doctrine of the Evangelist, which differs so greatly from that of Aristotle, is maintained in various places of Holy Writ. For the royal Psalmist, along with the Prophet Jeremiah, says, <margin>Psalm 135:7, Jerem. 51:15</margin> *Depromit ventos è thesauris suis*: "He draws forth the winds out of his treasures" <note>original Latin: *Depromit ventos è thefauris fuis*</note>. But the Scriptures prove that the earth is not the seat or place of God’s treasure, where it says: <margin>Deut. 28:12</margin> *Aperiet tibi JEHOVAH thesaurum suum optimum, cœlo, dando pluviam terræ suo tempore*: "Jehovah will open to you his best treasure, the heavens, giving rain to the earth in its due time" <note>original Latin: *Aperiet tibi JEHOVAH thefaurum fuum optimum, cœlo, dando pluviam terræ fuo tempore*</note>. He does not say the earth, but the heavens; so between these two there is as great a difference as between night and day. 

Therefore it is evident that the heaven, or the universal element of air, is the secret cabinet of these *meteorologica Dei magnalia*, or "great meteorological wonders of God" <note>original Latin: *meteorologica Dei magnalia*</note>. Because of this, it is said in another place, <margin>Psalm 78:24-26</margin> *Jannas cœlorum aperuit plenus Manna, etc.*: "He opened the gates of heaven," raining down Manna <note>original Latin: *Jannas cœlorum aperuit plenus Manna*</note>. Again, it is so hard a thing for a mortal man who is not illuminated with the spirit of wisdom to find out or discover this hidden treasury of God, that Jehovah himself speaks to Job—though he was a just man and one who feared God, and even more so He points this at the wise man or philosopher of this world, who never was acquainted with the divine Word—in this manner: <margin>Job 38:22</margin> *Pervenisti ne in thesauros nivis, & in thesauros grandinis inspexisti non haber?*: "Have you entered into the treasures of the snow, or have you any insight into the treasury of the hail?" <note>original Latin: *Pervenisti ne in thefauros nivis, & in thefauros grandinis infpexifti non haber?*</note>. This argues that man could not know these things unless His Spirit had shown or revealed His treasury.

Using scriptural evidence from John, Psalms, and Job, the text asserts that weather phenomena are voluntary acts of God rather than mechanical processes of the earth.</summary>

treasury, it was impossible to know it. And for this reason, Solomon says, <margin>Wisdom 9:15</margin> "The body, which is subject to corruption, burdens and weighs down the soul; and we hardly conjecture or guess at those things which are upon the earth. Who has found out or discovered the things which are in heaven, unless you give and bestow wisdom upon him?" <note>original Latin: *Corpus infectum corruptione aggravat animam, & vix confpicimus ea quæ in terra funt: quæ autem in cœlis funt quis inveftigavit, nifi tu dederis fapientiam*?</note>

Now Solomon confesses that he knew the force of the elements and the power of the winds, and consequently their real origin or beginning; for, he says, "Wisdom, the worker of all things, taught me." <note>original Latin: *Sapientia omnium artifex me docuit*</note> <margin>Wisdom 7:17</margin> However, Aristotle’s false philosophy and his ethnic <note>original: "Ethnick"; meaning pagan or non-Christian</note> and worldly wisdom show that he never attained the wisdom which descends from above, even from the Father of Light. 

But to proceed to the doubt, which is: whether, according to Aristotle’s intention, the original matter of the wind is from the earth, and its first motion is from the earth into heaven? A man much more learned and wise in the mysteries of nature than Aristotle ever was answers in this manner: <margin>Ecclesiastes 11:5</margin> "Man does not know the way or path of the winds; man does not know the work of God—namely, by what means He effects all these things." <note>original Latin: *Venti viam ignorat homo, ignorat homo opus ipfius Dei, qua via faciat hæc omnia*</note>

But Aristotle was a man—yes, and a pagan man—and therefore he could judge all the less rightly about such abstruse things as these. Therefore, JEHOVAH, appearing to deride the boldness of such a worldling and, as it were, reprimanding him, speaks in these words: <margin>Job 38:24</margin> "Do you know where the way is in which the exhalation is divided, which spreads the wind upon the earth?" <note>original Latin: *Nosti ne ubinam sit via, in qua dividitur exhalatio quæ spargit ventum fuper terram*?</note>

He argues from this the impossibility for a worldly man's capacity to conceive or understand these things unless he is taught and instructed by the Spirit of Wisdom, who teaches all things; this Spirit is bestowed by God on whomever He pleases. And yet Aristotle seems impudently to answer God and say, "I know it well; for the path of this exhalation is from the earth upward to the middle region of the air. There—partly by an <term>antiperistasis</term> <note>A philosophical concept where a quality is intensified by being surrounded by its opposite, such as heat being intensified by surrounding cold</note> caused by cold driving it downward again, and partly by other exhalations which are successively ascending—the exhalation is compelled to move sideways across the face of the earth," etc. 

But I will show the impossibility of this reasoning by what follows immediately hereafter. Regarding the second and third parts of this clause, I say that the medium by which the winds are carried or moved is far more vast and large than what Aristotle assigns to it; for the wind does not blow and act only in the lower region, but also in the middle and even in the upper region of the air. If, therefore, the wind blows in the middle region of the air, then the strength of Aristotle’s definition will be removed. This is because the effectiveness of his argument depends chiefly on this: that a hot and dry exhalation (which is the cause of wind) is not allowed to penetrate the middle region of the air but is instead reflected, precipitated, and beaten down again by the power of the middle region’s cold, which resists the heat of the rising exhalation. 

Now, if there is any wind in the middle region of the air, this cause of the wind will be invalidated. In that case, the exhalation would not be repelled downward into the lower region, where it would meet other ascending exhalations to make a noise and be dispersed sideways across the earth. For the exhalation which causes a wind in the middle region will not be driven down by the cold, but is observed to blow and to move the clouds and thunders in the center of that sphere. 

Indeed, it is made clear by daily experience that the upper or higher clouds (which are white and yellow, and therefore lighter and more subtle because of their fiery brightness) as well as the lower clouds (which are thicker and darker) are driven and pushed by the winds from any quarter of the world to the opposite. Unless the winds were also present in that higher region, those clouds could never move "on the wings of the wind" in such a manner. 

Do we not also observe that the wind blows from one quarter <note>original: "fourth horn horizon," likely referring to the four "horns" or corners of the compass</note> of the horizon, and another from the next (which is northern), so that both winds have dominion in both horizons at the exact same time? Consequently, it often happens that great and dark clouds, moving from opposite quarters by the power of four of those contrary angelic spirits, meet at a point in the horizon. They form one mass or huge sea of clouds, serving as a <term>tabernacle</term> <note>a dwelling place or tent</note> for the great Spirit of wonders who works or causes these things. From this follows great lightning and thunder, caused by the meeting of opposite angelic natures—who are the messengers, ministers, and voice of the Almighty—which never could have been...

### Sect. 1.
## Mosaical Philosophy.

—been achieved, unless the winds, by the will of the Almighty, had moved impetuously one against the other in the middle region of the air. And this we have also confirmed out of Scripture, where it is said: *Ascendit fumus e naribus JEHOVÆ, carbones accensi sunt ab eo, inclinavit cælos, & descendit, & caligo sub pedibus ejus, & ascendit super Cherubin, & volavit & lapsus est super pennas venti. Posuit tenebras in circuitu suo latibulum, cribrans aquas de nubibus cælorum, præ fulgore in conspectu ejus nubes succense sunt, sonabat de cælo Dominus, &c.* <note>original Latin text from 2 Samuel 22:9-14: "Smoke ascended out of the nostrils of JEHOVAH, coals were kindled by him. He bowed the heavens and descended, and darkness was under his feet. And he rode upon a Cherub, and did fly; he was seen upon the wings of the wind. He made darkness pavilions round about him, dark waters, and thick clouds of the skies. Through the brightness before him were coals of fire kindled. The Lord thundered from heaven..."</note> *Smoke ascended out of the nostrils of JEHOVAH, coals are kindled by him. He inclined or bowed down the heavens and descended, and darkness was under his feet, and he ascended upon the Cherubim, and did fly, and glide upon the wings of the wind. He put the darkness round about him, to serve to hide him, sifting out waters from the clouds of heavens, before his face; for at his presence the clouds were set on fire, and the Lord did thunder from heaven, etc.* From this speech we gather that not only the clouds, thunder, and lightnings are moved by the wind-bearing ministers or angels of the Lord, but also that Divinity itself, being encompassed by dark clouds in the middle region of the air, is carried upon the airy Cherubim and uses the wings of the winds as instruments to move upon. 

By this, any wise man may easily perceive that worldly wisdom or Peripatetic <note>original: "Peripateticall Philosophy"; referring to the school of Aristotle, who taught while walking (peripatētikos)</note> Philosophy is plain foolishness. It attempts to fully persuade the world that such essential acts as the angelic winds (whose inward essence is the bright Spirit of the Lord) are caused accidentally and are moved and stirred up by external force. However, by the doctrine of true wisdom, it is evident that they are endowed with the most essential internal agents, and therefore they move where and when they please, according to that before-mentioned statement by St. John: For (he says) *Spiritus ubi vult: The Spirit <note>The Greek and Latin words for "Spirit" (Pneuma/Spiritus) also mean "Wind."</note> blows where it lists.* Since this is apparent, the wind has *actum, formam, & principium internum: An essential and inward act, form, and principle,* by whose motion it is moved or directed whichever way the inward mover pleases. Therefore, the Text says, *Spiritus ubi vult: It blows where it will,* and consequently it is endowed with a voluntary choice or will. 

Thus, every man may see how far from the truth is the Peripatetics' reasoning regarding this point. They admit no essential and internal form to the winds but make them a thing merely accidental. For example, they claim the stars, by their heat, stir or draw up a smoke <note>meaning vapors or exhalations</note> out of the earth; this smoke, soaring on high, is pushed down again by the coldness of that place, and then by other ascending fumes, it is forced to move sideways. I beseech you (who are wise and impartial) to teach me which of all these external accidents in the procreation of the winds can be esteemed as that internal or essential principle which can cause a voluntary motion in the winds, or can produce any angelic act in the air? For the Text says, *Spiritus ubi vult.* If there is no such essential, voluntary, internal, or central agent to be found or even imagined in Aristotle's fiction of "faint wind," then let the breath of those who teach Christians such falsehoods be esteemed as vain as his doctrine is deceptive <note>original: "prestigious"; here meaning full of tricks or illusions</note> in itself. 

Was not the unlikelihood of the Aristotelian assertion the reason that made some of the wisest of his own scientific <note>original: "Physicall"</note> disciples recoil and doubt—yea, and plainly turn their opinions away from this vain doctrine of their master concerning the winds? Among these was John Fregius <note>Johann Thomas Freig (1543–1583), a German scholar</note>, a man well-versed in the philosophy of Aristotle. After he had mentioned the causes of the meteors <note>original: "Meteors"; in this period, "meteor" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon like wind, rain, or snow</note>, he immediately departed from the mind of his master regarding the winds and broke forth into these terms: *Quanquam tota disputatio de ventis, sicut de aliis Meteoris plena sit admirabilium operum Dei, quorum nulla firma & sufficiens in natura causa proferri possunt, tamen prodest videre quousque humana ratio progredi possit. Sacra quidem literæ dicunt Deum ventos producere, de thesauris suis unde ipsius flatus audimus, sed unde veniant aut quo vadant nescimus.* <margin>2 Samuel 22:8.</margin> *Although the whole dispute concerning the winds, as also of the rest of the meteors, is full of the admirable works of God—for which no firm or sufficient cause can be produced in nature—yet it is beneficial and fit to look into this mystery as far as human reason is able to penetrate. The Holy Scripture does say that God produces the winds out of his treasury, whereupon we hear their blasts, but know not from where they come or where they go.* Thus far Fregius, in his 25th book, upon the cause of the winds.

But I will proceed a little further in this my inquiry. Aristotle and his Peripatetic disciples assert that the stormy and tempestuous wind called *Ecnephia* <note>original: "Ecnephia"; a Greek term for a storm-wind breaking out of a cloud</note>, as also the whirlwind, are certain sudden <note>original: "repentine"</note> winds which are forcibly expelled—
